iikGG5Se3J.one_liner: Dense multi-view matching from frozen foundation-model features plus GPU dense bundle adjustment on regular pixel grids anchored to source rays.
iikGG5Se3J.problem: Direct regression in deep 3D models discards sub-pixel geometric constraints, while classical optimization reaches sub-pixel precision but does not scale to dense correspondences and relies on heuristic discrete track building.
iikGG5Se3J.method: Extracts dense correspondences from latent features of a frozen multi-view backbone, reducing per-pair decoding to lightweight coarse matching and local convolutional refinement. It then runs dense bundle adjustment on a regular view graph over 2D pixel grids with tracks anchored to source rays, marginalizing millions of depth variables in parallel.
iikGG5Se3J.key_idea: Formulate bundle adjustment densely on regular 2D pixel grids with tracks anchored to source rays, so depth variables are marginalized in parallel without keypoint quantization or track merging.
iikGG5Se3J.evidence: Unordered (ETH3D, Texture-Poor) and sequential (TUM RGB-D, ETH3D-SLAM) benchmarks, with ablations and rolling-shutter camera modeling per reviews.
iikGG5Se3J.claimed_gains: Improves relative-pose AUC@1 degree to 88.6% on ETH3D; a review cites 78.4 for the next most accurate method, in 8.8 versus 189 seconds.
iikGG5Se3J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DMap delivers large accuracy gains at lower cost across unordered and sequential benchmarks, with the matching and dense optimization contributions separated by ablations.
iikGG5Se3J.main_concern: The efficiency claim is considered overstated (the pipeline is at least quadratic end to end and slower than DROID-SLAM on TUM RGB-D), and novelty lies mainly in integrating known components.

X4lPQWX5Ds.one_liner: Models RNN gradients as a linear cocycle over a Markov chain, proves nonzero fluctuation variance, and regularizes it.
X4lPQWX5Ds.problem: Regularizers that drive the top Lyapunov exponent to zero for marginal stability leave the non-autonomous gradient dynamics uncharacterized, so gradients can still explode or vanish over finite horizons.
X4lPQWX5Ds.method: They model gradient dynamics as a linear cocycle over an ergodic Markov chain and prove that the Lyapunov spectrum of RNN gradient dynamics is well-defined and input-independent, with a companion central limit theorem whose asymptotic variance sigma^2 is strictly positive. They then provide a regularizer for this residual diffusion.
X4lPQWX5Ds.key_idea: Penalize the asymptotic variance sigma^2 of log gradient norms, the CLT fluctuation term left after the top Lyapunov exponent is zeroed, in addition to the drift.
X4lPQWX5Ds.evidence: Proofs under stated assumptions (the CLT assumes i.i.d. inputs) plus experiments on psMNIST, the adding problem, and noise-padded CIFAR-10, including a sweep of the flossing coefficient alpha.
X4lPQWX5Ds.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the proof that fluctuations around the Lyapunov drift stay strictly positive, which explains why setting the top exponent to zero is not enough.
X4lPQWX5Ds.main_concern: The empirical gains from the variance regularizer are weak and confined to controlled benchmarks, the CLT assumes i.i.d. inputs, and the link to finite-window flossing and to feedforward Jacobian-spectrum literature is underdeveloped.

rO8xykiPQP.one_liner: Reframes heterogeneous treatment effect identification as Markov-blanket discovery over sparse-autoencoder features of pre-treatment representations
rO8xykiPQP.problem: Existing HTE methods trade expressivity for interpretability, and when heterogeneity drivers are unmeasured both ends of that spectrum can give spurious HTE characterizations with no causal reading.
rO8xykiPQP.method: The paper re-frames HTE identification as Markov-blanket discovery on a sufficient and aligned pre-treatment representation and introduces NEXIS, an iterative selection procedure with a provable selection guarantee. Reviewers describe it as forward selection over sparse-autoencoder dictionary coordinates of foundation-model embeddings.
rO8xykiPQP.key_idea: Select effect modifiers by forward Markov-blanket search for the treatment effect over sparse-autoencoder dictionary coordinates of multimodal pre-treatment embeddings.
rO8xykiPQP.evidence: A provable selection guarantee under stated assumptions, semi-synthetic experiments (including a CelebA setup), and deployment on two anti-poverty programs in Africa augmented with satellite imagery.
rO8xykiPQP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the principled distinction between causal effect modifiers and correlated proxies, the use of sparse-autoencoder dictionaries as a scalable hypothesis space, and the strong real-world applications.
rO8xykiPQP.main_concern: The guarantees depend on strong assumptions (measurement sufficiency, representation sufficiency, principal alignment, faithfulness) that may not hold for the satellite features, so selected features may be proxies rather than direct modifiers.

Ga5ICrf1fi.one_liner: Shows frontier models change confidence, suspicion and reasoning depending on the identity of the inferred user
Ga5ICrf1fi.problem: AI assistants often know who they are talking to, for example through an e-mail address in context, but it is unclear how this user awareness shifts model behavior.
Ga5ICrf1fi.method: The paper defines user awareness and compares model behavior when the inferred user is a specific recognized AI researcher or is affiliated with certain AI organizations against a general-population comparison, measuring self-reported confidence, suspicion of harmful requests, and amount of reasoning.
Ga5ICrf1fi.key_idea: Vary the user identity visible in context (recognized AI researchers, organizational affiliation) and measure shifts in model self-confidence, suspicion of harmful requests and reasoning effort.
Ga5ICrf1fi.evidence: Behavioral tests on frontier models including Claude Sonnet 5 (reviewers note only two Claude models), with controls and robustness checks; effects vary across models and individuals.
Ga5ICrf1fi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the user-awareness idea interesting and cleanly operationalized, with appropriate controls, varied outcome measures and robustness checks.
Ga5ICrf1fi.main_concern: The effects are small and often not statistically significant, only two Claude models are tested, and it is unclear whether the result reflects a deeper construct or a mechanical response to names.

og3q6q0PxP.one_liner: Inference-time guidance for flow models using minimum-norm Lyapunov feedback control on a predicted terminal sample's constraint violation.
og3q6q0PxP.problem: Enforcing test-time constraints on pretrained flow models currently relies on projection, posterior sampling or iterative optimization of the generative trajectory.
og3q6q0PxP.method: At each sampling step LyapuFlow predicts the terminal sample the flow is heading toward, evaluates constraint violation on it, and computes the minimum-norm control that satisfies a prescribed Lyapunov decrease condition. The control stays inactive when the flow already reduces violation at the prescribed rate and otherwise applies a correction inside a flow-relative trust region.
og3q6q0PxP.key_idea: Apply a Lyapunov decrease condition to the constraint violation of the predicted terminal sample and solve for the minimum-norm control, which is zero when the flow already decreases violation.
og3q6q0PxP.evidence: Data-space and latent-space experiments on physics-constrained generation (PDE dynamics) and image inverse problems such as super-resolution, against DPS, FlowDPS, PCFM and OC-Flow, with component ablations and runtime comparisons per reviews.
og3q6q0PxP.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims outperformance over alternative test-time constraint-enforcement mechanisms, with no numbers.
og3q6q0PxP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the control-theoretic formulation and the clear, practical feedback construction, and note gains over DPS, FlowDPS, PCFM and OC-Flow across PDE and image tasks.
og3q6q0PxP.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the Lyapunov mechanism: with stop-gradients the controller reduces to normalised gradient guidance, so gains may come from normalisation and clipping, and positioning against MPC-Flow is thin.

9a4dEL5xo8.one_liner: Training-free 8-bit quantization of linear-attention recurrent states via per-window quantization, high-precision outlier compensator tokens, and residual smoothing.
9a4dEL5xo8.problem: Quantizing the recurrent state of hybrid linear-attention LLMs such as Gated DeltaNet and Kimi Delta Attention degrades quality through accumulating rounding errors and outlier rows and columns.
9a4dEL5xo8.method: Per-window quantization quantizes the state only once at the end of a window while outputs use the fixed low-bit state plus high-precision buffered updates. The largest outliers are kept as high-precision compensator tokens sharing the update path of real tokens, and the residual is smoothed before quantization.
9a4dEL5xo8.key_idea: Quantize the state once per token window instead of at every step, hold outliers as high-precision compensator tokens, and smooth the residual to cut rounding error.
9a4dEL5xo8.evidence: Qwen, Kimi and GLM model families, with accuracy and systems performance across several GPU types and ablations of each component.
9a4dEL5xo8.claimed_gains: Near-lossless performance under 8-bit recurrent-state quantization; the abstract is cut off before further numbers.
9a4dEL5xo8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely, the two error sources are clearly identified, and the combination of per-window quantization, compensator tokens and smoothing is effective on accuracy and runtime.
9a4dEL5xo8.main_concern: Scope of evidence: only 8-bit state quantization is evaluated (no more aggressive precision or weight-activation quantization), and reported speedups depend on comparing against FP32 baselines.

UbWa5tcebQ.one_liner: AssemblyWorld is an interactive 3D environment and 100-task benchmark where general-purpose agents assemble rigid parts from rendered views.
UbWa5tcebQ.problem: It is unknown whether pretrained general-purpose agents can assemble 3D objects through visual interaction without assembly-specific fine-tuning.
UbWa5tcebQ.method: Agents inspect rendered views and manipulate supplied rigid parts, guided by images or assembly manuals, without direct access to mesh vertices or faces, and assemblies are scored geometrically. AssemblyWorldBench has 100 tasks across 80 objects spanning furniture, industrial assembly, and fracture reassembly.
UbWa5tcebQ.key_idea: Agents perceive part geometry only through 2D views and manipulate parts numerically, with final assemblies scored geometrically.
UbWa5tcebQ.evidence: Eight agent systems evaluated on AssemblyWorldBench, with analyses of visual references, interaction trajectories, and failures, and comparisons against specialized methods.
UbWa5tcebQ.claimed_gains: The strongest system achieves 80.9% part accuracy but 59.4% complete-assembly success.
UbWa5tcebQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a timely, well-designed interactive benchmark spanning furniture, industrial, and fracture domains, with extensive experiments and informative analyses.
UbWa5tcebQ.main_concern: Comparisons with specialized methods are not run under a matched protocol, and the 80-object evaluation set leaves unclear whether system differences are robust to object selection.

WIuBd6xzdW.one_liner: Corrects deterministic forecasts using a predicted ordered categorical distribution over value bins, with a peak-precursor memory, for high-value regions.
WIuBd6xzdW.problem: Time-series forecasters are accurate on average but unreliable in rare high-value regions, because they lack explicit mechanisms for modeling historical patterns that precede high-value outcomes.
WIuBd6xzdW.method: PeakTS predicts an ordered categorical distribution over future value bins and uses its mean and upper quantiles to correct deterministic forecasts. A Risk-Conditioned Peak Memory stores general and peak-precursor prototypes and retrieves patterns from time-, difference-, and frequency-domain views, and a tail-aware ordinal objective applies frequency-based threshold reweighting and upper-tail weighting.
WIuBd6xzdW.key_idea: Use risk statistics of a predicted ordinal value-bin distribution, modulated by retrieved peak-precursor prototypes, to adaptively correct point forecasts toward high values.
WIuBd6xzdW.evidence: Multiple forecasting benchmarks (nine datasets per reviews) with ablations and evaluation on the top 75%, 50%, and 25% high-value regions.
WIuBd6xzdW.claimed_gains: Consistent improvements in high-value forecasting while keeping competitive overall performance; no figures stated in the abstract.
WIuBd6xzdW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the focus on rare high-value regions well motivated and practically relevant, with comprehensive experiments on nine datasets and ablations supporting the components.
WIuBd6xzdW.main_concern: Baseline comparisons do not isolate the contribution (undocumented baseline losses and tuning, unauditable ordinal-baseline numbers), and evaluation omits more extreme regions such as the top 10% or 5%.

j2MT0hGQPt.one_liner: Fine-tunes MoE models so each sequence prefers few experts, which are cached on GPU to cut CPU-GPU transfer.
j2MT0hGQPt.problem: MoE models need all parameters in GPU memory, and expert-offloading methods suffer I/O latency from transferring experts between CPU and GPU.
j2MT0hGQPt.method: MELINOE fine-tunes an MoE model to prefer a smaller number of experts per sequence so those experts can be cached in GPU memory, reducing expert churn. Per reviews, it tunes router weights, gate projection, and LoRA experts using cache-simulation and rank-matching losses.
j2MT0hGQPt.key_idea: Add cache-simulation and rank-matching losses during fine-tuning to concentrate each sequence's routing on a small, cacheable expert set.
j2MT0hGQPt.evidence: Throughput comparisons against offloading baselines on three MoE architectures and several GPUs, plus downstream task accuracy (for example GSM8K).
j2MT0hGQPt.claimed_gains: Throughput up 1.2-3x over efficient baselines and up to 14.7x over transfer-heavy baselines while retaining or improving downstream performance.
j2MT0hGQPt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practical for on-device MoE deployment, the cache-simulation and rank-matching losses well motivated, and the throughput gains substantial and consistent across architectures and hardware.
j2MT0hGQPt.main_concern: Accuracy comparisons are unfair because MELINOE is fine-tuned on the task while baselines are not, and the method is tied to per-task checkpoints and a specific cache configuration.

dPh6tE8IQm.one_liner: Autoregressive continuous thoughts sampled from a conditional diffusion head on a causal transformer instead of regressed with mean squared error.
dPh6tE8IQm.problem: Continuous-thought reasoning methods predict thoughts with MSE, yielding a unimodal Gaussian model that averages multiple valid strategies and mode-collapses.
dPh6tE8IQm.method: Autoregressive Continuous Thought uses a causal transformer for reasoning context and a conditional diffusion head to sample the next continuous thought from a multimodal distribution, preserving the autoregressive structure; reviews describe an RL objective with latent and text terms.
dPh6tE8IQm.key_idea: Model each next continuous thought as a sampled conditional distribution via a diffusion head, rather than a deterministic MSE regression, to avoid averaging over strategies.
dPh6tE8IQm.evidence: Mathematical reasoning, planning and algorithmic tasks, with a matched MSE baseline, Pass@100 coverage and greedy answer-decoding checks per reviews.
dPh6tE8IQm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multimodality problem is well motivated and the lightweight diffusion head preserves the backbone, with Pass@100 gains supporting latent sampling.
dPh6tE8IQm.main_concern: The benefit of the learned flow generator is not isolated from simple stochasticity and from RL, comparisons with related latent-reasoning RL methods are missing, and majority-vote results are mixed.

mgQ5gW3E0W.one_liner: Generator of temporal-KG questions certified, by symbolic axis-dropping checks, to require structural, temporal and geographical reasoning jointly.
mgQ5gW3E0W.problem: Existing TKGQA benchmarks test only structural and temporal reasoning even though event graphs carry latent geography.
mgQ5gW3E0W.method: They ground locative anchors to a shared geographical knowledge layer, design twelve schema families composing structural, temporal and spatial operators, execute logical forms symbolically, and keep a question only if dropping any one axis's constraints changes the gold answer, with no human annotation or LLMs.
mgQ5gW3E0W.key_idea: Certify each question by symbolic execution: keep it only if removing the constraints of any one of the three axes changes its gold answer.
mgQ5gW3E0W.evidence: Four standard event graphs, 67,565 questions with difficulty bands and four generalization splits, and ten baselines from four paradigms over 160 runs with generator-backed error attribution.
mgQ5gW3E0W.claimed_gains: The pipeline yields 67,565 questions; the strongest of ten baselines wins ten of sixteen cells but resolves only 0.4116 of mean-pooled questions, and 19.94% of questions defeat all ten methods.
mgQ5gW3E0W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the tri-axial certification is well designed and the evaluation of ten baselines with closed-book and unanswerable controls is comprehensive.
mgQ5gW3E0W.main_concern: The conclusion that decomposition hurts is not robust to the scoring protocol (RTQA and RALM rankings flip under unified strict scoring), and certification does not prove models actually use all three axes.

ntDX6zio1N.one_liner: Hierarchical data selection that evaluates representative leaf regions and infers other regions' utility with empirical Bayes posteriors.
ntDX6zio1N.problem: Train-free data selectors rely on proxies that may not match the target objective, while train-based selectors need many costly train-evaluate iterations.
ntDX6zio1N.method: HARP organizes the training pool into a node-leaf hierarchy, evaluates only representative leaves, infers unmeasured utilities with empirical Bayes posteriors, and selects with HARP-C (conservative redundancy control) or HARP-E (additive reward for complementary regions).
ntDX6zio1N.key_idea: Estimate the downstream utility of unmeasured data regions from a few measured representative leaves via empirical Bayes, then select under redundancy-aware envelopes.
ntDX6zio1N.evidence: 3 base models, 3 finetuning datasets, 8 baselines and 4 reasoning benchmarks, with theory bounding selection error under local smoothness and bounded estimation error.
ntDX6zio1N.claimed_gains: HARP variants outperform the strongest baseline by up to +4.9 points on average, and HARP-C trains on roughly 9x fewer examples.
ntDX6zio1N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree HARP addresses a practical data-selection problem with comprehensive experiments, an intuitive design and a much smaller final training set.
ntDX6zio1N.main_concern: End-to-end cost savings are not demonstrated because leaf-level train-evaluate runs add selection cost, and Random, a strong baseline, is excluded from the ranking.

n5Cz9BxMXc.one_liner: Online fine-tuning of a pretrained actor-critic from preferences, using a critic gauge for reward scale and active, abstention-aware query selection.
n5Cz9BxMXc.problem: With a pretrained checkpoint but no offline data or reward function, a preference-learned reward is identified only up to scale and offset, which corrupts the critic's values, and preference queries are costly and may be abstained.
n5Cz9BxMXc.method: A critic gauge recovers the reward implied by the frozen critic and regresses the learned reward onto it to fix scale and offset; queries are scored by expected posterior-variance reduction under a Gaussian posterior over reward parameters, weighted by an online estimate of the labeler's chance of answering.
n5Cz9BxMXc.key_idea: Pin the preference-learned reward's scale and offset to the reward implied by the frozen pretrained critic, and choose queries by expected variance reduction weighted by answer likelihood.
n5Cz9BxMXc.evidence: Online fine-tuning with preference feedback compared with WSRL (which has the true reward) and PEBBLE, with ablations and approximate-submodularity guarantees for greedy selection.
n5Cz9BxMXc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the offline-to-online setting without data or reward access is practical and underexplored, and the method is sound with reasonable ablations.
n5Cz9BxMXc.main_concern: The critic gauge assumes the frozen offline critic is approximately Bellman-consistent with the true reward, which may fail under critic error and distribution shift, and the active-selection contribution overlaps prior work.

XND4c4fKFW.one_liner: Empirical study of what makes a good initialization for on-policy self-distillation, plus a divergence-aware SFT warm-up upweighting low-divergence tokens.
XND4c4fKFW.problem: OPSD supervision degrades when the student drifts far from the teacher, making it sensitive to student checkpoint and teacher configuration, while prior work assumes stronger students or privileged teachers always help.
XND4c4fKFW.method: Hundreds of experiments across model scales, SFT checkpoints and privileged-teacher settings relate OPSD gains to teacher accuracy on student-failed problems and token-level teacher-student divergence; they then propose a divergence-aware SFT warm-up that upweights low-divergence tokens.
XND4c4fKFW.key_idea: Upweight low teacher-student-divergence tokens during SFT warm-up so initialization targets are easy to learn and the teacher complements the student.
XND4c4fKFW.evidence: Hundreds of experiments over model scales (Qwen3 1.7B, 4B and 8B per reviews), SFT lengths and teacher conditions, evaluated on math benchmarks including AIME24 and AIME25.
XND4c4fKFW.claimed_gains: The divergence-aware warm-up gains +11.67 over initialization on AIME24 versus +5.00 for standard SFT+OPSD, and +11.25 on AIME25.
XND4c4fKFW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is systematic and well controlled, with an actionable finding that a stronger SFT checkpoint or more accurate teacher does not guarantee better OPSD.
XND4c4fKFW.main_concern: Scope is narrow (Qwen3, math, non-thinking mode) and gains are measured from a lower starting point, and one reviewer found internally inconsistent correlation values in the tables.

pfRc4xNq1u.one_liner: End-to-end trainable sparse attention memory with learned document selection, compressed KV cache and document-wise RoPE for 100M-token context.
pfRc4xNq1u.problem: Full attention limits LLMs to roughly 1M tokens, and linear attention, fixed-size memory or external storage lose accuracy, add latency, or lack end-to-end optimization.
pfRc4xNq1u.method: MSA uses scalable sparse attention with document-wise RoPE for linear complexity, KV cache compression with Memory Parallel for 100M-token inference on 2xA800 GPUs, and a Memory Interleave mechanism for multi-hop reasoning across scattered memory segments.
pfRc4xNq1u.key_idea: Encode documents independently, retrieve only relevant compressed KV memory through learned sparse attention, and interleave retrieval with generation for multi-hop reasoning.
pfRc4xNq1u.evidence: Long-context QA benchmarks compared with frontier LLMs, RAG systems and memory agents, with scaling from 16K to 100M tokens, ablations and efficiency measurements.
pfRc4xNq1u.claimed_gains: Less than 9% degradation when scaling from 16K to 100M tokens, with 100M-token inference on 2xA800 GPUs.
pfRc4xNq1u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree MSA combines learned retrieval, compressed memory and sparse attention into a workable route to very large memory banks, with strong QA results and ablations.
pfRc4xNq1u.main_concern: The 100M-token claim mostly reflects addressable memory-bank size within document-centric QA rather than general long-context modeling, and choices like document-wise RoPE are not independently validated.

iQG0FJJ0uk.one_liner: Four successive evaluations test LLMs on time: knowledge of temporal rules, duration prediction, human-task duration judgments, and time-cost decisions.
iQG0FJJ0uk.problem: LLMs encounter time only through descriptions, and it is unclear whether this hinders reasoning and decisions that involve time.
iQG0FJJ0uk.method: The paper traces time competence from knowledge to action through four evaluations: questions built from theorems of time-related literatures, self-completion-time estimates, durations of human tasks with wording effects, and decisions about tool use under wait times.
iQG0FJJ0uk.key_idea: Evaluate temporal competence along a ladder from knowing the rules of time to predicting durations to acting on time costs, using axioms and theorems from psychology and economics.
iQG0FJJ0uk.evidence: Four evaluations of LLMs; per reviews, the self-duration experiment uses 16 METR tasks and the tool-use experiment tests sensitivity to wait times.
iQG0FJJ0uk.claimed_gains: Findings rather than gains: models score 91.9-95.8% on time-theorem questions but underestimate their own completion times by up to 99.5%, magnify human biases by 1.3x, and ignore a 1,200-fold increase in wait time.
iQG0FJJ0uk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question timely and the four-level evaluation rigorous and well organized, with interdisciplinary grounding and relevance to agents that schedule work.
iQG0FJJ0uk.main_concern: Without a stated value of time to users there is no optimal-choice benchmark (ignoring a 1,200-fold wait may be rational), and the duration experiment uses only 16 METR tasks, mostly coding and research.

1xjSetmIGX.one_liner: Trains a textual memory writer against a frozen reader, crediting each rewrite by its marginal gain over the preceding memory
1xjSetmIGX.problem: Learning what to remember is a credit-assignment problem: a memory rewrite may pay off many steps later, and much of the observed utility is inherited from information already stored.
1xjSetmIGX.method: Memory Gain Policy Optimization (MGPO) credits each rewrite for its marginal contribution to current and future downstream utility, comparing pre- and post-rewrite memories under the same reader and target. It is studied on document-level information extraction, where structured supervision makes the effect of each memory update measurable.
1xjSetmIGX.key_idea: Compare downstream utility of the memory after a rewrite with that of the memory before it, isolating the rewrite's incremental value from inherited utility.
1xjSetmIGX.evidence: Document-level information extraction (SciREX per reviewers) with a Qwen3-8B memory writer, transfer across domains and downstream readers without further training, and a gradient-variance analysis.
1xjSetmIGX.claimed_gains: MGPO improves extraction while reducing average memory length by nearly 80% relative to the initial memory policy before optimization.
1xjSetmIGX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the counterfactual formulation separating inherited utility from a rewrite's contribution is intuitive and well motivated, and that the performance-memory trade-off is compelling.
1xjSetmIGX.main_concern: Reviewers say the advantage of the pre-rewrite baseline over other baselines and the variance-reduction explanation are not established at trained checkpoints, and training uses only a Qwen3-8B writer with limited retention validation.

6hKhOvyIo8.one_liner: GRPO attacker reward adding strategy-level and realization-level diversity terms, applied only to attacks above an effectiveness threshold
6hKhOvyIo8.problem: Reinforcement learning with attack success as the only reward collapses jailbreak attackers onto a narrow set of prompts, biasing safety evaluation toward near-duplicate attacks, and existing diversity methods trade off success or inference cost.
6hKhOvyIo8.method: CoFiBreak adds to GRPO a coarse reward encouraging strategies underrepresented within each group and a fine reward discouraging reuse of personas, framings, and output formats after harmful-intent information is removed from prompt embeddings. Diversity rewards apply only to attacks above an effectiveness threshold and are computed only during training.
6hKhOvyIo8.key_idea: Reward strategy-level rarity within a GRPO group plus intent-removed embedding dissimilarity of how strategies are realized, gated on attack effectiveness so diversity cannot come from failed attacks.
6hKhOvyIo8.evidence: Multi-turn jailbreak training with Llama3.1-8B-Instruct as the victim, transfer to other victims including Claude-Opus-4.6, and ablations of reward components.
6hKhOvyIo8.claimed_gains: The TLDR states 2 times more diversity score while maintaining high attack success; the abstract reports 1.6 to 2.0 times as many distinct items, with the sentence cut off in the batch.
6hKhOvyIo8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coarse-to-fine reward is clear and intuitive, handles two kinds of diversity collapse without trading off attack success, and is supported by experiments, ablations, and transfer to other victim models.
6hKhOvyIo8.main_concern: Reviewers say all main numbers come from a single GRPO seed, the benefit of diverse attacks for safety training is untested, and the complex reward is not clearly necessary since removing a component raised attack success.

2OlT5tjxRq.one_liner: Evolves an agent harness by mining papers into topic-clustered improvement strategies per module, then implementing and combining them
2OlT5tjxRq.problem: Harness evolution by a meta coding agent relies on the agent's existing knowledge and observed failures, which restricts exploration and makes adaptation reactive.
2OlT5tjxRq.method: ScholarEvolve organizes harness evolution directions into functional modules, uses topic modeling over research papers to identify distinct improvement strategies for each module, implements those strategies, and evaluates their combinations. It is designed to incorporate new publications over time.
2OlT5tjxRq.key_idea: Retrieved papers are clustered by topic modeling into distinct strategies per harness module, then implemented and recombined by evolutionary search to drive proactive harness improvement.
2OlT5tjxRq.evidence: AppWorld and τ²-Bench experiments with evolution, validation, and test data separated, including held-out Amazon and Gmail tasks, compared against Meta Harness with cumulative ablations.
2OlT5tjxRq.claimed_gains: Raises Qwen3.5-27B task goal completion from 49.6% to 63.6% on AppWorld Challenge and GPT-5.4-mini pass¹ from 72.7% to 81.9% on τ²-Bench Telecom.
2OlT5tjxRq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning from research literature is an intuitive, promising alternative to feedback-only harness evolution, and that held-out gains on AppWorld and τ²-Bench are substantial.
2OlT5tjxRq.main_concern: Reviewers say the ablations do not isolate the contribution of external papers or fresh literature, retrieval may surface benchmark-specific methods, and the optimization cost is unclear.

ljJmMrSuQr.one_liner: Selects instruction-tuning data whose gradients are jointly compatible, using flow probing, cone-compatible subsets, and smooth minibatch scheduling.
ljJmMrSuQr.problem: Data selection methods rank examples independently by quality, diversity, difficulty, or influence, although individually valuable examples can have conflicting gradients when optimized together in minibatches.
ljJmMrSuQr.method: CoFlow operationalizes gradient-flow compatibility through compact flow probing, cone-compatible subset construction, and smooth minibatch scheduling, so selected examples are both individually useful and jointly compatible in gradient space.
ljJmMrSuQr.key_idea: Pick subsets whose per-example gradients fall within a compatible cone and schedule them smoothly across minibatches, instead of ranking examples independently.
ljJmMrSuQr.evidence: Experiments on NuminaMath, AlpacaEval, HumanEval, and MultiPL-E; reviews cite 4 datasets, 13 baselines, ablations, and a control varying only gradient coherence among subsets from the same influence-score band.
ljJmMrSuQr.claimed_gains: CoFlow improves average downstream performance by 10.6% over strong selection baselines and reduces gradient conflict by 34.8%; the abstract is cut off after saying it reaches full-data-level.
ljJmMrSuQr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the gradient-compatibility motivation clear and well supported, with a controlled experiment showing coherence matters beyond individual scores, plus many datasets, baselines, and ablations.
ljJmMrSuQr.main_concern: Gradient conflict, the diagnostic behind the 34.8% claim, is never formally defined, and the main table compares the method at a 4.1% budget against baselines at 10%.

6k0c5tCz7Y.one_liner: Input-dependent low-rank controller compiled from output-sensitive corrective actions that edit hidden states of a frozen medical VLM.
6k0c5tCz7Y.problem: Correcting a frozen model's medical errors with a shared representation edit can help some inputs but harm others, disrupting predictions that were already correct.
6k0c5tCz7Y.method: A budget-weighted Jacobian identifies an output-sensitive subspace in which source labels define bounded corrective actions; these are compiled into an input-dependent low-rank controller via reduced-rank regression, then refined through the frozen backbone to improve predictions while preserving source margins. At inference the controller uses only the current hidden state.
6k0c5tCz7Y.key_idea: Compile label-defined corrective actions in a Jacobian-identified output-sensitive subspace into an input-dependent low-rank map, rather than applying one shared steering direction.
6k0c5tCz7Y.evidence: 2,100 retrospective radiologic questions with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B, with controls under matched source supervision, response subspace, and refinement budget, plus a text-model check and seven InternVL environments.
6k0c5tCz7Y.claimed_gains: Reaches 80.95% and 81.62% accuracy with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B, exceeding source-calibrated Native baselines by 11.95 and 11.24 percentage points (12.19 and 42.67 over the unmodified Native), and a learned shared direction by 13.31 and 28.45 points.
6k0c5tCz7Y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating sensitive-direction identification, corrective-target construction, and target prediction is well motivated, with informative controls and repair-versus-damage accounting.
6k0c5tCz7Y.main_concern: There is no aggregate comparison to a simple classifier or linear probe trained on the same frozen hidden states, so the benefit of intervening inside the model is unclear.

tw9P0Tb84O.one_liner: Scores a training example by the gradient energy it delivers to dominant, unsaturated directions of the model's learning spectrum.
tw9P0Tb84O.problem: LLM data curation relies on surface proxies such as token counts, text-space diversity, or post hoc benchmark deltas that describe the data rather than what it teaches the model.
tw9P0Tb84O.method: Spectral Data Valuation scores each example by projecting its gradient onto spectral directions weighted by eigenvalue and discounted by a per-direction saturation score that grows with accumulated gradient energy, turning data curation into maximizing information gain per token. The full pipeline also includes synthetic data.
tw9P0Tb84O.key_idea: Score examples by squared gradient projections onto spectral directions, weighted by eigenvalue and discounted by accumulated energy (saturation), so value updates as the model learns.
tw9P0Tb84O.evidence: Experiments across model families and scales, including subspace alignment among influence, weight rotation, and feature coverage, selection baselines under matched token budgets, and a no-synthesis ablation.
tw9P0Tb84O.claimed_gains: Subspaces recovered from influence, weight rotation, and feature coverage align with a mean principal overlap of 0.86 against a random baseline of 0.12; the remaining claimed gains are truncated in the abstract.
tw9P0Tb84O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that making data value depend on the current model state with diminishing returns is well motivated, the paper is clearly written, and the broad experiments show substantial gains over selection baselines.
tw9P0Tb84O.main_concern: Comparison protocols are unclear (refresh frequencies, unique versus consumed tokens, selection-only versus selection-plus-synthesis), and accumulated squared-gradient energy may not reliably measure what has been learned.

yZntGgtQth.one_liner: Defines good symbols for hybrid planning as solver-sufficient, and invents them by counterexample-guided search or from neural energy landscapes.
yZntGgtQth.problem: Planning methods use human-defined or language-derived symbols without asking what makes a symbol computationally useful for solving the planning problem.
yZntGgtQth.method: For finite-horizon piecewise-affine systems, solver sufficiency is characterized exactly and a counterexample-guided algorithm invents symbols; the principle is extended to neural-network energy functions through their optimization landscapes.
yZntGgtQth.key_idea: Judge a symbol by whether fixing its discrete commitments simplifies the remaining solve, and induce such symbols from piecewise-affine structure or continuous optimization landscapes.
yZntGgtQth.evidence: Simulated and real-robot tasks; theory for piecewise-affine systems, with the neural case checked on sampled descents per reviews.
yZntGgtQth.claimed_gains: Invented symbols reduce solving cost while preserving solution quality, and improve interpretability and steerability; no numbers stated.
yZntGgtQth.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is well posed and the solver-oriented definition is principled, with efficiency gains across problem types.
yZntGgtQth.main_concern: Gains are not isolated from simpler mode partitioning, and reported speedups exclude the cost of symbol discovery.

Gt3ZzbKnkd.one_liner: Measures plasticity and stability of transformer modules on declarative and procedural tasks, finding stability does not mirror plasticity.
Gt3ZzbKnkd.problem: Plasticity and stability are usually studied at whole-model level and task-agnostically, with divergent conclusions across settings.
Gt3ZzbKnkd.method: A controlled synthetic environment tests which modules (QK, VO, MLP) learn each task type and how much they disrupt stored memory, with module reset-and-recovery experiments and a realistic-model check.
Gt3ZzbKnkd.key_idea: Compare modules by training each alone on procedural or declarative tasks, showing plasticity follows a module's primary role while stability depends on all dependencies on that module.
Gt3ZzbKnkd.evidence: Synthetic experiments on a 25M-parameter transformer across three seeds, plus a realistic setting with Qwen2.5-0.5B per reviews.
Gt3ZzbKnkd.claimed_gains: When learning a new procedure, updating QK retains over half of stored declarative memory, updating MLPs retains far less, and updating VO loses roughly four-fifths.
Gt3ZzbKnkd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the synthetic setup is clean and well controlled, with parameter-matched baselines, and that the QK versus VO contrast is convincing.
Gt3ZzbKnkd.main_concern: The paper does not pin down why VO updates erase far more memory than QK updates, and the core insight overlaps prior work.

e7DIU2hXBJ.one_liner: Learns discrete buyer types with a behavior-aware VQ-VAE and feeds them to LLM web agents as persona tokens.
e7DIU2hXBJ.problem: LLM web agents collapse to one average buyer policy, and hand-crafted prompt personas are brittle and cannot represent population-level behavior.
e7DIU2hXBJ.method: A behavior-aware VQ-VAE induces a discrete buyer-type space from raw clickstreams, each type maps to a persona token, and the agent is fine-tuned with these tokens on real browsing traces. At inference each synthetic buyer gets a token via one encoder pass, and populations sample types from each merchant's empirical codebook distribution.
e7DIU2hXBJ.key_idea: Quantize clickstream behavior into a discrete codebook of buyer types, each exposed as one learned persona token, and sample tokens from per-merchant empirical type distributions.
e7DIU2hXBJ.evidence: Evaluated on 8.37M buyers across 42 held-out live storefronts.
e7DIU2hXBJ.claimed_gains: 78% conversion-rate alignment with real buyers, and outperforms larger-parameter baselines on goal-oriented shopping (abstract cut off).
e7DIU2hXBJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical and under-explored, and value evaluation on held-out live production storefronts.
e7DIU2hXBJ.main_concern: The persona token's contribution is not isolated, since evaluation also supplies funnel-derived intent and the VQ-VAE inputs overlap with signals used to judge conversion fidelity.

wkLF5A2bY5.one_liner: RSI-Index is an external benchmark scoring LLM agents on four autonomous AI-research tasks against the best known results.
wkLF5A2bY5.problem: Autonomous AI research ability, a prerequisite for recursive self-improvement, is measured mainly by model developers on their own models and internal tasks.
wkLF5A2bY5.method: The authors introduce four tasks covering pre-training, post-training and harness engineering, each scored against the best known result. They evaluate 19 models from eight providers and track scores across model releases.
wkLF5A2bY5.key_idea: Score an agent's research output on pre-training, post-training and harness-engineering tasks relative to the best known result, then extrapolate the trend across model releases.
wkLF5A2bY5.evidence: Evaluation of 19 models from eight providers on four tasks; reviews mention behavioral analysis such as sequential post-training and premature termination.
wkLF5A2bY5.claimed_gains: The strongest model, Claude Opus 5.5, scores 0.373; performance rose steadily across releases, with gains mainly from combining established techniques.
wkLF5A2bY5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is important and timely and that the analysis of agent behavior across many models is detailed and insightful.
wkLF5A2bY5.main_concern: The link to recursive self-improvement is weak, so extrapolating four-task scores to frontier-level improvement within a year is not well justified.

91J8Mxqudq.one_liner: ProCraft is a 0.5B codec language model editing 30-second music mixes from free-form, compound instructions across seven operations.
91J8Mxqudq.problem: Existing text-guided music editors support few operations or instruments, work on short clips, or handle one operation per instruction, unlike real workflows with several simultaneous changes.
91J8Mxqudq.method: ProCraft is an autoregressive codec language model that aligns intermediate representations with pretrained music embeddings and pitch and instrument targets, and uses gated cross-attention in every decoder layer. On-the-fly Editing-pair Synthesis generates paired instructions and audio that combine track-level operations with effect changes for compound training.
91J8Mxqudq.key_idea: Pair representation alignment to music embeddings and pitch and instrument targets with per-layer gated cross-attention to the instruction, trained on compound edits synthesized on the fly.
91J8Mxqudq.evidence: Single-task comparison with task-specific systems, compound-instruction comparison with four free-text editors on MoisesDB and Slakh, and a listening study with 16 listeners.
91J8Mxqudq.claimed_gains: Competitive with task-specific systems on single-task editing and better than four free-text editors on compound instructions for track removal, extraction and denoising; no numbers in the abstract excerpt.
91J8Mxqudq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the compound free-form editing task is practical, the on-the-fly pair synthesis is a clean solution to missing training data, and the evaluation including the listening study is thorough.
91J8Mxqudq.main_concern: The only ablation removes gated cross-attention and alignment losses together, so gains cannot be attributed to either mechanism, and the components reuse existing ideas (BLIP-2, Flamingo, REPA).

cVUStYNEDI.one_liner: Builds a per-query agent harness via MCTS guided by a learned policy and utility predictor, without executing candidates.
cVUStYNEDI.problem: The best agent harness (roles, instructions, tools, communication structure) depends on the query, but its value is observable only by execution, so per-query tailoring needed costly inference-time execution or manual design.
cVUStYNEDI.method: SHIFT trains a local LLM architect with a policy over harness-building actions learned from search and a value function that predicts, from measured executions, a utility balancing accuracy against execution cost. For each query, Monte Carlo tree search uses these predictions to construct a harness, and only the selected harness is executed.
cVUStYNEDI.key_idea: Predict harness utility with a learned value function so tree search can build roles, instructions, and tools per query without executing alternatives at inference time.
cVUStYNEDI.evidence: 9,193 tasks across six benchmarks (math, document, and general-assistant) with a Gemini 3.5 Flash executor, compared with 17 baselines spanning prompting, prompt optimization, and workflow search, plus action-space ablations.
cVUStYNEDI.claimed_gains: SHIFT reaches about 80% mean accuracy, 7.2 percentage points above the strongest of 17 baselines, a cheaper mode uses 32% fewer execution tokens than the strongest baseline, and joint choice beats instruction-only or tool-only by up to 9.1 points.
cVUStYNEDI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical, moving execution out of the search loop is a sound idea, and the policy, value, and search combination gives strong empirical results.
cVUStYNEDI.main_concern: Reviewers say MCTS's contribution is not isolated (greedy construction reaches 79.8% versus 79.9%), and gains are concentrated in small benchmarks (OfficeQA and GAIA with 41 and 51 test questions) with unweighted benchmark averaging.

Wfe6Wrh6xw.one_liner: Down-weights view-level 2D rewards whose cross-view ranking disagrees with RGB edge-based structural evidence when aligning 3D diffusion models.
Wfe6Wrh6xw.problem: Optimizing generic 2D reward scores over rendered views can erode the structural prior of a pretrained 3D diffusion model, and existing safeguards need structure-aware models or depth and normal estimators.
Wfe6Wrh6xw.method: GRPQ uses the degree of mismatch between 2D-reward cross-view rankings and structural evidence to estimate the reliability of each view-level reward and assigns optimization weights accordingly, suppressing harmful signals without extra structural supervision.
Wfe6Wrh6xw.key_idea: Weight each rendered view's reward by the agreement between its reward ranking and a structural-evidence ranking, with weights computed without gradient and normalized to unit mean.
Wfe6Wrh6xw.evidence: Three alignment methods, multiple 3D diffusion models and diverse reward models; the abstract is truncated before results.
Wfe6Wrh6xw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the intervention is simple, addresses a relevant failure mode of rendered-view reward optimization, and avoids auxiliary geometry estimators while fitting several alignment objectives.
Wfe6Wrh6xw.main_concern: Reviewers say the key reliability assumption is not validated: edge density depends on texture and contrast, and no comparison with shuffled ranks or simple view weighting shows that rank disagreement predicts harmful updates.

qVhrkzlscY.one_liner: Predicts a per-request MoE expert pruning mask from an agent's system and task prompts using a lightweight predictor.
qVhrkzlscY.problem: Static expert pruning applies one offline-calibrated mask to every request, which fails when multi-agent systems on one MoE backbone recruit different experts for different tasks and roles.
qVhrkzlscY.method: A lightweight predictor trained on workflow transcripts maps an agent's system and task prompts to a specialized per-request expert mask in a single forward pass, with no per-configuration calibration.
qVhrkzlscY.key_idea: Predict the needed expert subset directly from the agent's system and task prompt text, turning pruning from one-off calibration into per-request prediction.
qVhrkzlscY.evidence: Tested across diverse tasks and roles, model scales and MoE architectures against static pruning and merging baselines, with generalization to unseen workflows, workflow families, benchmarks and domains.
qVhrkzlscY.claimed_gains: The abstract claims better overall accuracy than static pruning and merging baselines, with the numeric margin cut off; a review cites a 63.4 mean score at 25% of experts retained versus 1.2 to 6.7 for static baselines.
qVhrkzlscY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the workload-heterogeneity problem in multi-agent systems is well motivated and that DEP outperforms static baselines, especially at aggressive pruning rates.
qVhrkzlscY.main_concern: Missing dynamic-pruning baselines (EASY-EP, IFPruning) and limited originality over prompt-conditioned pruning, with unaddressed batching and serving efficiency when requests need different expert masks.

fziKPqt90H.one_liner: HiCTE selects which latent dimensions each target expert receives, using variance-derived reliability and per-sample iterative refinement of a global estimator.
fziKPqt90H.problem: Expert-based incomplete multimodal methods transfer entire observed representations to every target expert, ignoring latent-dimension-level transferability differences and sample-specific transfer needs.
fziKPqt90H.method: Each observed modality is modeled in a probabilistic latent space with reliability derived from latent variance. A global estimator gives initial per-target transferability, refined per sample by local iterative optimization during training with gradients propagated to the estimator, and cross-expert and residual representations are combined with the self representation by adaptive weighting.
fziKPqt90H.key_idea: Estimate dimension-wise, target-specific transferability from latent variance with a global estimator refined per sample, so each target expert only receives selected source dimensions.
fziKPqt90H.evidence: Experiments on three multimodal benchmarks (MOSI, MOSEI and IEMOCAP per reviews) under different missing protocols, with whole-transfer and shared-selector controls and latent variance tracked against missing rate.
fziKPqt90H.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (a review cites gains of 1.32, 0.51 and 1.10 percentage points over Whole Transfer on MOSI, MOSEI and IEMOCAP).
fziKPqt90H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling cross-expert transferability at the dimension level is well motivated and that results are competitive across benchmarks and missing conditions, with informative ablations.
fziKPqt90H.main_concern: Incremental contribution that combines known pieces, with latent variance as reliability insufficiently justified and recent baselines such as CorrKD, MPLMM and DecAlign missing from comparisons.

Lfk4uVj5gv.one_liner: Casts Muon variants as chained linear minimization oracles and proposes TensorChain, which normalizes stacked cross-layer weight tensors along axes.
Lfk4uVj5gv.problem: Muon-style optimizers that compose several matrix normalizations are fragmented without a unified view, and many chains fall outside the standard LMO framework and can diverge on smooth convex objectives.
Lfk4uVj5gv.method: Defines chained LMOs as compositions of LMOs, analyzes convergence limits and a linear associative memory setting where chaining beats Muon under anisotropic embeddings. TensorChain stacks compatible weight matrices across layers and normalizes the resulting 3D tensor across its axes.
Lfk4uVj5gv.key_idea: Compose several LMO-based normalizations, including a layer-axis normalization over stacked compatible weight matrices from different layers, alongside row and column normalization.
Lfk4uVj5gv.evidence: Theory (counterexamples, associative-memory separation) and Qwen3 0.6B and 1.7B pretraining compared against chained baselines and Muon.
Lfk4uVj5gv.claimed_gains: TensorChain outperforms all chained baselines in average token efficiency, with average token savings of 9.6% over Muon at matched validation loss.
Lfk4uVj5gv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the chained-LMO framework gives a useful unified view of Muon variants backed by substantive theory, with consistent gains over Muon across settings.
Lfk4uVj5gv.main_concern: No ablation isolates the contribution of the layer-axis normalization from the existing row and column normalizations.

cKscm6ONRj.one_liner: Extends the Continuous Thought Machine with matrix-valued short- and long-term memories that a Transformer jointly updates.
cKscm6ONRj.problem: Recurrent networks compress information into a single vector state, forcing short-term computation and long-term retention to share one representation.
cKscm6ONRj.method: The Continuous Memory Machine keeps the CTM's short-term memory of recent neural activity with neuron-level models and adds a persistent long-term memory. A Transformer updates both stores with bidirectional read-write access.
cKscm6ONRj.key_idea: A Transformer jointly updates a short-term memory of recent neuron activity and a persistent long-term memory, letting each store rewrite itself and read from and write to the other.
cKscm6ONRj.evidence: Algorithmic, in-context learning and recurrent reasoning tasks (reviews mention sorting, Copy, few-shot regression, maze, ImageNet), with ablations such as CTM-Ext. and CMM-STM.
cKscm6ONRj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating long-term and short-term memory is well motivated and performs well across diverse tasks, with meaningful ablations.
cKscm6ONRj.main_concern: The value of the long-term memory is not firmly shown: maze results vary widely across few seeds and CMM trails its own ablations on some tasks such as Copy.

Rzrg1FpHjj.one_liner: Proves dimension-independent sensitivity bounds and small coresets for axis-aligned projective clustering, with lower bounds and excess-risk bounds.
Rzrg1FpHjj.problem: Existing projective-clustering methods lack small-coreset guarantees on arbitrary real-valued inputs for j,k at least 2, and prior guarantees assume bounded input coordinates.
Rzrg1FpHjj.method: Restricts subspaces to axis-aligned j-dimensional affine subspaces, bounds total sensitivity, and applies sensitivity sampling to get weighted coresets. Also gives lower bounds and expected excess-risk bounds on the unit sphere for linear and affine subspaces.
Rzrg1FpHjj.key_idea: Restricting subspaces to be axis-aligned makes total sensitivity independent of ambient dimension, so sensitivity sampling yields small coresets without coordinate bounds.
Rzrg1FpHjj.evidence: Theoretical analysis only: upper bounds, lower bounds showing log n and exponential min{j,k} dependence are unavoidable already in R^{j+1}, and excess-risk bounds; no experiments are described.
Rzrg1FpHjj.claimed_gains: Total-sensitivity bounds of (j+k)^{O_z(min{j,k})} log n independent of ambient dimension, and O-tilde_z(sqrt(kj/n)) expected excess-risk bounds, optimal up to logarithmic factors for the linear class when d >= 2kj and n is large enough relative to kj.
Rzrg1FpHjj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is technically strong and that the upper and lower bounds together give a comprehensive picture of sensitivity for axis-aligned projective clustering.
Rzrg1FpHjj.main_concern: The axis-aligned assumption is seen as restrictive, and the paper does not make its relevance to machine learning clear (no implementation or consolidated running time of the construction).

WVsewV3lHF.one_liner: Learns a discrete codebook language, encoder and interpreter from input-output pairs, then searches programs to generalize compositionally.
WVsewV3lHF.problem: Neural networks represent computation implicitly and monolithically while symbolic program synthesis needs a predefined language, so neither recovers reusable operations for out-of-composition generalization.
WVsewV3lHF.method: NeuLP learns a codebook of vectors representing abstract operations, an encoder that builds a sequence from the codebook given a task's input-output pairs, and an interpreter that applies the sequence to a novel input. Training uses a program-space curriculum and Bayesian-guided search (per the TL;DR).
WVsewV3lHF.key_idea: A learned discrete language of codebook operations separates programmer, language and interpreter, so programs can be composed and searched, with a curriculum handling unknown program length.
WVsewV3lHF.evidence: Synthetic categorical domains compared against baselines on recombination and length out-of-composition generalization, plus ablations and a continual language-growth test (as described in the reviews); the abstract is truncated before results.
WVsewV3lHF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the three-stage design well matched to the compositional-generalization challenge, with strong recombination and length results over baselines.
WVsewV3lHF.main_concern: Gains lean on test-time search with unequal search budgets across methods, the synthetic straight-line domains suit the method's inductive bias, and the three-stage training looks complex relative to its ablation gains.

LazS8eX6C0.one_liner: Single 3D generator pairing a pretrained context encoder, run once, with a lightweight rectified-flow decoder for multimodal inputs.
LazS8eX6C0.problem: 3D generators are typically specialized to one input type, and a single model is needed that accepts text, image, sketch, depth, point cloud, voxel and bounding-box inputs with fast inference.
LazS8eX6C0.method: A large transformer context encoder reads the input once, and a lightweight rectified-flow decoder generates the 3D latent in a few ODE steps while attending to the encoder representation. The encoder is pretrained with masked token prediction on single- and multi-modal contexts, including target 3D shape tokens, keeping one modality visible while heavily masking the other.
LazS8eX6C0.key_idea: Concentrate capacity in a once-run context encoder pretrained with cross-modal masking, so only a small decoder runs at every ODE step.
LazS8eX6C0.evidence: Comparisons with specialized single-task baselines across many input settings, and ablations against a parameter-matched decoder-only baseline and an encoder trained from scratch (per reviews).
LazS8eX6C0.claimed_gains: Competitive with specialized single-task baselines across a wide range of settings, with a compact variant enabling near real-time generation; no benchmark numbers are stated in the abstract.
LazS8eX6C0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the encoder-heavy, decoder-light design is reasonable and supported by ablations, with a good efficiency-quality balance.
LazS8eX6C0.main_concern: The any-combination and unified-semantic-space claims exceed the evidence, since the decoder is trained on single inputs or pairs only, and comparisons with recent unified 3D models are missing.

G0eMUChdpQ.one_liner: Traces medical concepts through Med-LVLMs and fixes errors by steering decoder activations with probe-gated concept directions.
G0eMUChdpQ.problem: Med-LVLMs answer medical concept questions wrongly even though the concepts remain recoverable from their internal representations.
G0eMUChdpQ.method: Linear probes, representational analyses, attention analysis and activation patching trace concepts through the visual encoder, connector and decoder. MedSteer then edits decoder activations with concept-specific directions derived from original and target-masked images, with a presence probe gating each edit.
G0eMUChdpQ.key_idea: Edit decoder activations along concept directions computed from original versus target-masked images, with a presence probe gating each edit.
G0eMUChdpQ.evidence: Probing, representational analysis and activation patching on three Med-LVLMs; MedSteer evaluated on VQA across several image types with random-direction controls (per reviews).
G0eMUChdpQ.claimed_gains: MedSteer improves average VQA accuracy by 5.2-12.6 percentage points over the unedited models across three Med-LVLMs.
G0eMUChdpQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the separation of information availability from information use, the multi-method analysis across three models, and the lightweight steering that improves every model and modality combination.
G0eMUChdpQ.main_concern: The benefit beyond the supervised presence probe that gates each edit is not isolated, since a probe-only predictor baseline is missing from the main comparison.

dUohJcw31i.one_liner: Post-trains step-level agent guardrails with prefix-level stage-aligned rewards and adaptive feedback self-distillation for timely intervention.
dUohJcw31i.problem: Existing training objectives for agent safety guardrails give limited supervision on how step evidence accumulates over time and when it justifies intervention.
dUohJcw31i.method: A training framework (named ASPO in the abstract) compares each response with others sampled at the same prefix and rewards the stage-appropriate action (continue, ask, or stop), then self-distills reasoning using step annotations and rules mined from its own false alarms. Training data carry a violation taxonomy and intervention window per step, extended by self-evolving multi-agent red-teaming, producing the StepSafe guardrail.
dUohJcw31i.key_idea: Credit each decision at its own step by comparing responses sampled from the same prefix, rewarding the stage-appropriate action, plus self-distillation from step annotations and mined false-alarm rules.
dUohJcw31i.evidence: Five benchmarks, multiple model scales and ablations (per reviews), using training data extended through self-evolving multi-agent red-teaming.
dUohJcw31i.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the intervention-window formulation and stage-aware design are well motivated, with thorough multi-benchmark evaluation and ablations showing consistent gains over open-source methods.
dUohJcw31i.main_concern: The framework combines many interacting components that are hard to isolate, and training labels rely on LLM annotation and predefined intervention windows without human verification, with mostly offline evaluation.

DERWmc3gpt.one_liner: Formulates decoding as regularized optimization on the probability simplex, composing regularizers and support constraints into new decoders.
DERWmc3gpt.problem: Decoding methods are treated as isolated sampling strategies, with limited theory on the behaviors they induce and how their objectives relate.
DERWmc3gpt.method: Decoding is posed as optimization over next-token distributions that balances expected model score against regularization under support constraints, which recovers familiar decoders and allows new ones by composition. The CompoSimplex library provides configurable support rules, regularizers and simplex solvers (mirror ascent per reviews) and integrates with Hugging Face Transformers and vLLM.
DERWmc3gpt.key_idea: Treat a decoder as the solution of a regularized objective over the simplex, so composing regularizers and support rules yields new decoders without rewards, critics or parameter updates.
DERWmc3gpt.evidence: Standard samplers, individual regularizers and compositions evaluated across multiple models and reasoning tasks (four model/benchmark pairs covering math, scientific reasoning, instruction following and code, per reviews).
DERWmc3gpt.claimed_gains: Compositions realise trade-offs between single-sample quality, multi-sample quality and diversity that individual decoding objectives do not attain; no numbers are stated.
DERWmc3gpt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the simple, general and extensible formulation and the library's integration with Hugging Face Transformers and vLLM.
DERWmc3gpt.main_concern: Gains may come from an effectively different temperature rather than composition (single base temperature, no temperature-tuned baselines), the derivations are largely direct applications of known tools, and empirical scope is limited.

Dhg6TEC1WG.one_liner: Quantization-aware training that refits dequantization parameters each step using saliency-weighted least squares over clipping ranges.
Dhg6TEC1WG.problem: QAT updates latent full-precision weights while the loss and gradients are computed on lossy reconstructions, a mismatch that leads to suboptimal trajectories and a higher loss floor.
Dhg6TEC1WG.method: At each training step QUASAR reconstructs the latent weights by searching a small set of clipping ranges and fitting dequantization parameters by saliency-weighted least squares, using an exponential moving average of squared gradients as the per-parameter saliency. Theory shows optimizing this reconstruction objective tightens QAT convergence and final-loss bounds.
Dhg6TEC1WG.key_idea: Refit clipping range and dequantization parameters every QAT step by saliency-weighted least squares, with EMA squared gradients as saliency.
Dhg6TEC1WG.evidence: Theoretical convergence and final-loss bounds, plus experiments across four model families and INT4, INT3, INT2 and NVFP4 quantization formats.
Dhg6TEC1WG.claimed_gains: Lower training and evaluation loss than the compared methods across INT4, INT3, INT2 and NVFP4 formats (abstract truncated); no numeric gains are stated.
Dhg6TEC1WG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a reasonable motivation and extensive experiments across models, formats and benchmarks, with strong INT2 results and a method that is efficient and fits existing QAT pipelines.
Dhg6TEC1WG.main_concern: The second-order approximation assumes a near-stationary latent weight and small quantization error, which likely fails early in training and at low bit widths, and ablations show most gains come from clipping-range search.

uLdRQaZwO0.one_liner: Steers offline multi-objective generation by displacing a diffusion model's initial noise along a few learned directions.
uLdRQaZwO0.problem: Diffusion models trained on offline data are not inherently better than the data and must be steered toward the Pareto front, while existing methods guide or condition every sampling step.
uLdRQaZwO0.method: A Recursive Feature Machine estimates a few objective-sensitive directions in initial-noise space once per task from function values alone, and a small cache serves every trade-off, so each candidate costs one noise displacement and one ODE solve with the sampler unchanged. Optional extra guidance uses novel data-adaptive and Pareto-aware operators.
uLdRQaZwO0.key_idea: Objectives as functions of initial noise are sensitive to few directions, so a Recursive Feature Machine finds them once and the noise is displaced along them.
uLdRQaZwO0.evidence: Off-MOO-Bench across 47 tasks, plus proofs that the displacement increases the learned scalarized objective in expectation and that sweeping trade-offs recovers the flow's attainable front up to proxy and steering errors.
uLdRQaZwO0.claimed_gains: Best average hypervolume rank among generative methods on 47 tasks at comparable or lower sampling cost, and steering alone outranks the best prior generative method at a fraction of its sampling cost.
uLdRQaZwO0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find moving optimization from the sampling trajectory to the initial noise a useful, simple and modular idea, with one-time precomputation shared across preference weights.
uLdRQaZwO0.main_concern: Comparisons omit closely related generative offline-MOO methods (SPREAD, PGD-MOO), and the efficiency comparison excludes the geometry precomputation cost.

npujifLssB.one_liner: Diagnostic benchmark for evidence-grounded reasoning over ultra-resolution images, with step-level ground-truth chains of thought.
npujifLssB.problem: Existing evaluations report only final-answer accuracy, giving little insight into whether VLMs acquire and integrate the visual evidence needed to reason over ultra-resolution images.
npujifLssB.method: UltraVR spans CCTV surveillance, remote sensing, whole-slide pathology and industrial anomaly detection; each instance has a structured ground-truth chain of thought with step-level questions, intermediate answers and operation labels (evidence grounding, local perception, quantification, evidence integration, decision inference).
npujifLssB.key_idea: Decompose each question into labeled reasoning steps with verified intermediate answers, enabling process-level diagnosis instead of black-box answer scoring.
npujifLssB.evidence: VLMs evaluated on four domains; the abstract is truncated before results, and reviews describe diagnostic settings such as predicted-step versus ground-truth-prefix inputs and local-crop versus full-image inputs.
npujifLssB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the step-level intermediate questions and operation labels make the benchmark useful for locating where models fail, beyond final-answer accuracy.
npujifLssB.main_concern: The headline diagnostic (accuracy rising when ground-truth prefixes are supplied) does not isolate visual evidence acquisition from downstream reasoning, and chain validity and language-prior shortcuts are not shown to be ruled out.

jY8rAyZAlK.one_liner: Hybrid video world model combining a key-value cache with camera-conditioned recurrent linear-attention memory for faithful scene revisits.
jY8rAyZAlK.problem: Key-value caches preserve detail but grow with video length, while recurrent memory compresses history so individual past observations are no longer directly accessible, hurting reproduction of revisited regions.
jY8rAyZAlK.method: In half of the transformer blocks, attention keeps a key-value cache of past observations; in the other half it is restricted to the current chunk and complemented by a recurrent linear-attention memory whose reads and writes are conditioned on projective camera geometry. Recurrent readouts flow into the subsequent cache-backed blocks.
jY8rAyZAlK.key_idea: Interleave KV-cache blocks with local-attention blocks plus a camera-geometry-conditioned linear-attention memory, so viewpoint shapes both memory addressing and stored content.
jY8rAyZAlK.evidence: The public MIND memory benchmark and held-out recorded trajectories, against representative world models and a same-recipe full-softmax model, plus bounded-memory streaming of long videos.
jY8rAyZAlK.claimed_gains: With full history LOCI lowers peak memory at equal length by about 30% relative to full softmax, and it reproduces revisited content more faithfully than representative world models.
jY8rAyZAlK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the matched-training comparison against a full-softmax baseline convincing evidence that the hybrid memory improves revisit fidelity and memory efficiency.
jY8rAyZAlK.main_concern: The specific contribution of projective camera conditioning is not isolated, since no matched recurrent model without it is evaluated on revisit quality and several factors change at once.

xXK8N6tQ1b.one_liner: JAX reinforcement learning library on Flax NNX with explicit training state, offering host-driven and fully compiled execution routes.
xXK8N6tQ1b.problem: Researchers lack a library where reusable RL components run both with host-driven environments and inside fully compiled JAX training loops.
xXK8N6tQ1b.method: KestRL uses NNX graph/state separation to organize updates around explicit training state, with a Standard route (Gymnasium environments plus compiled learner updates) and a Compiled route (Brax environments and updates inside compiled loops with batched independent runs). SAC and PPO share learning code across the two routes.
xXK8N6tQ1b.key_idea: Split the NNX graph from state so updates become pure functions usable in a host loop, under scan and under vmap, sharing learning code across routes.
xXK8N6tQ1b.evidence: Controlled update-timing comparisons, a five-run Ant PPO study at a fixed environment-step budget, and Brax SAC configurations compared with Rejax.
xXK8N6tQ1b.claimed_gains: In a five-run Ant PPO study, KestRL Standard reduces end-to-end time by 32.8% relative to eager CleanRL and 25.7% relative to the evaluated Inductor-enabled configuration.
xXK8N6tQ1b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dual-route explicit-state design is practical and that the paper honestly reports unfavorable as well as favorable results with careful timing checks.
xXK8N6tQ1b.main_concern: Speed comparisons are confounded (different evaluation workloads, learning rates and compilation scope versus Rejax and CleanRL), so gains may not reflect library design, and reuse is not measured.

648n9Mjt6z.one_liner: GPU cluster scheduling policies that cast job migration minimization as graph-matching problems.
648n9Mjt6z.problem: As model sizes grow, job migration costs become a major bottleneck for deep learning cluster schedulers.
648n9Mjt6z.method: Migration problems during scheduling are formulated as graph matching, and migration policies that minimize the number of job migrations are integrated into existing schedulers. Per the reviews, nested assignment problems relabel GPU assignments after scheduling and placement.
648n9Mjt6z.key_idea: Cast post-scheduling GPU assignment as graph matching to minimize the number of migrations, independent of the scheduler's priorities or objective.
648n9Mjt6z.evidence: Experiments integrating the policies into existing schedulers and comparing with existing approaches; reviews indicate a simulation-based evaluation against Gavel's heuristic migration policy.
648n9Mjt6z.claimed_gains: Tesserae improves average JCT by up to 1.36x and reduces the number of migrations by up to 2.68x compared to existing approaches.
648n9Mjt6z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the scheduler-agnostic, modular design is attractive for integration into existing cluster schedulers and cuts migration overhead cheaply.
648n9Mjt6z.main_concern: The evaluation scope is narrow (one job-generation setting, mostly one- or two-GPU jobs, a single weak baseline) and the objective counts migrations rather than measured migration cost.

gBfKH31uj0.one_liner: Robust Nash learning from human feedback over preference ambiguity sets, restored to convex-concave form via a joint scenario-response adversary.
gBfKH31uj0.problem: Standard NLHF assumes a unique fixed preference, but real preferences are uncertain or pluralistic, and the robust worst-case objective loses the convex-concave structure.
gBfKH31uj0.method: The adversary is lifted to a joint scenario-response law with conditional KL regularization, restoring convex-concave structure while preserving the robust value. For finite ambiguity sets this gives a closed-form joint entropic Mirror-Prox algorithm, extended to compact-convex uncertainty sets with affine preference kernels via a localization argument.
gBfKH31uj0.key_idea: Lift the preference adversary to a joint scenario-response distribution with conditional KL regularization, making the robust game convex-concave without changing the robust value.
gBfKH31uj0.evidence: Convergence theory for finite and continuous ambiguity sets, plus experiments including an IMDb setup (per reviews).
gBfKH31uj0.claimed_gains: O(1/T) convergence guarantee for finite ambiguity sets and an O(log T/T) rate for finite-dimensional compact-convex uncertainty sets with affine preference kernels.
gBfKH31uj0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the joint-law reformulation with conditional KL is a clean, generalizable technique backed by solid convergence analysis for finite and continuous uncertainty sets.
gBfKH31uj0.main_concern: There is a gap between theory and practice: continuous-set guarantees assume exact integration while experiments use fixed quadrature, and the practical motivation and ambiguity-set construction are weakly validated.

esrWgLkiW8.one_liner: Latent diffusion with channel-ordered coarse-to-fine autoencoder latents denoised asynchronously by one shared denoiser, adding no tokens.
esrWgLkiW8.problem: Aggressive spatial compression creates a reconstruction-generation dilemma: adding channels improves reconstruction but makes generation harder.
esrWgLkiW8.method: An autoencoder orders channel prefixes from structure to detail, and one shared denoiser generates the channel groups at staggered local times without adding tokens. The method works by matching what each level represents, when it denoises, and how training is allocated across the trajectory.
esrWgLkiW8.key_idea: Put a coarse-to-fine hierarchy in latent channels and denoise channel groups asynchronously at staggered times with one shared network.
esrWgLkiW8.evidence: ImageNet-512 at 64x and 128x spatial compression across channel counts, against existing methods and a compute-matched 256-token model.
esrWgLkiW8.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing methods at every evaluated channel count under 64x and 128x spatial compression on ImageNet-512, and outperforms a 256-token model at every evaluated budget; no FID values are stated in the abstract.
esrWgLkiW8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, adds no tokens or per-step cost, and gives large gains over DC-AE-style baselines in the hardest high-compression settings.
esrWgLkiW8.main_concern: Some margins (over the 256-token model and between ablation variants) are small relative to guidance-selection and run-to-run noise, and the contribution of the widest refinement groups to generation is not fully characterized.

SoSbLCz33T.one_liner: Reduces RL post-training memory for LLMs by keeping updates in low-rank gradient sketches with predicted-KL step control.
SoSbLCz33T.problem: The memory demands of reinforcement learning post-training for LLMs remain a barrier to broader adoption.
SoSbLCz33T.method: LoGRA retains useful learning signals in compact low-rank gradient sketches that support both model updates and efficient policy synchronization. Predicted-KL step control estimates the policy change before each update and adjusts its magnitude accordingly.
SoSbLCz33T.key_idea: Compute and store gradients directly as low-rank sketches, avoiding full gradient buffers, and cap update size by predicting the KL change before applying it.
SoSbLCz33T.evidence: Reasoning tasks with 1.5B, 7B and 27B models, compared with dense Adam and LoRA, with three seeds in the main experiments (per reviews).
SoSbLCz33T.claimed_gains: Reduces average training memory by up to 45.7% without sacrificing performance, and enables stable training of a 27B-parameter model for over 1,100 steps on a single eight-GPU node where dense Adam runs out of memory.
SoSbLCz33T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a concrete memory bottleneck with real savings while keeping accuracy close to dense Adam, and that the 27B result is the most convincing evidence.
SoSbLCz33T.main_concern: Module contributions are not isolated (the full recipe differs from the dense baseline in optimizer and schedule) and the gain over closely related gradient-compression work such as Flora is not validated.

TSwdHd7wBo.one_liner: Measures off-target alerts from LLM harm monitors on 240k real conversations and reduces them with taxonomy prompting and self-distillation.
TSwdHd7wBo.problem: LLM monitors built for rare high-severity harms look strong on benign content but overflag other kinds of harmful content in deployment, a failure the paper calls monitor bycatch.
