eYnQPCW2Ca.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find an output-only interface that adds spatial information to a frozen extractor useful, and the parameter-matched single-channel control and multi-extractor results convincing.
eYnQPCW2Ca.main_concern: Limited novelty relative to beamforming-guided neural post-filtering, and no capacity-matched post-filter baseline shows that the residual formulation itself matters.

gbr1MYbnP1.one_liner: Proves testing difficulty cannot certify contrastive error auditors, and shows audit regret is bounded by corruption fidelity to real errors.
gbr1MYbnP1.problem: Contrastive error auditors prefer harder, more plausible synthetic corruptions, but it is unknown whether hardness certifies how well an auditor ranks real errors.
gbr1MYbnP1.method: Prove that with pool, prevalence, representation, and real error process fixed, two corruptions can share the full binary testing region and optimal ROC curve yet rank real errors optimally and in exact reverse. Then bound audit regret by the ranking discrepancy (at most total variation) between corruption and error distribution plus the contrastive AUC shortfall.
gbr1MYbnP1.key_idea: Fidelity of the corruption to the target error distribution, not population testing hardness, controls audit regret; hardness criteria cannot separate optimal from exactly reversed rankings.
gbr1MYbnP1.evidence: Two theorems, plus crossed detector interventions with two detectors on FB15k-237 across anomaly ratios and seeds, image experiments at matched measured difficulty, and human-error studies.
gbr1MYbnP1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theoretical separation of hardness from fidelity sharp and interesting, on an important practical question, with carefully reported experiments.
gbr1MYbnP1.main_concern: The theory-experiment link is weak (knowledge-graph results use unmatched-difficulty synthetic corruptions, real-error results are mixed), and the fidelity term depends on the unknown real-error distribution, so no label-free selection procedure follows.

U3vf5yLJ0X.one_liner: Carries a geometry-aware recurrent scene state across action chunks, jointly denoised with actions in a flow-matching action expert.
U3vf5yLJ0X.problem: Chunked VLA policies execute many actions per observation, so earlier actions change the scene, occlusion degrades visual feedback, and the previous scene estimate is not propagated to the next control call.
U3vf5yLJ0X.method: Compact scene tokens unify within-chunk scene prediction, cross-chunk state propagation, and observation-based correction: the action expert jointly denoises actions and future scene states in one flow-matching process, and the VLM fuses the final scene state with new visual input at the next call. Two-level geometric anchoring applies local depth supervision to per-view features and global 3D feature supervision to the fused scene state, using a shared geometric decoder.
U3vf5yLJ0X.key_idea: The action expert denoises actions and future scene states jointly, and the final predicted scene state becomes the next control call's prior, corrected by new observations.
U3vf5yLJ0X.evidence: Per reviews, a matched LingBot-VLA* baseline with the same backbone and action chunk; the abstract excerpt is cut off before the results.
U3vf5yLJ0X.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract excerpt is cut off before any results).
U3vf5yLJ0X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and the design coherent, with a training-only scene predictor and a matched-baseline evaluation.
U3vf5yLJ0X.main_concern: It is unclear whether gains come from joint action-scene generation or from the added geometric supervision and recurrent memory, with no simpler recurrent-memory baseline and limited evaluation under realistic occlusion.

mZMPjxp2x1.one_liner: Randomly routes freed battery-test channels to calibration cells so conformal weights are known, giving valid early-stopping false-stop guarantees.
mZMPjxp2x1.problem: Stopping unpromising battery tests early is irreversible, and conformal false-stop guarantees fail under Bayesian optimization because it breaks exchangeability of calibration cells.
mZMPjxp2x1.method: The epsilon-stream sends each freed channel slot to a calibration cell with probability epsilon, drawn from a pre-registered sequence the optimizer never reads, so conformal weights are exactly known. The paper proves a ladder of guarantees priced in channel time, calibration cells, or delay, plus two classical floors and one impossibility.
mZMPjxp2x1.key_idea: Pre-registered random epsilon-sampling of calibration cells makes the conformal weights exactly known by design, restoring finite-sample false-stop control under adaptive candidate selection.
mZMPjxp2x1.evidence: Theorems for the certified modes and replays of five public battery corpora.
mZMPjxp2x1.claimed_gains: Replaying five public battery corpora, successive halving falsely stops as many as 96% of good cells, while the audit-only weighted rule stays within alpha on every seed of the unbudgeted setting.
mZMPjxp2x1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem important and well motivated, and the epsilon-stream a simple way to make conformal weights known instead of estimating them.
mZMPjxp2x1.main_concern: The guarantees do not cover the recommended audit-only weighted rule, the certified modes are impractical (Theorem 1 never stops, Theorem 2 has recall 0.00-0.01), and novelty over weighted-conformal prior work is questioned.

ISaSI9ro04.one_liner: Represents a transformer's attention-head and neuron interactions as a graph, then mines GNN-explanation motifs into logical behavioral rules.
ISaSI9ro04.problem: LLM internal computation patterns differ across input types but are hard to characterize because of distributed interactions among attention heads and feed-forward neurons.
ISaSI9ro04.method: Graph2Rule represents a pretrained transformer's computation as a directed weighted graph whose nodes are selected attention heads and feed-forward neurons and whose edges are forward interactions. A GNN classifies behavior classes from these graphs, then explanation subgraphs are mined for recurring class-discriminative motifs and converted into logical rules.
ISaSI9ro04.key_idea: Classify behavior from component-interaction graphs with a GNN, then mine its explanation-subgraph motifs and convert them into interpretable logical rules.
ISaSI9ro04.evidence: Three datasets and multiple transformer backbones, with results over four independent runs and motif stability analyses (per reviews).
ISaSI9ro04.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that graph-based classifiers achieve strong performance across three datasets and multiple backbones).
ISaSI9ro04.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written and organized, with extensive experiments across datasets and backbones and rules that reproduce the GNN's predictions with reasonably high fidelity.
ISaSI9ro04.main_concern: Extracted rules are not validated against the original transformer's behavior (fidelity is measured to an auxiliary GNN, with no interventions on identified components), and novelty over attribution graphs is questioned.

W3BvDsi9is.one_liner: Varies deployment context (the task during which choices are made) to show LLM country preferences and utilities shift across contexts.
W3BvDsi9is.problem: Pairwise preference and value evaluations ascribe stable model-level values to LLMs but only test robustness to syntax variation and option reordering, not to changes in the surrounding task context.
W3BvDsi9is.method: Treats deployment context, the high-level task performed while making value-dependent choices (for example writing a Reddit post or a news article), as the controlled variable in two pairwise paradigms: country preference ranking and utility elicitation.
W3BvDsi9is.key_idea: Hold the pairwise elicitation fixed and vary only the surrounding deployment-context framing, then test whether rankings and fitted utilities survive.
W3BvDsi9is.evidence: Five LLMs and over 1.2M pairwise elicitations, with country preference rankings over 15 countries and utility elicitation over 50 outcomes; context induces statistically significant rank shifts and Global North favouritism also appears context-dependent.
W3BvDsi9is.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is well targeted and practically relevant, and that the two-paradigm design with controls gives evidence that preference evaluations depend on task context.
W3BvDsi9is.main_concern: Methodological gaps: keeping only order-consistent AB/BA choices and unclear ratio definitions for fitted utilities may affect the findings, and links to prompt-sensitivity and preference-aggregation work are under-discussed.

jwFxPbLlev.one_liner: Adds a semantically verified, localized-edit reward to unit-test RL so debugging models make smaller edits without hallucinating bugs.
jwFxPbLlev.problem: Unit-test-only RL reward raises pass rates but teaches models to edit more and to hallucinate bugs in code that is already correct.
jwFxPbLlev.method: PreciseCoder augments the unit-test reward with a signal for semantically verified, localized edits (edit-level precision from aligning predicted edits to reference repairs). Reviewers add that recall is gated to one when the edit passes and each score is normalized separately in GDPO.
jwFxPbLlev.key_idea: The reward combines unit-test passing with semantically verified, localized edit precision, which discourages unnecessary edits and bug hallucination.
jwFxPbLlev.evidence: Training audit and reward ablations on 4B and 9B models trained on single-line bugs, evaluation on repository-level program repair, transfer of reasoning traces to frontier models, and a linguistic analysis of thinking traces.
jwFxPbLlev.claimed_gains: Reduces average edited lines from over 13 to 3 at a pass rate on par with unit-test-only training on 4B and 9B models; reasoning traces from the 9B model raise edit precision by 4.6 points and pass rate by 1.2 points for frontier models.
jwFxPbLlev.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between passing tests and making only necessary edits is practically relevant and well supported by the training audit, reward ablations, and multi-scale evaluation, and the paper is clearly written.
jwFxPbLlev.main_concern: Novelty and clarity: the edit-precision and recall metrics come from the PDB benchmark paper, the fault-alignment step is not clearly described, and one reviewer found an evaluator implementation defect whose effect on rewards and results is unreported.

ssh6jqye1F.one_liner: Shows random collocation-point resampling delays high-frequency recovery in PINNs and proposes fixed-random interpolation schemes.
ssh6jqye1F.problem: Random collocation resampling is standard in PINN training and expected to help multi-scale problems, but its effect on high-frequency recovery has not been examined.
ssh6jqye1F.method: They compare random resampling with fixed sampling on multi-scale PINN benchmarks, link the delay to residual-gradient variance exceeding its mean, and introduce spatial and temporal interpolations between fixed and random resampling.
ssh6jqye1F.key_idea: Interpolate between fixed and random collocation resampling, in space and time, to lower residual-gradient variance while limiting collocation bias.
ssh6jqye1F.evidence: Multi-scale PINN benchmarks (mostly analytically constructed multiscale solutions with small tanh MLPs, per reviewers), with ablations on frequency, collocation count, learning rate, and Fourier features.
ssh6jqye1F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is practically relevant, the diagnostic analysis (gradient variance and SNR) is logically structured, and the experiments examine many factors including frequency, point count, and reuse ratio.
ssh6jqye1F.main_concern: Evidence is limited to constructed multiscale solutions and small MLPs, there is no theoretical analysis of the interpolation schemes, and the sources of the reuse gains remain unseparated.

zogux71Kbu.one_liner: Finds sparse OCR attention heads that overlap text retrieval/copy heads, suggesting OCR reuses a multimodal copy-and-paste circuit.
zogux71Kbu.problem: It is unknown whether a general VLM becomes an OCR specialist by building a new reading circuit or reusing an existing mechanism, in full-sequence OCR rather than local-answer retrieval.
zogux71Kbu.method: Using held-out causal interventions, they identify sparse OCR-head sets in GLM-OCR, MinerU2.5, and PaddleOCR-VL-1.6, compare them with independently identified retrieval/copy heads in general VLMs, and compare matched base and specialized models.
zogux71Kbu.key_idea: Locate OCR heads by causal intervention and show they coincide with textual retrieval/copy heads, which specialization redistributes rather than replaces.
zogux71Kbu.evidence: Causal interventions on three OCR specialist VLMs and two general VLMs, including matched base-to-specialized comparisons.
zogux71Kbu.claimed_gains: Visual OCR heads overlap retrieval/copy heads with untuned top-20 intersections of 73.3% and all-head Spearman correlations of 0.677-0.886, and specialization retains 17-20 of the top 20 heads with rank correlations of 0.874-0.942.
zogux71Kbu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mechanistic question is meaningful and that separating candidate discovery from held-out causal validation, together with the OCR-retrieval head overlap, is a strength.
zogux71Kbu.main_concern: Ablations show the heads matter but not that they implement retrieval and copying, discovery uses only correctly generated tokens, and random-head ablation controls are missing.

hVJ98YDEOv.one_liner: GRAFT continually distills new foundation-model teachers into one backbone, using the previous student as teacher, readout tokens and relational loss.
hVJ98YDEOv.problem: Multi-teacher distillation assumes a fixed teacher set, so adding a new foundation-model teacher requires repeating expensive joint distillation over all teachers.
hVJ98YDEOv.method: When a new teacher arrives, the previously distilled model serves as a teacher to preserve capabilities while the student learns jointly from it and the new teacher. Teacher Specific Readout Tokens give each teacher an independent readout of the shared encoder, and a Geometry Agnostic Relational Loss aligns a vision-language teacher by matching image-text similarity structures.
hVJ98YDEOv.key_idea: Distill each newly arriving teacher together with the previous student acting as a proxy teacher, with per-teacher readout tokens and a similarity-structure loss for incompatible geometries.
hVJ98YDEOv.evidence: Sequential integration of heterogeneous teachers (DINOv2, SigLIP2 and MASt3R named) into a single backbone covering five domains, compared with other multi-teacher distillation methods.
hVJ98YDEOv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the sequential multi-teacher formulation worth studying, with the method yielding a single backbone that acquires several heterogeneous capabilities.
hVJ98YDEOv.main_concern: Novelty is moderate since the core idea is known from continual learning, and comparisons with other multi-teacher methods are not controlled for backbones and teacher sets.

57FSJsrXwz.one_liner: Upsamples or synthesizes under-represented examples identified by early loss dynamics to mimic SAM's reduction of simplicity bias.
57FSJsrXwz.problem: The role of simplicity bias in Transformer training dynamics is theoretically unexplored, and the generalization benefit of SAM comes at higher wall-clock and memory cost.
57FSJsrXwz.method: Proves that SAM reduces simplicity bias in a multi-head self-attention model, then partitions data by early loss dynamics and upsamples or synthesizes (with diffusion LLMs) the examples tied to less-represented features.
57FSJsrXwz.key_idea: Early loss drops flag examples with dominant features, so upsampling slow-dropping examples evens out feature learning, emulating SAM's effect.
57FSJsrXwz.evidence: Theory for a multi-head self-attention model; supervised finetuning of Llama2 (7B), Phi2 (2.7B), Llama3.2 (1B), Gemma3 (1B), and Qwen3 (0.6B) with AdamW and Muon.
57FSJsrXwz.claimed_gains: Consistent improvements with AdamW and Muon across five models, with a 6x wall-clock speedup and 2x memory reduction over SAM.
57FSJsrXwz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory clearly connected to the algorithm and the empirical gains consistent across models, tasks, and optimizers.
57FSJsrXwz.main_concern: The link from simplicity bias to generalization is not causally established, the theory covers a simplified linear attention model, and novelty relative to prior simplicity-bias work is questioned.

FXK4dgnR5a.one_liner: Annotates SAE features with monotone linear threshold functions over (offset, token) literals, scored as per-token detectors at natural prevalence.
FXK4dgnR5a.problem: SAE feature descriptions are scored on balanced accuracy although features fire at a prevalence of about 10^-4, so descriptions collapse when rescored at natural prevalence.
FXK4dgnR5a.method: Treats annotating a feature as learning a Boolean function over the one-hot encoding of a token and its context, fitted as a monotone LTF over (offset, token) literals and evaluated directly as a per-token detector on held-out text, with no LLMs.
FXK4dgnR5a.key_idea: Fit each SAE feature as a monotone linear threshold function over offset-token literals, giving an executable detector whose weights expose multilingual concepts and superposition.
FXK4dgnR5a.evidence: All 147k features across three GemmaScope dictionaries annotated on a single quad-GH200 node and compared with LLM descriptions on the field's own benchmarks, plus application to a protein language model.
FXK4dgnR5a.claimed_gains: LTF annotations score about 5-24x higher than LLM descriptions at natural prevalence (where descriptions collapse to 0.01-0.05 F1) and annotate 147k features in 7 hours.
FXK4dgnR5a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the natural-prevalence critique of balanced description scoring important and the method simple, fast, and LLM-free.
FXK4dgnR5a.main_concern: It is unclear what the annotations are for and whether they are human-readable (the median annotation has several hundred literals), and the comparison with LLM descriptions changes the information and supervision available.

UK86lJSrOJ.one_liner: Models event and censoring times jointly through a shared latent frailty with neural decoders trained by a censored-data variational objective.
UK86lJSrOJ.problem: Survival models assume censoring is uninformative given covariates, which fails when unobserved factors drive both event and censoring times.
UK86lJSrOJ.method: The Deep Variational Frailty Model (DVFM) uses a shared latent frailty and nonlinear conditional decoders instead of a prespecified copula family. It is trained with a beta-regularized censored-data variational objective and amortized inference.
UK86lJSrOJ.key_idea: A shared subject-level latent frailty, inferred by amortized variational inference, couples neural event and censoring decoders in place of a fixed copula.
UK86lJSrOJ.evidence: Synthetic and semi-synthetic benchmarks with IBS and MAE, a matched ablation without the latent (d_z=0), and an identifiability theorem for a restricted multiplicative frailty model.
UK86lJSrOJ.claimed_gains: Matches the strongest dependent-censoring baseline and a Cox-Gamma frailty model on IBS and MAE, and outperforms four frailty-free models by 21-35% within a dataset.
UK86lJSrOJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling event-censoring dependence with a shared latent frailty instead of a fixed copula is well motivated and a worthwhile methodological alternative.
UK86lJSrOJ.main_concern: Gains over the strongest baseline (Cox-Gamma frailty) are marginal, and the prediction procedure using the aggregate posterior is inconsistent with the stated generative model.

EFrCRk03wb.one_liner: Decomposition-based study of when high-magnification teacher features help low-magnification pathology slide models via cross-resolution distillation.
EFrCRk03wb.problem: The conditions under which high-magnification representations usefully transfer to low-magnification whole-slide analysis are unclear.
EFrCRk03wb.method: Develops a decomposition of teacher access, representation loss and model excess, motivating three questions: whether teacher targets help, whether low-magnification students can predict them, and whether slide models benefit from the predictions. Tests them in controlled experiments comparing direct and residual prediction and native-feature retention.
EFrCRk03wb.key_idea: Separate teacher usefulness, student predictability and downstream delivery, showing reconstruction error alone does not predict whether transferred features help.
EFrCRk03wb.evidence: Ten pathology cohorts spanning classification, grading and survival prediction, with frozen-feature prediction and encoder adaptation.
EFrCRk03wb.claimed_gains: Providing teacher regional means alongside native low-magnification features raises the average primary score in all ten cohorts; no magnitudes are stated.
EFrCRk03wb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper asks a meaningful question and that its framework, separating teacher usefulness, predictability and downstream benefit, helps interpret apparent transfer gains.
EFrCRk03wb.main_concern: The experiments do not separate predictor limitations (such as the 256-dimensional bottleneck and early-stopped training) from limits of the available information, so why prediction fails remains unexplained.

ci0N7NZ7iP.one_liner: Training-free DiT caching using a channel-wise Kalman filter to predict residuals and choose between full computation and skip.
ci0N7NZ7iP.problem: Training-free diffusion caching with fixed schedules, local proxies and model-specific calibration gives limited control over cache reliability and accumulated skip errors.
ci0N7NZ7iP.method: Formulates caching as sequential residual estimation: a lightweight channel-wise Kalman filter predicts residual evolution and uses predictive uncertainty to choose FULL or SKIP. Prediction errors observed at FULL steps refine later decisions and the residual reconstructions at SKIP steps, with no change to pretrained weights and no calibration tables.
ci0N7NZ7iP.key_idea: Use a Kalman filter's predictive uncertainty to gate recompute versus reuse, and correct later skipped-step reconstructions with errors observed at full steps.
ci0N7NZ7iP.evidence: Image and video DiTs (DiT-XL/2, FLUX.1-dev, Wan2.1-1.3B) compared against full computation, step reduction and TeaCache.
ci0N7NZ7iP.claimed_gains: 1.91x latency speedup on DiT-XL/2 (FID 2.241 vs. 2.282 for full computation), 3.10x on FLUX.1-dev (LPIPS 0.199 vs. 0.368 for step reduction at 2.88x), and 2.13x on Wan2.1-1.3B (PSNR 29.55 vs. 23.16 dB for TeaCache at 2.05x).
ci0N7NZ7iP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the closed-loop correction is a coherent, calibration-free use of online feedback that improves fidelity to full computation across image and video models.
ci0N7NZ7iP.main_concern: The uncertainty score is validated only against plain-reuse error on fully computed trajectories, not against actual reconstruction errors at deployed cached states, and recent caching baselines are missing.

1RWGgfwRoD.one_liner: 9B VLM for live MOBA commentary trained with event-localized multi-turn RL that rewards turns describing telemetry-recorded events.
1RWGgfwRoD.problem: Existing streaming VLMs sound natural but often miss key events such as kills and objectives in real-time MOBA commentary.
1RWGgfwRoD.method: MOBA-VL, a 9B-parameter model, uses game telemetry that records when each event occurs as supervision for event-localized multi-turn reinforcement learning. The authors also collect MOBACast (860 professional matches, about 460 hours, three MOBA games) and MOBACast-Bench.
1RWGgfwRoD.key_idea: Use telemetry-timed events to locate which turns describe each event, then adjust token-level advantages for those turns in multi-turn RL.
1RWGgfwRoD.evidence: MOBACast-Bench from held-out tournaments, comparing against streaming VLMs, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and supervised fine-tuning, with RL variants compared under matched SFT initialization and reward.
1RWGgfwRoD.claimed_gains: MOBA-VL achieves the highest Overall score on full matches (63.25 vs. 55.12 for StreamingVLM) and clips (63.45 vs. 56.22 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), and event recall at +-3 s rises from 18.8 to 27.5 over supervised fine-tuning.
1RWGgfwRoD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the central RL comparison is well controlled (same SFT initialization, reward, and windows) and that MOBACast is a useful large dataset, with main results and ablations showing effectiveness.
1RWGgfwRoD.main_concern: The evaluation does not cleanly measure timely, correctly attributed commentary (timestamps removed, wide matching tolerance, assist credit accepted), so latency and attribution quality remain unclear.

J9thOiL6oK.one_liner: Training-free graph of source-linked behaviors helps monitors flag consequential agent decisions, evaluated on the new AgentMonBench.
J9thOiL6oK.problem: For long-horizon agents, the volume of activity and fragmented evidence make it hard to decide which decisions warrant user verification.
J9thOiL6oK.method: AgentMonBench is a software-engineering benchmark with three subsets covering requirement-behavior alignment and awareness of consequential decisions. The Evidence-Grounded Behavior Graph (EBG) groups source-linked evidence into behaviors, organizes their relationships into a graph, and presents task-oriented views to monitors.
J9thOiL6oK.key_idea: Group source-linked evidence into behaviors, link them in a graph, and show monitors task-oriented views of that graph instead of the raw context.
J9thOiL6oK.evidence: Experiments across eight models on three benchmark subsets (SpecGAP, SilentSwap, FeedbackTrace), hyperparameter and input-scale tests, and real-world application examples.
J9thOiL6oK.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says EBG improves decision identification and evidence localization in most settings compared with direct access to the original context, without figures).
J9thOiL6oK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the oversight problem is practically useful, the three benchmark subsets are well motivated with independent review, and EBG is simple, training-free, and improves evidence localization.
J9thOiL6oK.main_concern: The benchmark gives monitors privileged knowledge (for example exactly five changes or a guaranteed decision), disclosure operating points remain weak, and EBG's benefit in real agent harnesses is not established.

9qH7yp0oGW.one_liner: Conditions a temporal imputation diffusion model on ViT features of rendered line graphs through a cross-attention bottleneck with learnable anchors.
9qH7yp0oGW.problem: When missing values are dense or form long contiguous gaps, observed temporal context is sparse and gives weak structural guidance to diffusion-based time-series imputation.
9qH7yp0oGW.method: VT-Diff renders multivariate series as variable-aware line graphs and encodes them with a Vision Transformer into global and local structural tokens. A Cross-Attention Bottleneck with learnable temporal anchors turns these into time-step-wise conditions for the temporal denoising network, while generation stays in the numerical domain.
9qH7yp0oGW.key_idea: Use the rendered-plot visual prior only as conditioning, translating ViT tokens into per-time-step conditions via learnable temporal anchors, while diffusion generates numerical values.
9qH7yp0oGW.evidence: Seven datasets, 17 deterministic and probabilistic baselines, point, subsequence, and block missingness at several rates, component ablations, downstream forecasting, and computational cost.
9qH7yp0oGW.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract is cut off after mentioning extensive experiments).
9qH7yp0oGW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is sensible, keeping generation numerical while using visual structure as a prior, with broad evaluation across datasets, baselines, and missing patterns.
9qH7yp0oGW.main_concern: Gains are not isolated to the visual representation, since the rendered image derives from interpolated observations and a numerical conditioning branch, added capacity, or the auxiliary loss may explain the improvement.

wptKDpt3fz.one_liner: CANOPY compresses retrieved multimodal evidence by scoring hierarchy nodes at adaptive granularity and requesting follow-up retrieval when evidence is insufficient.
wptKDpt3fz.problem: Multimodal RAG must choose how much context to keep within each retrieved item, since coarse units include irrelevant content and uniformly fine selection drops needed context, and existing compressors are modality-specific.
wptKDpt3fz.method: Retrieved items are represented as hierarchies, a node encoder fine-tuned on gold evidence scores regions against the query, and parent-relative refinement selects regions at different granularities without LLM calls. A critic requests targeted follow-up retrieval when evidence seems insufficient, and new items are compressed before being added.
wptKDpt3fz.key_idea: Compare child and parent relevance scores in a hierarchy so branches stop at different depths, with a critic triggering extra retrieval when evidence is insufficient.
wptKDpt3fz.evidence: Five QA benchmarks over a 33M-item heterogeneous corpus, with ablations of iterative retrieval, compression, and node-encoder fine-tuning using paired bootstrap confidence intervals per reviews.
wptKDpt3fz.claimed_gains: Higher average answer accuracy than the evaluated retrieval baselines across five QA benchmarks; no numbers stated in the visible abstract.
wptKDpt3fz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified, modality-agnostic compression with parent-relative refinement is well motivated and that the experiments on a large heterogeneous corpus are rigorous and honestly reported.
wptKDpt3fz.main_concern: Most accuracy gains come from critic-guided iterative retrieval rather than the compression mechanism, whose accuracy effects have confidence intervals including zero.

3Loaz94xKS.one_liner: Retrieval agent keeping a persistent, never-compressed evidence state of cited source spans separate from compressible interaction history.
3Loaz94xKS.problem: In long retrieval-agent histories, supporting observations are buried among irrelevant hits, errors, and reasoning traces, and truncating or summarizing the history can discard evidence.
3Loaz94xKS.method: Code2Evidence is a coding-based retrieval agent that searches raw corpora with shell commands and banks source spans with provenance in an evidence state that guides further search and is the only input to the final answer. Multiple role-specialized searchers can reconcile their evidence states.
3Loaz94xKS.key_idea: Separate a freely compressible transient history from an append-only, provenance-tagged evidence state that drives search and is the sole input for answering.
3Loaz94xKS.evidence: Six Wikipedia QA datasets (MHQA), FinQA, and BioProBench with GPT-5.4-mini and GPT-5.5, plus GLM-5.3 on MHQA, holding model, tools, turn budget, and compression policy fixed.
3Loaz94xKS.claimed_gains: Answering from the evidence state matches or beats answering from compressed history in all ten task-backbone pairs, and with GLM-5.3 on MHQA adding the evidence state raises meaning-match accuracy from 74.3% to 80.7%.
3Loaz94xKS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evidence-state separation is a clear, training-free, backbone-agnostic fix for evidence being buried or lost in long histories, supported by controlled comparisons and ablations.
3Loaz94xKS.main_concern: Novelty over memory-based agents (MemGPT, A-Mem) is limited, and the gain is not isolated from extra tokens, actions, and compute or from simpler persistent-scratchpad alternatives.

UDSidLSfle.one_liner: Proves cautious momentum stays accelerated for coordinate coupling O(kappa^-1/2) and diverges at Omega(kappa^-1/2) on time-varying quadratics.
UDSidLSfle.problem: It is unknown how much off-diagonal coordinate coupling the raw cautious momentum rule, which suppresses updates whose signs disagree with the gradient, can tolerate while keeping accelerated convergence.
UDSidLSfle.method: Analyzes the raw, unnormalized cautious momentum rule on time-varying quadratics with a common minimizer, diagonal curvature ratio kappa, and relative coupling rho, using a piecewise quadratic Lyapunov argument for convergence and an explicit predetermined Hessian sequence for divergence (abstract truncated).
UDSidLSfle.key_idea: Match a Lyapunov-based convergence bound at coupling rho = O(kappa^-1/2) with an explicit divergence construction at rho = Omega(kappa^-1/2), identifying the sharp robustness scale.
UDSidLSfle.evidence: Theorems under a fixed tuning with zero initial momentum, with explicit universal constants for convergence and divergence; reviewers note there are no experiments.
UDSidLSfle.claimed_gains: Reaches relative error epsilon within O(sqrt(kappa) log(2+kappa) log(1/epsilon)) gradient evaluations under coupling rho = O(kappa^-1/2), versus Theta(kappa log(1/epsilon)) for linear methods with predetermined coefficients; convergence and divergence constants differ by about 2.14.
UDSidLSfle.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is clearly posed and that matching convergence and divergence bounds, up to a constant of about 2, give a sharp and well-stated characterization.
UDSidLSfle.main_concern: The setting is narrow (one fixed tuning, exact gradients, time-varying quadratics with a common minimizer, constants around 10^11, no experiments), so relevance to practical cautious optimizers is unclear.

ulZlVk7YB0.one_liner: Trains world models with nested Matryoshka representations so planners can vary predictive fidelity across replanning, CEM iterations, and rollout depth.
ulZlVk7YB0.problem: Planning with learned world models trades predictive fidelity against compute, and existing approaches vary search effort with a fixed latent representation or train separate models for different representation sizes.
ulZlVk7YB0.method: MWM learns a shared hierarchy of predictive representations that can be truncated or expanded at test time without retraining. The planner can then allocate high-fidelity computation selectively across episode-level replanning, CEM optimization iterations, and rollout depth.
ulZlVk7YB0.key_idea: Train one world model with nested predictive fidelities, then schedule fidelity during planning so high fidelity is spent only where fine-grained prediction matters.
ulZlVk7YB0.evidence: Variable-fidelity planning against fixed-fidelity planning baselines on navigation and manipulation tasks.
ulZlVk7YB0.claimed_gains: Matches the success rate of the full-fidelity baseline at up to 108.8x less compute and exceeds the best baseline by up to 59% at the same compute budget.
ulZlVk7YB0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transferring nested Matryoshka representations to action-conditioned world models is a clean idea that lets fidelity vary during planning, with strong performance-compute trade-offs.
ulZlVk7YB0.main_concern: Statistical evidence is thin: scheduling gains rest on one training seed, a single evaluation seed, and selected best configurations without uncertainty estimates or frozen final tests, and key concepts such as fidelity and schedules are hard to follow.

a3lClegCtb.one_liner: Agent harness converts a reference implementation into an IR, analyzes transformations, and runs a measurement-gated optimization loop for multi-GPU deployment.
a3lClegCtb.problem: Real-time multimodal pipelines need application-specific placement, streaming, and parallelism decisions, and existing serving systems and compilers commit to limited transformations so each application needs a hand-crafted implementation.
a3lClegCtb.method: Under a chain-of-program paradigm, the agent converts a developer-written reference into an IR capturing data dependencies and persistent state, validates it with a sequential interpreter, and statically analyzes it for candidate transformations. The agent then implements, verifies, and benchmarks them in a measurement-gated loop.
a3lClegCtb.key_idea: Guide a generic coding agent with a dependency- and state-annotated IR and static transformation analysis, accepting optimizations only when measured gains hold.
a3lClegCtb.evidence: Five applications including video world models and multimodal LLMs on NVIDIA B200 GPUs, with a LiveAvatar ablation and a formal task-graph analysis of the deployment problem per reviews.
a3lClegCtb.claimed_gains: Up to ~70x latency reduction while sustaining the highest observed throughput, up to 2.8x throughput improvement on NVIDIA B200 GPUs, and up to 3.6x (abstract is cut off after this figure).
a3lClegCtb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the work has strong analytical grounding (task-graph formalization and trade-off proofs) and shows gains over a non-trivial baseline across hardware and agents, with ablations tied to failure modes.
a3lClegCtb.main_concern: Evidence of generality is narrow (similar application archetypes, ablations mostly on LiveAvatar, a proprietary agent), and the headline latency is measured against a weak reference.

HvFVDCH671.one_liner: Proves gradient-descent convergence and a memorization-generalization threshold for a one-layer Transformer DDPM on Gaussian mixtures.
HvFVDCH671.problem: It is unclear how finite-sample training shapes the learned denoiser in diffusion models and when it leads to memorization rather than generalization.
HvFVDCH671.method: They analyze a one-layer single-head Transformer trained by gradient descent on the DDPM objective with Gaussian mixture data. GD learns the empirical mode means and within-mode variance, and a Gaussian-CDF memorization rate gives a sample complexity threshold, with an empirical-prototype attraction mechanism behind memorization.
HvFVDCH671.key_idea: Gradient descent drives the denoiser to empirical mode means and variance, so samples are attracted to empirical prototypes, and a Gaussian-CDF rate sets the memorization threshold.
HvFVDCH671.evidence: Theoretical analysis for Gaussian mixture data under the DDPM objective, validated by simple experiments per reviews.
HvFVDCH671.claimed_gains: not stated (theory: training loss approaches the empirical oracle denoising risk and the generalization gap diminishes with sample size)
HvFVDCH671.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses an important question with a unified finite-sample analysis linking GD convergence, generalization, and sample-specific memorization, with a useful mechanism.
HvFVDCH671.main_concern: The setting is restrictive (one-layer single-head Transformer, orthogonal-mean Gaussian mixtures), its generality and novelty over prior memorization theory are unclear, and some proof steps need justification.

LOwG4xUpfa.one_liner: Samples trajectories from a population of parameter-perturbed policies to produce label-free group-relative signals for continual test-time learning.
LOwG4xUpfa.problem: Repeated test-time adaptation with self-generated supervision can cause policy collapse, degraded reasoning, and catastrophic forgetting in LLMs, and external supervision is often unavailable.
LOwG4xUpfa.method: Builds a population of locally perturbed policies around the current model, samples trajectories from those parameter regions, and aggregates them into label-free group-relative learning signals that update the central student.
LOwG4xUpfa.key_idea: Explore in parameter space with perturbed copies of the policy so diverse self-supervision persists even when the central policy drifts.
LOwG4xUpfa.evidence: Single-task test-time adaptation and multi-task continual learning experiments across multiple backbones; reviews cite four backbones, MATH-500, MMLU, and ablations.
LOwG4xUpfa.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract.
LOwG4xUpfa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the topic and the combination with evolution strategies timely, report the highest average accuracy across four backbones, and value the failure-mode analysis.
LOwG4xUpfa.main_concern: The link to Evolution Strategies is questioned (no fitness-based selection), baseline values look low, and the continual-learning claim is validated on one small backbone and one task order.

GYxHHEF2d0.one_liner: ReFrame dynamically rebinds GPU memory frames between expert weights and KV cache in MoE serving.
GYxHHEF2d0.problem: Static GPU memory partitioning between expert weights and KV cache leaves underutilized expert memory unusable by the KV cache, so requests wait for KV capacity.
GYxHHEF2d0.method: Typed frame rebinding lets GPU memory alternate between expert and KV roles while keeping the native tensor and block views each needs. A bounded allocation policy decides when and how much to borrow, confines each loan to the triggering request, and uses private capacity first.
GYxHHEF2d0.key_idea: Rebind typed memory frames between expert and KV use under tagged ownership, borrowing a bounded number of frames confined to the triggering request.
GYxHHEF2d0.evidence: Two mixed workloads with Qwen3-235B-A22B against CPU-offloading baselines vLLM 0.29 and SGLang 0.5.17, plus an independent matched-batch comparison with vLLM 0.29.
GYxHHEF2d0.claimed_gains: Geometric mean speedups of 2.75x over vLLM 0.29 and 2.94x over SGLang 0.5.17 in trace completion time, and 2.74x in an independent matched-batch comparison with vLLM 0.29.
GYxHHEF2d0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the typed-frame ownership design is a coherent solution to a practical memory-management problem and that end-to-end gains over CPU-offload baselines persist across workloads, with transparent reporting.
GYxHHEF2d0.main_concern: The isolated benefit of rebinding is unclear: the 12% long-request TTFT gain comes from retrospectively selected pairs, the four-pair average is only 1.24% with a 2.29% TPOT p95 regression, and baselines use generic layer-wise CPU offloading rather than MoE-aware offloading.

M8SLVtX9zL.one_liner: Data-derived contractible covers split topologically complex supports into regions modeled by a posterior-regularized mixture of normalizing flows.
M8SLVtX9zL.problem: Invertible flows cannot change support topology without severe growth in their bi-Lipschitz constants.
M8SLVtX9zL.method: CoCoFlow constructs a contractible cover of the target support and trains flow components confined to its elements. Posterior regularization coordinates the mixture while retaining exact likelihood evaluation and deterministic maximum-likelihood training.
M8SLVtX9zL.key_idea: Assign separate normalizing-flow components to contractible cover elements that are homotopically compatible with a Gaussian base.
M8SLVtX9zL.evidence: Synthetic and real-world density-estimation experiments compare likelihood and generative-map continuity, including Jacobian analysis.
M8SLVtX9zL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find topology-aware graph covers a useful direction and regard the numerical results as encouraging.
M8SLVtX9zL.main_concern: The core topological construction is difficult to follow and needs clearer explanations, illustrations, and worked examples.

LK65ZzNO4J.one_liner: KL policy regularization and occupancy-weighted quadratic reward penalties yield fast rates for a regularized adversarial imitation objective.
LK65ZzNO4J.problem: The finite-sample benefits of combining reward and policy regularization in adversarial imitation learning remain underexplored.
LK65ZzNO4J.method: Dually Regularized AIL combines KL-regularized policy learning with a quadratic reward penalty weighted by expert and learner occupancies. Its analysis uses online mirror descent for convex reward classes and optimistic policy learning.
LK65ZzNO4J.key_idea: Regularize both sides of the imitation game using policy KL and an occupancy-weighted quadratic reward penalty.
LK65ZzNO4J.evidence: Theoretical guarantees cover finite-horizon Markov decision processes with general function approximation and finite expert trajectories and online episodes.
LK65ZzNO4J.claimed_gains: For K online episodes and N expert trajectories, the regularized imitation-gap bound is O-tilde(1/K+1/N), yielding O-tilde(1/epsilon) sample complexity in both resources for fixed regularization.
LK65ZzNO4J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the reward-side analysis and theoretical investigation of regularization in adversarial imitation learning.
LK65ZzNO4J.main_concern: Fast rates concern a regularized saddle-point objective and do not establish comparable improvements in the original expert–learner imitation gap.

sREFxShRQP.one_liner: Global change-focused scoring and local multimodal judgments rerank composed-image retrieval candidates against the requested modification.
sREFxShRQP.problem: Description-based retrieval can prioritize unchanged reference content and fail to verify what candidate images preserve or modify.
sREFxShRQP.method: Sharpen strengthens the requested change in query embeddings and suppresses images similar to many composed queries. It then reuses an MLLM to judge candidates both against the change alone and against the full reference-conditioned request.
sREFxShRQP.key_idea: Combine change-emphasized query scoring and popularity suppression with candidate judgments made with and without the reference image.
sREFxShRQP.evidence: Training-free evaluation uses a 4B open-weight MLLM on three benchmarks, including CIRCO, CIRR, and FashionIQ, with component and sensitivity studies.
sREFxShRQP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the failure mode well motivated and the modular scoring and verification approach empirically promising.
sREFxShRQP.main_concern: Popularity suppression uses other evaluated test queries, giving transductive information unavailable to query-independent baselines.

ZYx3wrCsTq.one_liner: Measures paired generative-loss changes under controlled image interventions to test alignment with human naturalness judgments.
ZYx3wrCsTq.problem: Raw generative losses reflect scene content and complexity, obscuring their relationship to perceived naturalness.
ZYx3wrCsTq.method: The study applies content-preserving paired interventions to facial configurations and illumination, then measures directional changes in generators' native prediction errors. It compares these changes with human ratings while controlling for encoder distances and image-quality metrics.
ZYx3wrCsTq.key_idea: Subtract native prediction losses across content-preserving intervention pairs to isolate sensitivity to facial and illumination relationships.
ZYx3wrCsTq.evidence: Tests span 25 open image and video generators, human psychophysical judgments, the Thatcher effect, and shape-dependent illumination inconsistencies.
ZYx3wrCsTq.claimed_gains: Item-level correlations with human judgments span r = .30–.84 on faces and .04–.64 on illumination scenes.
ZYx3wrCsTq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled paired interventions and carefully designed human evaluation and statistical analysis.
ZYx3wrCsTq.main_concern: Evaluation covers only facial configurations and illumination, limiting conclusions about human naturalness perception more broadly.

VmIZ1oePtW.one_liner: Amortizes spike-and-slab variable selection with a transformer pretrained on synthetic linear models containing pairwise interactions.
VmIZ1oePtW.problem: Exact Bayesian variable selection scales exponentially, while per-dataset MCMC can be costly and fail to converge within budget.
VmIZ1oePtW.method: LinearPFN trains a prior-data fitted transformer on synthetic datasets from an explicit conjugate prior. One forward pass returns inclusion probabilities, posterior-mean coefficients, and predictive distributions without per-dataset fitting.
VmIZ1oePtW.key_idea: A transformer learns spike-and-slab posterior quantities from prior-generated datasets, including main effects and pairwise interactions.
VmIZ1oePtW.evidence: The network is checked against exact enumerated posteriors in tractable settings and evaluated on real social-science predictor matrices with generated outcomes and prior-misspecification tests.
VmIZ1oePtW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the explicit prior and validation against exact posteriors as strong evidence for the intended amortized inference task.
VmIZ1oePtW.main_concern: Prior-matched benchmarks and limited misspecification tests leave the method's applicability outside its training assumptions insufficiently established.

lgenoAYj7q.one_liner: Combines gated variable-axis and time-axis attention with randomized training horizons and adaptive multiscale forecasts.
lgenoAYj7q.problem: Universal forecasting must accommodate changing variable schemas, prediction horizons, and temporal resolutions within one model.
lgenoAYj7q.method: Morpheus-2.0 places targets and covariates on a variable-time grid and mixes parallel attention over both axes with learned layer gates and axis-aware rotary encoding. It randomizes training horizons, while Morpheus-Multiscale weights forecasts across temporal resolutions.
lgenoAYj7q.key_idea: Parallel variable and temporal attention share each layer through learned gates, while horizon sampling and resolution weighting handle differing forecast scales.
lgenoAYj7q.evidence: GIFT-Eval experiments span domains and frequencies, with ablations of attention, positional encoding, horizons, patch widths, and training curriculum.
lgenoAYj7q.claimed_gains: Morpheus-2.0 attains 0.685 relative MASE with 81M parameters on GIFT-Eval.
lgenoAYj7q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified target-covariate representation and the extensive analysis of architectural and training choices.
lgenoAYj7q.main_concern: Comparisons do not sufficiently isolate architectural gains from established axial attention and encoder ensembling.

sdbvbJqDi7.one_liner: Feeds token readouts back into a persistent continuous diffusion state to preserve dependencies during parallel language generation.
sdbvbJqDi7.problem: Parallel discrete diffusion samples tokens independently, while continuous diffusion lacks token-configuration feedback during denoising.
sdbvbJqDi7.method: HC-DLM couples a persistent continuous latent trajectory with discrete token readouts under a variational token-likelihood objective. Each step feeds the readout tokens back as a scaffold for the next latent update.
sdbvbJqDi7.key_idea: Tokens read from a shared continuous latent at every denoising step guide the next update of that persistent latent state.
sdbvbJqDi7.evidence: Matched-size comparisons cover Sudoku, Countdown, LM1B, and OpenWebText, with ablations of token scaffolding, corruption kernels, and sampling steps.
sdbvbJqDi7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the continuous-discrete coupling promising and the structured-task results supported by component ablations.
sdbvbJqDi7.main_concern: Differences in guidance, baseline adaptations, and training configurations complicate attribution of gains to the proposed coupling.

DXxip7cMa7.one_liner: Checks financial agents' executed actions and business states against explicit permissions while measuring lawful task completion.
DXxip7cMa7.problem: Financial agents must respect state-dependent permissions without sacrificing useful task completion, which aggregate or final-text evaluations can miss.
DXxip7cMa7.method: The benchmark defines executable asset-management cases across customer service, internal assistance, and autonomous production. Checkers score actions, intermediate events, and resulting states, with selected continuation tests separating claimed authorization from changed records.
DXxip7cMa7.key_idea: Executable rules compare agent actions and business-state transitions with recorded permissions, scoring violations separately from legitimate completion.
DXxip7cMa7.evidence: Evaluation uses 877 cases across thirteen business subscenarios and nine models in 144 model-agent-defense configurations.
DXxip7cMa7.claimed_gains: Hermes lowers Qwen3.6-27B's adversarial violation from 24.6% to 12.8% but raises Qwen3.8-27B's from 7.9% to 19.4%.
DXxip7cMa7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating both executed violations and lawful completion prevents blanket refusal from counting as successful safety.
DXxip7cMa7.main_concern: Imperfect checker accuracy and limited auditing weaken confidence in the reported safety differences.

doVwH1xfbE.one_liner: Separates cache preparation and request workflows to benchmark approximate KV-cache reuse against full-prefill quality and latency.
doVwH1xfbE.problem: Reusing context-dependent KV states across requests can alter generation quality, with trade-offs varying by model and workflow.
doVwH1xfbE.method: KVBench modularizes tasks, models, reuse methods, and request workflows. It compares task quality and online time-to-first-token with full-prefill references across context reuse, agent communication, and reusable skills.
doVwH1xfbE.key_idea: Controlled task-model-workflow combinations pair approximate cache reuse with full-prefill references to measure quality and first-token latency.
doVwH1xfbE.evidence: Experiments cover five full- or hybrid-attention models, RAG-style reuse, multi-agent communication, and independently prepared skill caches on SkillsBench.
doVwH1xfbE.claimed_gains: HYPIC TRR retains 83.0% of skill-provided reward improvement while reducing first-call time-to-first-token to roughly 20–30% of full prefill on executions with large reusable-context fractions.
doVwH1xfbE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the broad controlled evaluation and explicit treatment of request structure and cache preparation.
doVwH1xfbE.main_concern: Small evaluation sets and single agent rollouts leave uncertainty around quality retention and method rankings unquantified.

fORSAsyOix.one_liner: Uses matched numerical-shortcut variants to measure language models' shortcut execution, applicability judgments, and problem generation.
fORSAsyOix.problem: Language models may execute shortcuts when prompted yet fail to recognize when those shortcuts apply.
fORSAsyOix.method: SenseMath varies digit scale and shortcut availability while holding item format consistent. It evaluates shortcut use, applicability judgment, and problem generation through strong-shortcut, weak-shortcut, and control variants.
fORSAsyOix.key_idea: Matched arithmetic variants manipulate numerical structure and digit scale to distinguish shortcut execution from judgments of shortcut applicability.
fORSAsyOix.evidence: The benchmark contains 4,800 items spanning eight shortcut categories and four digit scales, evaluated across six model configurations.
fORSAsyOix.claimed_gains: Explicit number-sense prompting yields accuracy gains of up to 23.0 percentage points on shortcut-amenable items.
fORSAsyOix.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the carefully designed benchmark and its examination of numerical reasoning beyond answer accuracy.
fORSAsyOix.main_concern: The behavioral definition of number sense needs clearer grounding and separation from numerical representation or ordinary problem solving.

6eWAPkGv6S.one_liner: Decomposes functional connectomes into scan-conditioned population predictions and participant effects inferred from sets of support scans.
6eWAPkGv6S.problem: Treating repeated fMRI scans independently leaves stable participant information implicit and mixes it with task-dependent variation.
6eWAPkGv6S.method: P-MEGA combines a signed multi-window graph encoder and shared edge decoder with a low-rank participant random effect. A permutation-invariant set encoder infers a Gaussian posterior from support scans, with exact Gaussian inference also available at test time.
6eWAPkGv6S.key_idea: An additive participant-specific Gaussian random effect shared across scans supplements a scan-conditioned population reconstruction.
6eWAPkGv6S.evidence: Evaluation covers two multi-paradigm cohorts, including HCP with 865 young adults and 9 paradigms, using participant-separated folds and target-excluded support-swap controls.
6eWAPkGv6S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that controlled support swaps provide meaningful evidence of participant-specific information beyond demographic matching.
6eWAPkGv6S.main_concern: Target-excluded transfer experiments lack matched baseline comparisons, leaving the method's comparative advantage unresolved.

30lO0CpoMg.one_liner: Iteratively tests marker hypotheses against expression data, retaining unresolved cell clusters for further analysis or expert escalation.
30lO0CpoMg.problem: Fixed references incompletely cover rare, transitional, and context-dependent cell populations.
30lO0CpoMg.method: CellMaster-Core generates cell-type hypotheses and marker panels, inspects cluster expression and detection patterns, and revises labels with recorded rationales. Unresolved clusters trigger further iterations, sub-clustering, or escalation to specialists or humans.
30lO0CpoMg.key_idea: Iterative marker-hypothesis testing against cluster expression guides label revision, abstention, and targeted escalation.
30lO0CpoMg.evidence: Evaluation includes a nine-dataset breadth benchmark and deeper comparisons on three datasets against agents, zero-shot scGPT, and reference-based specialists.
30lO0CpoMg.claimed_gains: Core exceeds Biomni on every depth dataset, with up to a 17.6% relative increase in Cell Ontology score.
30lO0CpoMg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the ability to leave ambiguous clusters unresolved and expose evidence for further checks or expert intervention.
30lO0CpoMg.main_concern: The nine-dataset breadth results use AutoFill, while reference-free Core has results on only three datasets.

XDKx2J3Hg8.one_liner: Interleaving compressed video and player-tracking tokens in a causal Transformer learns predictive football play representations.
XDKx2J3Hg8.problem: Player-tracking trajectories lack visual context to disambiguate physical interactions in American football, while fusing raw game video with tracking incurs high computational cost.
XDKx2J3Hg8.method: NFL-World learns modality-specific representations from synchronized video and player tracking via temporal prediction and compresses them into compact latent tokens. A causal Transformer interleaves these tokens to predict successive modality states, fusing player geometry and visual context.
XDKx2J3Hg8.key_idea: Compress temporal representations of synchronized video and player tracking into latent tokens and interleave them in a next-state causal Transformer.
XDKx2J3Hg8.evidence: Evaluations on 2025 NFL game data test play classification, similar-play retrieval, and one-second player-motion forecasting with compression and modality ablations.
XDKx2J3Hg8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly modeling synchronized player tracking and game video with compressed interleaved tokens addresses an underexplored sports-analytics setting while cutting fusion compute.
XDKx2J3Hg8.main_concern: All three reviewers note weak empirical support for multimodal world-model claims, as adding video improves classification only marginally (+0.73 pp), worsens next-second motion forecasting relative to tracking alone, lacks multi-step rollouts or counterfactuals, and compares fine-tuned fusion against frozen baselines.

La5pYzpBsd.one_liner: Pose–appearance graphs identify replaceable observations for online eviction from fixed-capacity spatial memory in long-horizon video generation.
La5pYzpBsd.problem: Full-history memory grows without bound, while one-time retention decisions fail to adapt as stored observations become redundant or low fidelity.
La5pYzpBsd.method: Keepsake builds a graph over retained and newly generated observations using camera-pose proximity and visual similarity. A training-free controller revisits retention priorities according to available substitutes and evicts redundant observations within fixed capacity.
La5pYzpBsd.key_idea: Recompute each observation's redundancy from pose–appearance affinities to current alternatives before deciding which memories to retain.
La5pYzpBsd.evidence: MemCam and WorldMem experiments compare full retention and budget-matched FIFO, K-center, and MCE, measuring generation quality, memory capacity, and retrieval time.
La5pYzpBsd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find dynamic fixed-capacity memory management practical and recognize improvements in long-horizon quality and memory footprint.
La5pYzpBsd.main_concern: Ablations do not sufficiently establish whether gains come from the proposed relational redundancy mechanism rather than removing degraded memories.

SAPs4Kiod0.one_liner: A virtual search tree combines heavy-light decomposition and sparse-vector searches for private frequent-substring mining.
SAPs4Kiod0.problem: Private substring mining faces a tradeoff between near-optimal error and practical time and space complexity.
SAPs4Kiod0.method: The algorithm represents frequent substrings in a private virtual tree and searches it using heavy-light decomposition and the sparse vector technique. Constant-time frequency and subtree-size oracles avoid materializing the full tree.
SAPs4Kiod0.key_idea: A virtual substring tree supports private monotone-tree searches through heavy-light decomposition, sparse-vector queries, and constant-time oracles.
SAPs4Kiod0.evidence: The theoretical analysis establishes improved error guarantees with near-linear time and space for user-level differentially private substring mining.
SAPs4Kiod0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize quantitative improvements over prior private substring-mining algorithms.
SAPs4Kiod0.main_concern: Reviewers find the central construction and proof difficult to understand or audit from the main paper.

wnaqms59aX.one_liner: Online denoising rollouts train constrained diffusion models with guidance included in the sampling process.
wnaqms59aX.problem: Training-time constraint objectives and inference-time corrections can mismatch the states encountered during diffusion sampling.
wnaqms59aX.method: IMCD fine-tunes diffusion models by differentiating through online rollouts with the fixed noise schedule used during sampling. Constraint violations along the denoising trajectory inform training.
wnaqms59aX.key_idea: Backpropagating constraint losses through online denoising rollouts exposes training to the guided sampler's intermediate states.
wnaqms59aX.evidence: Experiments on bouncing-ball simulation and real-world traffic trajectories compare constraint satisfaction and sampling quality against prior methods.
wnaqms59aX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the training-sampling mismatch meaningful, with clear presentation and empirical improvements noted by two reviewers.
wnaqms59aX.main_concern: The rollout loss and learned guidance scaling overlap with prior constrained-diffusion methods, leaving the methodological distinction unclear.

9vJiGCBgy5.one_liner: LLM-generated JavaScript games run through an efficient Gym-compatible pipeline for pixel-based reinforcement learning.
9vJiGCBgy5.problem: Creating or modifying reinforcement-learning game environments requires extensive manual coding.
9vJiGCBgy5.method: PlayTrain combines prompted JavaScript game generation with efficient execution, drawing, rasterization, and shared-memory collection. The generated games support both human play and agent training.
9vJiGCBgy5.key_idea: A shared JavaScript game file feeds human-playable environments and a fast pixel-observation reinforcement-learning pipeline.
9vJiGCBgy5.evidence: Atari and ProcGen clones, modified game variants, throughput measurements, and learning curves demonstrate the framework.
9vJiGCBgy5.claimed_gains: PlayTrain trains pixel-based agents end-to-end at over 1M agent-decisions per second on a single GPU node.
9vJiGCBgy5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical combination of editable LLM-generated games, easy human playtesting, and efficient training.
9vJiGCBgy5.main_concern: Automated checks establish format and determinism but do not verify game-rule fidelity or quantify required human refinement.

FlVspU2igD.one_liner: Evidence-grounded corrupted recommendation queries test whether LLMs proactively detect and handle faulty premises.
FlVspU2igD.problem: Recommendation benchmarks seldom test whether assistants recognize flawed requests using user and candidate evidence.
FlVspU2igD.method: RPCBench pairs visible recommendation contexts with corrupted queries across five domains and ten premise-failure types. Its evaluation separates detection, localization, handling strategy, and evidence faithfulness.
FlVspU2igD.key_idea: Controlled premise corruption within visible recommendation evidence supports separate assessment of detection and subsequent handling.
FlVspU2igD.evidence: Evaluation of 11 LLMs identifies proactive detection as a bottleneck and underspecified premises as the hardest error category.
FlVspU2igD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard evaluating flawed recommendation premises as a useful extension beyond conventional recommendation accuracy.
FlVspU2igD.main_concern: Reviewers question whether recommendation-specific premise critique differs sufficiently from existing premise-critique and general LLM evaluation benchmarks.

nMfoOlJcm6.one_liner: Coding agents reformat neuroscience datasets while human process rubrics assess scientific correctness beyond successful execution.
nMfoOlJcm6.problem: Fragmented neuroscience formats require interpretation, and executable conversion code can still introduce scientifically significant errors.
nMfoOlJcm6.method: The benchmark supplies agents with datasets, code, and papers to prepare neural-decoding data. Outcome metrics and independent human process ratings compare conversions with manual reference solutions.
nMfoOlJcm6.key_idea: Human-scored conversion decisions complement outcome metrics to detect semantic errors that aggregate statistics and decoder accuracy can miss.
nMfoOlJcm6.evidence: Eight mouse neural-recording papers support evaluations across models, prompts, and agent harnesses with two independent human evaluators.
nMfoOlJcm6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value testing scientifically valid data processing beyond executability and using human assessment to examine failures.
nMfoOlJcm6.main_concern: Reviewers question the reliability of error labels, including low-precision automated judging and conflation of incorrect conversions with defensible reference disagreements.

OGZNUIjBjz.one_liner: Confidence-weighted object measures transfer multimodal detector supervision through teacher locations and unbalanced transport.
OGZNUIjBjz.problem: Different detector architectures complicate feature alignment and teacher-student prediction association in LiDAR distillation.
OGZNUIjBjz.method: OMT-Distill represents decoded boxes and class labels as confidence-weighted object measures. Teacher-location supervision covers omitted responses, while unbalanced transport distributes supervision through many-to-many associations.
OGZNUIjBjz.key_idea: Teacher-location supervision and unbalanced transport align confidence-weighted teacher and student object predictions across heterogeneous detection architectures.
OGZNUIjBjz.evidence: Experiments on nuScenes evaluate four heterogeneous teacher-student pairs, including a CenterPoint-Voxel student, alongside object-interchange diagnostics.
OGZNUIjBjz.claimed_gains: OMT-Distill achieves 61.07 mAP and 67.92 NDS on the nuScenes validation set with a CenterPoint-Voxel student.
OGZNUIjBjz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find decoded objects a sensible common interface and the diagnostic experiments useful for motivating heterogeneous distillation.
OGZNUIjBjz.main_concern: Missing component ablations and simpler matching controls leave the specific contribution of optimal transport unclear.

eWATIpmPOE.one_liner: Cached composed samples and reference-model correction amortize repeated diffusion composition across subsequent samples.
eWATIpmPOE.problem: Existing diffusion-composition methods repeatedly evaluate multiple constituent models for every sample from an unchanged target.
eWATIpmPOE.method: AmCo caches samples and constituent-density information from an existing composition method, then builds importance-weighted clean predictions. A single reference model corrects shared finite-cache error during subsequent sampling.
eWATIpmPOE.key_idea: Importance-weighted cached samples estimate composed clean predictions, while a reference constituent corrects correlated finite-sample errors.
eWATIpmPOE.evidence: Finite-cache estimator analysis and experiments cover one-dimensional composition, classifier-free-guided image generation, and product-of-experts ligand generation.
eWATIpmPOE.claimed_gains: Stage-2 generation uses one constituent-model evaluation per step.
eWATIpmPOE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find amortizing repeated composition well motivated and the reference correction supported by useful estimator analysis.
eWATIpmPOE.main_concern: The practical quality-cost benefit remains uncertain without matched shorter-sampler and reference-only controls that establish the cache's contribution.

KqZWjDn0td.one_liner: Transition consistency matches denoising token log-ratios to changes in a terminal-reward-anchored potential during diffusion-language-model reinforcement learning.
KqZWjDn0td.problem: Existing diffusion-language-model RL objectives can ignore differences in reward contribution across intermediate denoising states.
KqZWjDn0td.method: PACT jointly learns a policy and scalar state potential anchored by terminal rewards. Each transition matches revealed-token policy-to-reference log-probability ratios to potential changes without sequence-likelihood estimation or ratio clipping.
KqZWjDn0td.key_idea: A transition loss equates revealed-token policy-reference log-ratios with differences in a learned reward-anchored state potential.
KqZWjDn0td.evidence: Experiments fine-tune LLaDA-8B-Instruct on GSM8K, MATH500, Countdown, and Sudoku.
KqZWjDn0td.claimed_gains: PACT improves LLaDA-8B-Instruct by +9.9 points on GSM8K, +12.0 on MATH500, +55.7 on Countdown, and +72.6 on Sudoku.
KqZWjDn0td.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize empirical gains and a practical way to train on intermediate denoising transitions without response-level likelihood estimation.
KqZWjDn0td.main_concern: Best-test-checkpoint selection and insufficiently matched baseline settings weaken confidence in the comparative results.

76I5tYcfGA.one_liner: Optimal-transport coupling of data and velocity pairs simplifies both levels of hierarchical flow matching.
76I5tYcfGA.problem: Hierarchical rectified flow can preserve difficult multimodal distributions at each level, making nested integration expensive.
76I5tYcfGA.method: The method applies mini-batch optimal transport to data pairs and velocity pairs. These couplings concentrate velocity and acceleration distributions while straightening outer and inner trajectories.
76I5tYcfGA.key_idea: Coupling data endpoints simplifies outer velocities, while coupling velocity endpoints simplifies inner accelerations in nested flow matching.
76I5tYcfGA.evidence: Theoretical distribution-simplification results accompany experiments on synthetic data, MNIST, CIFAR-10, CelebA-HQ 256, and ImageNet 256.
76I5tYcfGA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the motivated coupling construction, theoretical analysis, and image-scale evidence of improved hierarchical flow generation.
76I5tYcfGA.main_concern: The incremental benefit of velocity coupling remains unclear relative to prior data coupling and second-stage training without velocity optimal transport.

jVPV7ITCFG.one_liner: Learned anchor retrieval and a bilinear conditional flow extrapolate multimodal visuomotor action distributions to unseen goals.
jVPV7ITCFG.problem: Goal-conditioned imitation policies often fail outside demonstration support or lose multimodal behavior when extrapolating.
jVPV7ITCFG.method: BFP decomposes an unseen observation-goal pair into a retrieved training anchor and a residual using pretrained visual features and learned anchor selection. A bilinear conditional flow models their joint effect on actions.
jVPV7ITCFG.key_idea: A learned training anchor and observation-goal residual interact through a bilinear flow field that predicts multimodal actions.
jVPV7ITCFG.evidence: A distributional-error bound, simulated manipulation evaluations, and two real-robot tasks support the approach.
jVPV7ITCFG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the extrapolation problem well motivated and recognize empirical benefits from combining retrieval with generative action prediction.
jVPV7ITCFG.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the bilinear interaction from changes in retrieval and conditioning inputs.

AVXqDYsi04.one_liner: Tail-guided rotations, lattice quantization, and fixed-step action-field reuse reduce vision-language-action head precision and evaluation frequency.
AVXqDYsi04.problem: Repeated action-head execution creates heavy weight traffic, while scalar two-bit quantization can destroy task success.
AVXqDYsi04.method: CRAFT selects rotations from original weight-tail statistics and quantizes action heads with lattice codewords to W2A4. Fixed-step caching reuses the last field prediction while continuing solver updates.
AVXqDYsi04.key_idea: Selective weight rotation and lattice quantization combine with fixed-step field reuse to skip repeated action-head evaluations.
AVXqDYsi04.evidence: Evaluations cover eight VLA models, simulation benchmarks, multiple hardware platforms, and ablations of quantization, rotation, and caching.
AVXqDYsi04.claimed_gains: With a W4 backbone, W2A4 head, and caching, LIBERO-Object success is 98.4% and 97.8% on GR00T N1.5 and π0.5, while batch-1 RTX 3090 speedups reach 1.88× and 2.36× using W4A8-backbone kernels.
AVXqDYsi04.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the action-head efficiency motivation and analyses of low-bit errors, rotation, and caching.
AVXqDYsi04.main_concern: Severe success-rate degradation on π0 and CogACT raises concerns about applicability across VLA architectures.

RgSqH9x5CK.one_liner: Action-supervised future visual latents and temporal force feedback guide humanoid bimanual manipulation.
RgSqH9x5CK.problem: World action models emphasize future prediction without explicitly ensuring that predicted representations support contact-rich action generation.
RgSqH9x5CK.method: PHI learns compact action-relevant representations from privileged future observations, then predicts them from current context at deployment. A temporal force encoder adds recent contact dynamics to action generation.
RgSqH9x5CK.key_idea: A hierarchy predicts action-shaped future visual latents and combines them with encoded force histories to condition actions.
RgSqH9x5CK.evidence: Evaluation uses five real-world humanoid bimanual manipulation tasks, including tests with unseen objects and visual distractors.
RgSqH9x5CK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find action-relevant future prediction well motivated and appreciate the real-robot evaluation.
RgSqH9x5CK.main_concern: The experiments do not establish selective prediction's benefit over nonselective or reconstruction-based future representations.

Q5ysCw1VT2.one_liner: Centered within-trajectory molecular scores supplement global trajectory advantages to assign turn-specific reinforcement-learning credit.
Q5ysCw1VT2.problem: Outcome-level reinforcement learning gives every molecular refinement turn the same advantage despite differences in molecular quality.
Q5ysCw1VT2.method: L2E compares cumulative scores across trajectories sharing initial molecules and objectives, then adds weighted, centered within-trajectory score advantages. Centering preserves the global advantage as the mean turn advantage.
Q5ysCw1VT2.key_idea: A centered local molecular-score advantage modifies each turn's credit while preserving the trajectory-level mean advantage.
Q5ysCw1VT2.evidence: Gradient analysis and experiments on S2-Bench and MuMOInstruct assess molecular optimization, unseen instructions, and additional refinement turns.
Q5ysCw1VT2.claimed_gains: On S2-Bench, molar refractivity improves in 69.7% of cases versus 45.3% for the strongest outcome-level RL baseline, with mean relative improvement reaching 1.66×RLOO’s.
Q5ysCw1VT2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the local-global credit rule simple, clearly motivated, and supported by theoretical analysis.
Q5ysCw1VT2.main_concern: The added benefit of local credit is smaller and less consistent than headline comparisons suggest, especially across objectives and stronger baseline settings.

y0eBW6eigt.one_liner: Pooling options across shared-context questions creates harder multiple-choice evaluations and enables exact abstention scoring by answer deletion.
y0eBW6eigt.problem: Small per-question option sets can reward elimination and make benchmarks appear saturated without requiring answer recognition.
y0eBW6eigt.method: AnswerPool merges the options of questions sharing a context and asks models to assign each question its answer using existing labels. Deleting correct options from the shared pool provides an exactly scored abstention test.
y0eBW6eigt.key_idea: Replace separate answer lists with a shared option pool for co-context questions and delete answers to test abstention.
y0eBW6eigt.evidence: Experiments cover eight text, image, and video benchmarks and eighteen models, including comparisons with MMLU-Pro-style added options.
y0eBW6eigt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the format change simple and useful for reusing existing benchmarks without additional labels, with broad multimodal evaluation.
y0eBW6eigt.main_concern: The accuracy drop does not isolate elimination credit from added candidate load, joint matching, and unfamiliar-format demands.

SZkRt9HWBw.one_liner: Joint audio-MIDI latent flow modeling supports music generation, transcription, separation, rendering, and editing within one model.
SZkRt9HWBw.problem: Separate symbolic and audio music models do not reflect workflows that move between notes, arrangement, timbre, and texture.
SZkRt9HWBw.method: MuseDuo fine-tunes a pretrained music DiT into a joint audio-MIDI latent rectified-flow model with a MIDI-VAE and on-the-fly MIDI extraction. Inference-time choices of inputs, outputs, and conditioning support multiple tasks across mixes and instrument stems.
SZkRt9HWBw.key_idea: Jointly model audio and MIDI latents while varying modality noise levels and conditioning to realize different music tasks.
SZkRt9HWBw.evidence: Evaluation spans 10 music tasks and comparisons with 15 recent task-specific baselines, including transcription, source separation, rendering, and note-level editing.
SZkRt9HWBw.claimed_gains: MuseDuo matches or outperforms 15 recent task-specific baselines on the majority of evaluated tasks and metrics.
SZkRt9HWBw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a single checkpoint that handles a broad range of audio and symbolic music tasks with competitive results.
SZkRt9HWBw.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate whether joint MIDI modeling itself causes the reported improvements in audio tasks.

IkXey9R7vp.one_liner: Self-derived feature memories provide attraction-repulsion feedback for training one-step generative flows without an external correction model.
IkXey9R7vp.problem: Trajectory supervision can leave generated endpoints mismatched with the data distribution, while correction methods often depend on separate teachers or encoders.
