IkXey9R7vp.method: Self-Drift combines local transport and fixed-clean-endpoint prediction with distribution correction in the flow's own representations and class-conditional memories. A frozen-lens semi-gradient and capped whitening stabilize training without changing one-step inference.
IkXey9R7vp.key_idea: Apply detached attraction-repulsion targets through predicted endpoints using the flow's own whitened feature space and class-conditional memory.
IkXey9R7vp.evidence: Reviewers report one-step generation comparisons across four model sizes, trajectory-only baselines, and ablations of the training design.
IkXey9R7vp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize strong one-step generation results using internal representations without a separate pretrained correction model.
IkXey9R7vp.main_concern: Matched comparisons are insufficient to isolate the proposed trajectory formulation from existing flow or consistency training with similar drift losses.

WWYo0uvBHk.one_liner: Linear projections rank Gaussian noise candidates to approximate reward-guided diffusion selection without evaluating every candidate neurally.
WWYo0uvBHk.problem: Candidate selection requires many neural evaluations, while mean-shift guidance uses only a single reward-gradient direction.
WWYo0uvBHk.method: Linear Noise Ranking scores Gaussian noise candidates through inner products with a local reward direction. The paper unifies selection and mean shift through the distribution of directional strength and proposes corrected directions and least-squares slopes for non-differentiable rewards.
WWYo0uvBHk.key_idea: Rank candidate Gaussian noises by their inner product with an estimated reward-improving direction instead of evaluating each candidate's reward.
WWYo0uvBHk.evidence: Local asymptotic predictions are checked on MNIST, with image-generation experiments comparing reward-time tradeoffs and guidance variants.
WWYo0uvBHk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the inexpensive noise-ranking idea and its clear local theoretical connection to mean-shift guidance.
WWYo0uvBHk.main_concern: The single-winner local analysis does not cover the aggregation and direction corrections responsible for the strongest practical results.

fsFSEB5qDW.one_liner: A flow pose prior combines with Cauchy reprojection and Gauss–Newton corrections for occlusion-tolerant multiview triangulation.
fsFSEB5qDW.problem: Occluded detections undermine markerless 3D pose reconstruction, while long behavioral recordings demand efficient inference.
fsFSEB5qDW.method: GenTri combines multiview geometry with a flow-matching pose prior at inference time. It replaces squared reprojection error with a redescending Cauchy objective and uses geometry-aware Gauss–Newton guidance to determine correction direction and magnitude.
fsFSEB5qDW.key_idea: Guide a flow-matching pose prior using Cauchy-robust multiview reprojection corrections computed with Gauss–Newton geometry.
fsFSEB5qDW.evidence: Evaluations include three mouse datasets under synthetic occlusion, claimed real-occlusion reconstruction, and extensions to human pose benchmarks.
fsFSEB5qDW.claimed_gains: GenTri matches its first-order variant with 2× (mouse) to 17× (human) less guidance time and reduces mean MPJPE by approximately 25% relative to RANSAC across three mouse datasets under synthetic occlusion.
fsFSEB5qDW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful occlusion results and efficient guidance across detectors with a shared configuration.
fsFSEB5qDW.main_concern: Synthetic occlusion benchmarks and dependence on clean pose priors leave practical performance on naturally occluded datasets insufficiently established.

zPzPgtZfOW.one_liner: High-dimensional logit analysis separates signal alignment, context noise, and parameter-estimation noise in in-context binary classification.
zPzPgtZfOW.problem: Calibration and the distinct noise sources affecting in-context classification lack a quantitative account in simple attention models.
zPzPgtZfOW.method: The paper derives an asymptotic joint law for model and teacher logits in linear attention trained with logistic loss. It uses this law to analyze probability calibration, data scaling, separability, and sensitivity to context length and regularization.
zPzPgtZfOW.key_idea: Characterize the joint model-teacher logit distribution to separate alignment, context noise, and anisotropic estimation noise.
zPzPgtZfOW.evidence: Finite-dimensional simulations and trained linear-attention models support predictions, while standard softmax-attention experiments show qualitatively related behavior.
zPzPgtZfOW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a technically detailed high-dimensional account of in-context classification and calibration.
zPzPgtZfOW.main_concern: Heuristic approximations and unproved assumptions leave the mathematical status of the theoretical predictions insufficiently clear.

UUfeq4Fj92.one_liner: A multimodal backbone generates descriptions, learns under reasoning instructions, and mines its own negatives for single-vector retrieval.
UUfeq4Fj92.problem: Task-specific multimodal retrieval data are scarce, and existing training pipelines often require external teachers or annotation models.
UUfeq4Fj92.method: The framework uses the backbone to enrich image documents with descriptions and trains embeddings contrastively under reasoning-oriented instructions. The resulting retriever mines highly ranked non-relevant documents as hard negatives for refinement without extra reasoning tokens at inference.
UUfeq4Fj92.key_idea: Bootstrap retrieval training from self-generated image descriptions, reasoning-conditioned contrastive learning, and self-mined hard negatives.
UUfeq4Fj92.evidence: Experiments evaluate Qwen3-VL-Instruct and VLM2Vec-V2 across retrieval tasks, including EDIS-Noisy and WebQA-Noisy, with component and instruction ablations.
UUfeq4Fj92.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reuse of backbone capabilities and single-vector retrieval without explicit inference-time reasoning generation.
UUfeq4Fj92.main_concern: Retrieval improvements from reasoning instructions do not establish that the model internalizes reasoning-specific computation.

pfCcN78V45.one_liner: Interpolated conditional velocity fields generate textured 3D morphing trajectories directly from shared Gaussian noise.
pfCcN78V45.problem: Existing textured 3D morphing can require internal feature manipulation or costly inversion and still produce abrupt transitions.
pfCcN78V45.method: FlowMorpher interpolates conditional velocity predictions from pretrained image-to-3D flow models at shared states. Sampling starts from shared Gaussian noise, avoiding inversion and internal attention changes; a regularity analysis establishes terminal-latent continuity with respect to the morphing weight.
pfCcN78V45.key_idea: Start from shared noise and interpolate conditional velocity predictions during sampling to construct intermediate textured 3D objects.
pfCcN78V45.evidence: MorphEdit3D evaluates color, shape, and semantic changes, alongside conditional Lipschitz-continuity analysis and qualitative comparisons with training-free methods.
pfCcN78V45.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, clearly presented, and compatible with existing flow-based 3D generators.
pfCcN78V45.main_concern: The contribution needs clearer positioning and comparisons against existing condition composition and simpler interpolation baselines.

ZBSCfEJm3a.one_liner: History-based error estimates coordinate classifier-free guidance branch refresh and reuse during image-to-3D generation.
ZBSCfEJm3a.problem: Evaluating both classifier-free guidance branches at every denoising step is expensive, and their reuse errors can interact.
ZBSCfEJm3a.method: CodaCache estimates conditional reuse and unconditional omission effects from completed denoising history using latent motion and time separation. Before current evaluation, it selects full guidance, conditional-only refresh, or conditional-only reuse without extra denoiser calls.
ZBSCfEJm3a.key_idea: Use completed trajectory history to estimate branch omission and reuse errors and choose the next classifier-free guidance computation.
ZBSCfEJm3a.evidence: Experiments use TRELLIS.2 and Hunyuan3D 2.1 on Toys4K and an Objaverse-XL subset, with branch diagnostics and scheduling ablations.
ZBSCfEJm3a.claimed_gains: CodaCache uses 37.6-44.7% of Full-CFG denoising FLOPs and achieves 2.34-2.73× end-to-end speedup excluding offline calibration, with mean Chamfer distance increasing by at most 0.15% across valid outputs.
ZBSCfEJm3a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize substantial acceleration with average geometric quality close to full guidance and useful multi-backbone evaluation.
ZBSCfEJm3a.main_concern: The heuristic history-based error scores lack sufficient justification for modeling branch interactions and controlling accumulated geometric error.

7Nyat4nsqh.one_liner: A shared latent-reasoning framework separates representation constraints from supervision and motivates adaptive curriculum training.
7Nyat4nsqh.problem: Coupled latent representations and training objectives obscure which design choices determine latent chain-of-thought performance.
7Nyat4nsqh.method: LatentGrid systematically varies representation constraints and supervision under a common setup, measuring accuracy, rationale recoverability, alignment, and optimization. Adaptive Curriculum Thinking combines curriculum learning with direct and token-level supervision to support adaptive generation lengths.
7Nyat4nsqh.key_idea: Cross representation constraints with supervision strategies under a common training setup, then combine curriculum learning with token-level grounding.
7Nyat4nsqh.evidence: Experiments include seven basic variants, four arithmetic benchmarks, ProsQA, and Llama- and Qwen-family models, with representation probes and gradient analyses.
7Nyat4nsqh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the shared-protocol comparison and analyses beyond task accuracy for studying latent reasoning choices.
7Nyat4nsqh.main_concern: Coupled changes in grounding, stopping, reconstruction grouping, and budgets prevent clean attribution to individual design choices.

GeVWfM1QxG.one_liner: Frequency-adjusted target gradients and shared-query attention improve item embeddings transferred from next-item pretraining to recommendation.
GeVWfM1QxG.problem: Rare items receive weak embedding supervision, while self-attention makes pretraining gradients overly sensitive to recent interactions.
GeVWfM1QxG.method: Frequency Adjustment strengthens output gradients for infrequent targets, and shared-query cross-attention aggregates history with less reliance on the latest interaction. Both preserve the next-item objective and transfer only the pretrained item embeddings downstream.
GeVWfM1QxG.key_idea: Reweight infrequent positive-target embedding gradients and aggregate histories with a learned shared query during next-item pretraining.
GeVWfM1QxG.evidence: Evaluation covers 11 public datasets, five seeds, deeper encoders, and downstream transfer with frozen item embeddings.
GeVWfM1QxG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the focused frozen-embedding transfer setup and simple interventions tied to gradient analysis.
GeVWfM1QxG.main_concern: Insufficiently specified data boundaries and mostly uniformly sampled negatives limit confidence in the reported relevance to realistic CTR prediction.

S0A2LJyfWl.one_liner: Duration-aware physiological tokens and block-autoregressive translation map peripheral signals into full-night EEG spectrograms.
S0A2LJyfWl.problem: Translating peripheral physiology into EEG requires compact representations that accommodate independent temporal structures without accumulating drift.
S0A2LJyfWl.method: Sleep2Word chunks physiological embeddings and jointly quantizes content and duration into modality-specific wordbooks. A block-autoregressive translator predicts EEG word identities and occurrence-specific duration refinements within fixed-duration blocks.
S0A2LJyfWl.key_idea: Quantize physiological content with duration and translate independently segmented modalities through shared temporal blocks with duration refinement.
S0A2LJyfWl.evidence: Training uses over 20K PSG cases across 8 datasets, with spectrogram reconstruction, sleep staging, arousal detection, survival prediction, and unseen-cohort evaluations.
S0A2LJyfWl.claimed_gains: Sleep2Word compresses full night sequences by up to 69.7%.
S0A2LJyfWl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the peripheral-to-EEG task and the handling of temporal mismatch between independently segmented modalities.
S0A2LJyfWl.main_concern: The practical added value of generated EEG for downstream analysis remains insufficiently established.

uYkUeMCEVC.one_liner: Uses return variation across repeated imagined rollouts of the actor's policy to scale exploration and gate plan acceptance.
uYkUeMCEVC.problem: World-model agents must decide which alternative action sequences to explore in imagination and when an imagined plan should override the learned actor policy without relying on expensive ensembles.
uYkUeMCEVC.method: Sibling Disagreement in Imagination (SDI) performs repeated imagined rollouts of the actor's own action sequence from the same model state to measure baseline return variation. This shared actor-based reference scales candidate return spread for intrinsic exploration and gates decision-time planning during training data collection, while evaluation uses the learned actor alone.
uYkUeMCEVC.key_idea: Measures return variability across repeated imagined rollouts of the actor's own action sequence to normalize exploration spread and threshold plan acceptance.
uYkUeMCEVC.evidence: Evaluated across 18 continuous visual control tasks in Meta-World, Adroit, and DM-Control.
uYkUeMCEVC.claimed_gains: Across Meta-World, Adroit, and DM-Control, SDI achieves the highest average score in every suite and is competitive with or better than all baselines on 16 of 18 tasks.
uYkUeMCEVC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the ensemble-free unified reference mechanism connecting exploration and plan gating during data collection while keeping evaluation strictly actor-only.
uYkUeMCEVC.main_concern: The paper omits seed counts, standard deviations, and confidence intervals across training runs, as well as computational overhead analysis and matched-acceptance-rate gating ablations.

qHXju2NexN.one_liner: Analyzes how varying the fraction of loss-supervised suffix tokens steers Transformers toward MLP- or attention-dominated reasoning circuits.
qHXju2NexN.problem: Token-level supervision density is typically treated merely as a training efficiency choice rather than a factor that alters learned reasoning mechanisms and long-context generalization.
qHXju2NexN.method: The authors train 12-layer Transformers on a controlled multi-hop variable-binding task while varying the fraction of suffix tokens contributing to the loss from all-token prediction to last-token supervision. They evaluate convergence speed and generalization to longer contexts and deeper reasoning chains, and perform mechanistic analyses of the MLP and attention pathways.
qHXju2NexN.key_idea: Varies the fraction of supervised suffix tokens on a multi-hop variable-binding task to trace how loss density selects between MLP-dominated and attention-dominated circuits.
qHXju2NexN.evidence: Evaluated on 12-layer Transformers trained on a synthetic multi-hop variable-binding benchmark with length and depth extrapolation tests and mechanistic pathway analyses.
qHXju2NexN.claimed_gains: At convergence, sparse 25% supervision yields the strongest long-context generalization, whereas prolonged training eventually makes the last-token model the strongest generalizer.
qHXju2NexN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled investigation of how supervision density shapes training dynamics, length extrapolation, and internal MLP versus attention pathways clear and insightful.
qHXju2NexN.main_concern: Results are reported on a single synthetic task with a 12-layer RoPE Transformer without multiple training seeds or controls isolating supervision density from answer-loss weighting.

dRwh8qm6g9.one_liner: Aligns function-aware protein representations with chemically annotated reaction embeddings using a multi-positive contrastive dual encoder.
dRwh8qm6g9.problem: Existing enzyme-reaction prediction methods often overlook the relationship between active-site features and reaction chemistry and fail to model many-to-many bidirectional associations.
dRwh8qm6g9.method: Chemistry-Informed Reaction-Catalyst Embeddings (CIRCE) is a contrastive dual encoder for bidirectional enzyme-reaction retrieval. It combines function-aware protein representations with reaction embeddings encoding reactants, products, stoichiometry, cofactors, and chemical annotations under a multi-positive alignment objective.
dRwh8qm6g9.key_idea: Trains a bidirectional contrastive dual encoder with a multi-positive alignment loss linking functional-residue protein features to stoichiometry- and cofactor-aware reaction representations.
dRwh8qm6g9.evidence: Evaluated on enzyme screening and bidirectional enzyme-reaction retrieval benchmarks including ReactZyme.
dRwh8qm6g9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling enzyme-reaction compatibility as a many-to-many bidirectional problem combining active-site protein features and reaction chemistry is biologically well motivated.
dRwh8qm6g9.main_concern: Ablations and baseline comparisons do not isolate the individual feature encoders and loss components, and evaluation reliability is weakened by test-set inspection during development and a refit baseline outperforming CIRCE in the appendix.

TZYcwtU6Cb.one_liner: Detects and localizes task-relevant out-of-distribution shifts by projecting data distribution shifts onto model input sensitivity via Stein operators.
TZYcwtU6Cb.problem: Out-of-distribution detectors are typically either purely data-centric, ignoring whether a shift affects the deployed model, or purely model-centric, ignoring the geometry of the input distribution.
TZYcwtU6Cb.method: TASTE (Task-Aware STEin operators) uses a fixed predictor as a test function within a Stein operator to combine the training distribution score with the model's input sensitivity. Its coordinate-wise decomposition enables sample-level detection and pixel-level localization of shifts without retraining the classifier or requiring OOD samples.
TZYcwtU6Cb.key_idea: Applies Stein operators combining the training distribution score function with the deployed predictor's input derivatives to project distribution shift onto model sensitivity.
TZYcwtU6Cb.evidence: Evaluated with theoretical guarantees and experiments on controlled Gaussian shifts, MNIST under geometric perturbations, and perturbed CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K benchmarks.
TZYcwtU6Cb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the mathematical formulation linking input distribution geometry with predictor sensitivity via Stein operators and its coordinate-wise decomposition for local diagnostics.
TZYcwtU6Cb.main_concern: Input sensitivity does not directly guarantee task error degradation on realistic datasets beyond toy setups, and the paper under-discusses prior task-aware OOD detection literature while exhibiting table inconsistencies.

71aW30lVpo.one_liner: Jailbreaks aligned LLMs at inference time by flipping 5 to 25 targeted parameter bits in memory via Rowhammer.
71aW30lVpo.problem: Aligned large language models are assumed to maintain safety constraints unless manipulated by adversarial prompts or extensive parameter fine-tuning.
71aW30lVpo.method: PrisonBreak uses an efficient bit-selection algorithm to identify critical parameter bits whose flipping removes safety alignment while preserving general model utility. The authors pair this search with an end-to-end Rowhammer fault-injection exploit on physical GDDR6 GPU memory to alter weights in memory at inference time without modifying inputs.
71aW30lVpo.key_idea: Identifies and flips 5–25 high-impact parameter bits in GPU memory via Rowhammer fault injection to disable LLM refusal behavior without input prompts.
71aW30lVpo.evidence: Evaluated across 10 LLMs in simulation and 5 models via physical Rowhammer fault injection on a GDDR6 GPU, plus transferability and countermeasure tests.
71aW30lVpo.claimed_gains: Jailbreaks billion-parameter LLMs with 5–25 bit-flips (up to 40x fewer than prior bit-flip attacks) and identifies critical bits up to 20x faster, achieving 80–98% ASR across 10 LLMs and 69–91% ASR on 5 models via GDDR6 GPU Rowhammer using two physical bit locations.
71aW30lVpo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers highlight the compelling demonstration of an input-agnostic jailbreak requiring very few bit-flips and validated end-to-end with physical GPU Rowhammer attacks.
71aW30lVpo.main_concern: The claim of negligible utility loss overlooks notable accuracy drops on reasoning benchmarks like GSM8K (over 11–12 percentage points on some models), and simple runtime checksums or ECC memory limit real-world practicality.

2L04XFPBON.one_liner: Combines diffusion reconstruction error with the leading sensitivity spectrum of intermediate denoising features for unsupervised OOD detection.
2L04XFPBON.problem: Diffusion-based out-of-distribution detectors relying solely on reconstruction error fail when OOD inputs are reconstructed as accurately as in-distribution inputs.
2L04XFPBON.method: DUO (DUal-readout of diffusion models for OOD detection) extracts a complementary signal from a frozen diffusion model by perturbing the input and computing the leading sensitivity spectrum of intermediate denoising features. It standardizes and fuses this feature sensitivity score with reconstruction error for training-free OOD detection.
2L04XFPBON.key_idea: Fuses diffusion reconstruction error with the leading spectral sensitivity of intermediate denoising features under input perturbations.
2L04XFPBON.evidence: Supported by theoretical analysis on a Bayes denoiser and unsupervised OOD detection experiments primarily on 32x32 image benchmarks, plus FFHQ-256 and ImageNet-64 in the appendix.
2L04XFPBON.claimed_gains: DUO improves average AUROC by approximately 6% points over the strongest baselines while substantially reducing inference cost.
2L04XFPBON.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the dual-readout pipeline intuitive, clear, and computationally cheaper at inference than prior diffusion-based OOD detectors.
2L04XFPBON.main_concern: The intermediate-feature spectral score closely resembles EigenScore moved to an internal layer without a clear theoretical justification beyond a simplified Bayes denoiser, and experiments lack standard high-resolution ImageNet-1K OpenOOD benchmarks and FPR@95 metrics.

sduUdYxp5q.one_liner: Links visually grounded observations of the same physical instance across long videos into retrievable entity biographies for QA.
sduUdYxp5q.problem: Chronological text descriptions in long-video memory systems leave physical object identities unresolved across clips, failing to connect events involving the same specific entity over hours or days.
sduUdYxp5q.method: Grounded Entity Biographies (GEB) associates visually grounded observations of each physical instance across video clips into persistent, retrievable entity biographies while retaining local episodic context. At query time, the system retrieves relevant entity biographies alongside episodic evidence to answer long-horizon questions.
sduUdYxp5q.key_idea: Groups visually grounded cross-clip observations of identical physical instances into persistent entity biographies retrieved alongside episodic memory during question answering.
sduUdYxp5q.evidence: Evaluated across four long-video question-answering benchmarks including day-long and week-long recordings such as EgoLifeQA and MultiHop-EgoQA.
sduUdYxp5q.claimed_gains: On EgoLifeQA, GEB achieves 72.0% accuracy, 4.4 percentage points above the best published result.
sduUdYxp5q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that organizing long-video memory around persistent physical entity instances addresses a clear limitation of text-only chronological video memories and improves QA accuracy.
sduUdYxp5q.main_concern: The core cross-clip physical identity association mechanism is not directly evaluated for precision or recall, relies on recording-specific manually calibrated thresholds, and uses a larger memory footprint than baselines.

GFQstEABV5.one_liner: Recenter frozen source classifier geometry to define fixed per-class axes and ideal points for batch-size-one test-time adaptation.
GFQstEABV5.problem: Test-time adaptation with a batch size of one lacks reliable batch statistics and suffers from self-reinforcement and collapse when adapting on confident but misclassified samples.
GFQstEABV5.method: Origin-recentered Test-Time Adaptation (OriTTA) shifts the feature-space origin near the mean of synthetic class prototypes so class directions spread evenly, defining a fixed axis and ideal point for each class prior to deployment. During single-sample adaptation, it aligns features with their predicted class axis while penalizing excessive radius, retains one sample per class in memory to constrain absent classes, and resets the model if re-classifying memory indicates collapse.
GFQstEABV5.key_idea: Recenter the feature origin using synthetic prototypes to create fixed class axes and target points for single-sample feature alignment with memory-based collapse detection.
GFQstEABV5.evidence: Evaluated on batch-size-one test-time adaptation across corruption benchmarks including CIFAR-C and ImageNet-C.
GFQstEABV5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the geometric motivation and collapse detection mechanism well-motivated for addressing the practical challenge of batch-size-one test-time adaptation.
GFQstEABV5.main_concern: Ablations do not cleanly separate the novel origin-recentering geometry from established angular alignment and the collapse detector, while reliance on pseudo-labels and global hyperparameters remains.

0oIMOXDhIk.one_liner: Breaks deterministic cold-start traps in frozen in-context RL models by executing one random exploratory episode as context.
0oIMOXDhIk.problem: Frozen pretrained in-context reinforcement learning models acting deterministically from an empty context often repeat an uninformative default first episode and get trapped in suboptimal behavior.
0oIMOXDhIk.method: The authors diagnose this self-context trap via context-swap and reward-relabeling experiments across seven methods and ten task families. They propose exploratory prompting, which executes one random episode at the start and retains it as the prompt only if the resulting return is at least that induced by the agent's own first episode.
0oIMOXDhIk.key_idea: Runs one random initial episode and retains it as context if its induced return matches or exceeds the agent's deterministic first episode.
0oIMOXDhIk.evidence: Evaluated across seven in-context RL methods (including AD and DPT lineages) on ten task families such as HalfCheetah-Vel with context-swap, reward-relabeling, and seed controls.
0oIMOXDhIk.claimed_gains: Without retraining or demonstrations, exploratory prompting frees most stuck trials on the analyzed task family in four methods and raises the mean final return in 34 of 40 (family, method) pairs.
0oIMOXDhIk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled context-swap and reward-relabeling diagnosis demonstrating that frozen in-context RL models can use external task information even when trapped by their own deterministic rollouts.
0oIMOXDhIk.main_concern: The exploratory prompting selection rules were designed and chosen after inspecting the same held-out tasks used for the main evaluation, and the random episode reduces cumulative return across all episodes.

lXydTXvQLW.one_liner: Combines an analytically re-balanced autoencoder with a fairness-aware contrastive loss to prevent minority gradient dilution and dimensional collapse.
lXydTXvQLW.problem: Fair anomaly detection under severe group imbalance suffers from a trade-off between accuracy and fairness because standard regularizers dilute protected-group gradients and induce representation dimensional collapse.
lXydTXvQLW.method: FADIG pairs an adaptively re-balanced autoencoder with a fairness-aware contrastive objective for unsupervised anomaly detection. The re-balancing removes the dependence of group gradient contributions on the group imbalance ratio, while the contrastive objective prevents collapsed representations.
lXydTXvQLW.key_idea: Pairs analytical group-imbalance reweighting in an autoencoder with a fairness-aware contrastive objective to preserve protected-group gradients and prevent dimensional collapse.
lXydTXvQLW.evidence: Supported by theoretical gradient and representation analyses and empirical evaluations on four image and tabular anomaly detection datasets.
lXydTXvQLW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that fair anomaly detection under group imbalance is a practical problem and find the two-term autoencoder design simple, hyperparameter-light, and empirically effective.
lXydTXvQLW.main_concern: Two reviewers identified mathematical errors in the theoretical proofs, specifically an invalid deduction bounding the expectation of a ratio of gradient norms by the ratio of their expectations in Lemma 3.3.

WY4KFb90vB.one_liner: Trains a neural network unsupervised via perturbed pricing solves to predict self-consistent dual prices that accelerate column generation.
WY4KFb90vB.problem: Primal degeneracy in the restricted master problem during column generation causes repeated costly pricing subproblems that shift dual prices without improving the primal objective.
WY4KFb90vB.method: The authors propose an unsupervised learning framework that trains a neural network to predict self-consistent dual prices (SCDP) whose displacement from the current restricted master problem dual matches the ascent step induced by their own pricing responses. Using a proximal loss derived from the smoothed full-dual objective, the network is trained with unbiased gradient estimates from a single perturbed pricing solve per iteration while exact pricing at deployment preserves LP optimality.
WY4KFb90vB.key_idea: Minimizes a proximal smoothed full-dual loss using gradients from perturbed pricing subproblem responses to predict self-consistent dual prices without optimal-price labels.
WY4KFb90vB.evidence: Supported by theoretical ascent guarantees on the smoothed full-dual bound and experiments on three combinatorial optimization problems including CVRP and CVRPTW.
WY4KFb90vB.claimed_gains: Experiments demonstrate runtime reductions of 63%, 94%, and 47% on the evaluated routing and column generation benchmarks.
WY4KFb90vB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-motivated effort to mitigate column generation degeneracy using an unsupervised self-consistency loss that avoids precomputing optimal dual labels.
WY4KFb90vB.main_concern: The experimental choice of the upper bound parameter U on total column weight in CVRP/CVRPTW appears to use a lower bound on vehicle count, potentially violating the theoretical assumptions underlying the dual bound.

2XBkpFL2mp.one_liner: Identifies vulnerable collaborative subgraphs in multi-agent LLM systems and adapts adversarial attacks into structure-aware coordinated behaviors.
2XBkpFL2mp.problem: Collaborative communication structures in LLM-based multi-agent systems can amplify adversarial influence when malicious agents coordinate, depending on the topology.
2XBkpFL2mp.method: The authors analyze how internal attacker-to-attacker density and outward attacker-to-normal connections amplify attacks, formulating Collaboration-Induced Vulnerability (CIV). They build CIV-Amplify, a graph-based red-teaming framework that uses a learned risk predictor to select vulnerable collaborative subgraphs and an LLM planner to adapt existing attacks into structure-conditioned coordinated behaviors.
2XBkpFL2mp.key_idea: Predicts subgraph vulnerability from internal attacker coordination and outward propagation links, then plans role- and structure-conditioned collaborative attacks.
2XBkpFL2mp.evidence: Evaluated across four victim LLM backbones, four communication topologies, and three attack families, plus safeguard evaluations.
2XBkpFL2mp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distinction between internal attacker coordination and outward propagation useful and appreciate the broad evaluation across multiple topologies, backbones, and attack types.
2XBkpFL2mp.main_concern: Experiments lack comparisons against existing collaborative multi-agent attack baselines such as MAStrike, and ablations do not isolate structure-conditioned planning or within-graph predictor ranking accuracy.

7dkP0o1Z7e.one_liner: Models multi-agent collaboration as a hypergraph and distills recurring successful sub-hypergraphs into compact reusable skills.
7dkP0o1Z7e.problem: Existing adaptive multi-agent LLM systems re-execute explicit multi-agent communication from scratch on every query, causing redundant token consumption on recurring coordination routines.
7dkP0o1Z7e.method: HyperMAS represents functional roles as role-level mixture nodes over heterogeneous LLMs and coordinates multi-role interactions via high-order hyperedges. During training, it identifies reliable and cost-effective sub-hypergraphs from execution traces and distills them into compact skills; at inference, a verifier invokes compact skills for familiar routines and falls back to explicit hypergraph communication for uncertain cases.
7dkP0o1Z7e.key_idea: Distills validated multi-agent sub-hypergraph execution traces into single-call collaborative skills and uses a verifier at inference to switch between skills and explicit hypergraph communication.
7dkP0o1Z7e.evidence: Evaluated across mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks (including HumanEval) with cost, break-even, and component ablation analyses.
7dkP0o1Z7e.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distilling repeated multi-agent coordination trajectories into reusable skills with a verifier fallback is a practical way to reduce token costs on recurring workloads.
7dkP0o1Z7e.main_concern: The train/test split and skill-distillation data sources are insufficiently specified to rule out task overlap, and distilled skills execute as a single prompt without demonstrating a clear advantage of hypergraphs over standard graphs.

Dg2V9jzHe8.one_liner: Accelerates distilled causal video diffusion models training-free via step reduction, KV-cache windowing, clean-cache refinement, and runtime kernel optimizations.
Dg2V9jzHe8.problem: Few-step causal video diffusion models distilled from bidirectional teachers remain too slow for real-time streaming video generation.
Dg2V9jzHe8.method: UnStep is a training-free inference wrapper that runs distilled causal video diffusion transformers with fewer denoising steps than used during distillation and restricts the temporal attention KV-cache window. To recover generation quality, it renoises latent frames to a near-clean level to refine them during the existing clean-cache pass and applies truncated SVD to attention value and output projections, paired with fused Triton kernels and VAE runtime optimizations.
Dg2V9jzHe8.key_idea: Combines sub-distillation step reduction and KV-cache windowing with zero-extra-call clean-cache renoising refinement, truncated SVD projections, and kernel optimizations.
Dg2V9jzHe8.evidence: Evaluated on Wan2.1-1.3B-based causal video diffusion checkpoints (including Self-Forcing, Causal Forcing, and LongLive) using VBench on single and multiple H100 GPUs.
Dg2V9jzHe8.claimed_gains: UnStep reaches 50 FPS on a single H100 without quality loss and 77 FPS on multi-GPU setups.
Dg2V9jzHe8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the step-by-step cumulative ablation showing ~3x throughput gains and highlight the clever reuse of the clean-cache pass to refine quality without adding a DiT call.
Dg2V9jzHe8.main_concern: All experiments use a single Wan2.1-1.3B architecture where aggregate VBench scores mask drops in dynamic motion, and much of the speedup stems from systems engineering rather than validated across diverse backbones.

LikZL3qFXd.one_liner: Conditions diffusion robot policies explicitly on physical observation and action timestamps using continuous time-aware rotary position embeddings.
LikZL3qFXd.problem: Standard robot policies assume fixed-rate observation-action sequences, causing performance degradation when sensing rates, delays, or inference latencies vary.
LikZL3qFXd.method: Chronos Policy encodes physical observation capture times and target action execution times directly into a diffusion transformer via time-aware RoPE, while temporally randomizing sampled observations and action chunk start times during training. This allows attention weights to depend directly on physical time intervals and enables learning from asynchronous, multi-rate sensors.
LikZL3qFXd.key_idea: Applies continuous physical-time RoPE to observation and action tokens paired with training-time temporal schedule randomization.
LikZL3qFXd.evidence: Evaluated in simulation and real-world robotic manipulation experiments across quasi-static, dynamic (Pivoting, Conveyor), and multisensory tasks against Diffusion Policy and additive-timestamp controls.
LikZL3qFXd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the 2x2 ablations clean and convincing, showing that pairing explicit physical timestamps via RoPE with temporal randomization substantially improves robustness on dynamic and delayed tasks.
LikZL3qFXd.main_concern: Continuous-time RoPE and delay conditioning closely build on prior work, and the experiments omit critical baselines such as Delay-Aware Diffusion Policy, latency-matched chunk dropping, and timestamp resampling onto a nominal grid.

lIulRQEOUe.one_liner: Computes a shared permutation-invariant edge interaction representation that each endpoint scales with its own node embedding.
lIulRQEOUe.problem: Standard graph neural networks treat edges merely as directional message channels to a receiver rather than shared interactions that yield distinct consequences for each participant across diverse graph types.
lIulRQEOUe.method: Learning from Interaction Consequences (LINC) forms a single order-invariant representation of an interaction from both endpoint nodes of an edge. Each participating node then reads this shared interaction representation through a scale computed from its own embedding, producing two distinct endpoint consequences from one interaction.
lIulRQEOUe.key_idea: Constructs one shared order-invariant interaction representation per edge and modulates it separately at each endpoint using receiver-computed scaling factors.
lIulRQEOUe.evidence: Supported by permutation-invariance proofs and experiments across 16 graph benchmarks covering homophilic, heterophilic, heterogeneous, and directed graphs against 38 baselines.
lIulRQEOUe.claimed_gains: Achieves the best average rank in every group of 16 graphs against 38 baselines.
lIulRQEOUe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shared-interaction perspective intuitive, well written, and broadly effective across 16 diverse graph benchmarks.
lIulRQEOUe.main_concern: The formulation remains a special case of general receiver-conditioned message passing, and appendix ablations show that removing the endpoint-specific scaling slightly improves performance on 10 of the 16 datasets when the direct term is kept.

Vk08hTbBew.one_liner: Generates analytical literature surveys for AI agents using citation-graph retrieval, cross-paper clustering, code-repository inspection, and citation verification.
Vk08hTbBew.problem: Existing automated survey generation systems rely on abstracts and isolated paper processing, resulting in shallow summaries and unreliable citations that hinder downstream research agents.
Vk08hTbBew.method: DeepSurvey expands retrieval via citation graphs with hybrid filtering, extracts full-text structured keynotes, models cross-paper relationships via clustering and comparative tables, and deploys a code-agent subsystem to extract implementation details from repositories. It enforces evidence-constrained writing and multi-granularity agentic refinement to verify citation-claim alignment.
Vk08hTbBew.key_idea: Combines citation-graph retrieval, cross-paper clustering, repository code inspection, and multi-stage claim-citation verification to synthesize deep technical surveys.
Vk08hTbBew.evidence: Evaluated against open-source automated survey baselines and human-written surveys via rubric evaluations, human expert ratings, and a downstream research coding agent task.
Vk08hTbBew.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the comprehensive multi-stage system design, full-text and code-level synthesis, and thorough evaluation including downstream research-agent utility.
Vk08hTbBew.main_concern: Methodological novelty is largely an integration of existing components where the new code agent yields only minor ablation gains, results report best-of-three runs rather than means, and the agent-oriented framing is not isolated from general survey quality.

B2dFK5coye.one_liner: Disaggregates sparse-attention token indexing into a weight-free shared service with paged memory and direct device-to-device communication.
B2dFK5coye.problem: In long-context sparse-attention LLM serving, the token indexer's state grows linearly with sequence length in decoder HBM, exhausting memory at low concurrency and limiting batch size.
B2dFK5coye.method: IndexServe disaggregates index HBM storage and token-selection computation from inference engines into a shared weight-free service pooling multiple decoder instances. It uses direct device-to-device communication with a graph-compatible runtime to minimize critical-path latency, alongside PagedIndex and length-aware dynamic batching for memory allocation and scheduling.
B2dFK5coye.key_idea: Offloads weight-free sparse-attention index storage and top-k selection to a pooled remote service using PagedIndex memory management and graph-compatible device-to-device communication.
B2dFK5coye.evidence: Implemented and evaluated on Ascend A3 superpod hardware across two model families, three workload patterns, and multiple parallelism layouts against vLLM, ECHO, and HiSparse.
B2dFK5coye.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that disaggregating the weight-free sparse-attention indexer solves a real HBM batching bottleneck and is backed by solid systems engineering including PagedIndex and graph-compatible communication.
B2dFK5coye.main_concern: Throughput gains are evaluated at peak throughput without matched latency SLO constraints, selection equivalence is not directly verified on model quality, and the implementation relies on proprietary Ascend Unified Bus primitives with unclear portability to NVIDIA clusters.

HkwFRGvDP3.one_liner: Controlled turn partitions vary request order, initial information, and repetition to test multi-turn evaluation sensitivity.
HkwFRGvDP3.problem: Multi-turn performance and mitigation conclusions may depend on how a fixed request is divided into conversation turns.
HkwFRGvDP3.method: The study preserves final requirements and evaluation checkers while varying turn count, requirement order, opening information, and repetition. It compares model performance and mitigation effects across designs and uses matched single-message controls.
HkwFRGvDP3.key_idea: Hold task requirements and scoring fixed while systematically changing their partition and ordering across conversation turns.
HkwFRGvDP3.evidence: Five open-weight models are evaluated on four sharded-benchmark tasks across 24 conversation designs and four mitigation methods.
HkwFRGvDP3.claimed_gains: The best and worst conversation designs differ by a median of 0.123 on a 0-1 scale.
HkwFRGvDP3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the detailed experimental analysis showing that conversation design changes measured model performance.
HkwFRGvDP3.main_concern: The study's contribution beyond prior work on sharding and conversation configurations is insufficiently distinguished.

MacwI5NteS.one_liner: FedAGP shares group anchors for class-dependent client retrieval and uses anchor usage and update consensus to guide aggregation.
MacwI5NteS.problem: Global prompts miss client specialization, while exchanging personalized prompts ties shared knowledge to individual clients.
MacwI5NteS.method: Clients retain personalized prompts locally and retrieve class-dependent mixtures from shared group anchors. Retrieval weights determine server-side anchor refinement, while consensus with a collective update direction weights global prompt aggregation.
MacwI5NteS.key_idea: Reuse client-anchor relevance for both class-dependent retrieval and server aggregation while keeping personalized prompts local.
MacwI5NteS.evidence: Experiments cover 11 heterogeneous federated benchmarks, including personalization, cross-client transfer, novel-class generalization, and label and domain heterogeneity.
MacwI5NteS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value shared anchors as a mechanism for transferring specialized knowledge while improving the personalization-generalization trade-off.
MacwI5NteS.main_concern: The evidence does not fully isolate anchor sharing from the inference rule that excludes personalized representations for unseen classes.

PMrU91NBMn.one_liner: Weave Forcing routes character and background references separately and exposes masked historical KV tokens for compositional video generation.
PMrU91NBMn.problem: Whole-shot retrieval misses component-specific references, while combining complete historical memories introduces unrelated content into new shots.
PMrU91NBMn.method: An LLM decomposes prompts into semantic slots and selects historical references for each character and background. Contrastive slot attention masks compressed KV memories, while coverage-adaptive RoPE adjusts temporal offsets and memory retention to reference completeness.
PMrU91NBMn.key_idea: Retrieve references per semantic slot and mask historical KV tokens before applying coverage-dependent temporal positioning.
PMrU91NBMn.evidence: Reviews describe generation experiments and component analyses evaluating compositional recall and subject appearance consistency.
PMrU91NBMn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find component-specific memory routing a well-motivated response to compositional recall in multi-shot generation.
PMrU91NBMn.main_concern: Appearance-similarity metrics and limited visual validation do not convincingly establish correct preservation of all requested identities and composition.

TiwQrE48MI.one_liner: Temporal Zoom crops around predicted short moments and reruns a frozen VideoLLM for focused temporal localization.
TiwQrE48MI.problem: Aggregate temporal-grounding metrics hide severe short-event failures caused by duration bias and imprecise event placement.
TiwQrE48MI.method: The study stratifies grounding performance by event length and tests training and input-window interventions. A training-free Temporal Zoom gives a focused second pass only to events the model initially predicts as short.
TiwQrE48MI.key_idea: Use a short-duration first prediction to trigger a cropped second inference pass with the same frozen model.
TiwQrE48MI.evidence: Reviews describe length-stratified evaluation across three model families and three corpora, fine-tuning interventions, and controlled input-cropping experiments.
TiwQrE48MI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing short-moment failures hidden by aggregate scores is valuable and extensively supported.
TiwQrE48MI.main_concern: Cropping jointly changes search range, distractors, and temporal scaling, so the claimed search-space mechanism is not fully isolated.

NTzE7DcPQX.one_liner: Operation-level specialization and local routing consistency regularize MoE expert selection during agentic reinforcement learning.
NTzE7DcPQX.problem: Standard agent reinforcement learning leaves MoE routing unconstrained despite existing specialization across semantically similar operations.
NTzE7DcPQX.method: The framework aligns turn-level expert selection with operation labels and regularizes token-level selections for local consistency. Entropy-gated control addresses instability during post-training without changing the native inference architecture.
NTzE7DcPQX.key_idea: Regularize expert routing at operation and token levels, with entropy gating to control training instability.
NTzE7DcPQX.evidence: Experiments cover two agentic benchmarks and multiple RL algorithms, with ablations on operation labels, routing components, and load balancing.
NTzE7DcPQX.claimed_gains: The framework reports over 10-point improvements in success rate on all evaluated benchmarks.
NTzE7DcPQX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate using agent-operation labels to guide native MoE routing without inference-time architectural changes.
NTzE7DcPQX.main_concern: Inconsistent baseline results across tables make the reported gains and experimental comparisons difficult to verify.

LfJ1wxnyPU.one_liner: Weights from a recurrent transformer trained on procedural data expand into reusable initializations across model widths and depths.
LfJ1wxnyPU.problem: Procedural warm-up must ordinarily repeat its pretraining cost for each target transformer.
LfJ1wxnyPU.method: Procedural Core trains a small recurrent transformer on abstract procedural data, then expands its weights to initialize larger models. Analyses examine recurrence and suppression of high-norm tokens as sources of transfer.
LfJ1wxnyPU.key_idea: Learn shared recurrent weights on procedural data and expand them across the target transformer's width and depth.
LfJ1wxnyPU.evidence: Evaluations cover image classification, DINO, FineWeb-Edu, CodeParrot, and dense visual tasks, with architectural and weight-shuffling ablations.
LfJ1wxnyPU.claimed_gains: A 1M-parameter core initializing an 85M-parameter ViT-Base improves ImageNet top-1 by 2.2pp over standard random initialization, with ImageNet-S mAP 32.3 → 42.9, VOC07 CorLoc 9.9 → 18.4, and NYUv2 RMSE 1.104 → 0.998.
LfJ1wxnyPU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that compact reusable initialization is practically motivated and supported by experiments across tasks and domains.
LfJ1wxnyPU.main_concern: The paper does not adequately quantify training costs and amortized savings relative to direct procedural warm-up.

hwFK3ka2BR.one_liner: Adversarially trained KV-cache transformations suppress reconstruction of sensitive inputs while preserving task information.
hwFK3ka2BR.problem: Sharing KV caches between agents can leak sensitive contextual information beyond what textual-output safeguards inspect.
hwFK3ka2BR.method: LCGuard transforms cache representations before transmission and defines leakage through an adversarial decoder's reconstruction of sensitive inputs. Adversarial training balances task semantics against reconstructable sensitive information.
hwFK3ka2BR.key_idea: Train a cache transformation against a sensitive-input reconstruction adversary while retaining information needed for the shared task.
hwFK3ka2BR.evidence: Evaluations span Qwen, Gemma, and LLaMA models, privacy-oriented benchmarks, and multiple communication topologies.
hwFK3ka2BR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that latent KV communication creates an important privacy risk that output-only evaluations miss.
hwFK3ka2BR.main_concern: Reduced success for the chosen reconstruction attacks does not establish that shared caches no longer contain recoverable sensitive information.

CFgsXaipAm.one_liner: Task-focused extraction and structuring construct context representations for reasoning over document corpora beyond model context limits.
CFgsXaipAm.problem: Ad hoc context representations can omit interdependent information needed to solve tasks across large heterogeneous corpora.
CFgsXaipAm.method: R3Con operationalizes representation-design principles drawn from relevance realization through task-relevant extraction and structuring. It iteratively revisits documents in light of other summaries to construct representations for downstream reasoning.
CFgsXaipAm.key_idea: Extract task-relevant information and structure it into a shared representation, revisiting documents using contextual summaries.
CFgsXaipAm.evidence: Experiments compare nine baselines on CorpusQA and Loong with multiple model sizes and ablations of extraction, structuring, and repeated rounds.
CFgsXaipAm.claimed_gains: R3Con exceeds the strongest baseline by 20 and 8.4 percentage points, while 4B and 9B models outperform all evaluated 35B baselines.
CFgsXaipAm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize substantial same-backbone gains across two benchmarks and practical benefits for smaller models.
CFgsXaipAm.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate the proposed principles, especially iterative reinterpretation, whose additional rounds yield little demonstrated benefit.

dTWXayhVGK.one_liner: Calibration-derived unit representations feed bounded-cache causal attention and drift-conditioned decoding of neural activity.
dTWXayhVGK.problem: Motor decoders must handle changing neural units and nonstationary activity across recording sessions in a causal streaming setting.
dTWXayhVGK.method: R-NDT infers unit context from brief unlabeled calibration through a permutation-equivariant encoder and forms population tokens. A bounded-cache causal transformer uses moving-average state through adaptive layer normalization, while behavior queries decode its latent state through cross-attention.
dTWXayhVGK.key_idea: Infer unit context from calibration activity, then decode population tokens with bounded causal attention conditioned on a moving-average drift state.
dTWXayhVGK.evidence: Public-dataset pretraining and fine-tuning evaluate cross-session, cross-type, cross-subject, and cross-site behavior decoding, including whole-block streaming.
dTWXayhVGK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value flexible handling of neural units and the practically relevant causal streaming architecture.
dTWXayhVGK.main_concern: Missing controlled component ablations leave the contributions of unit inference and drift conditioning insufficiently isolated.

e2wlaA5EdH.one_liner: A six-level video-question taxonomy and separate generation-verification models benchmark cognitive abilities in video MLLMs.
e2wlaA5EdH.problem: Video benchmarks incompletely cover object permanence, episodic-like memory, and higher-level planning.
e2wlaA5EdH.method: CogViD organizes video questions into six cognition-inspired levels and 58 subtasks, including multiple-choice and open-ended formats. Level-specific templates guide model-generated annotation, separate models verify it, and filtering precedes human review.
e2wlaA5EdH.key_idea: Generate questions from level-specific cognitive templates, verify them with separate models, and evaluate video models across the resulting subtasks.
e2wlaA5EdH.evidence: CogViD evaluates 25 MLLMs using 25,505 QA pairs over 2,461 videos and 159.7 hours of footage.
e2wlaA5EdH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the breadth of video capabilities and complementary multiple-choice and open-ended evaluation.
e2wlaA5EdH.main_concern: Different videos across levels and unclear ability dependencies prevent establishing the proposed taxonomy as a controlled progressive cognitive hierarchy.

ya4fVEuIIS.one_liner: Fast-slow prediction and Kalman residual analysis convert multivariate time-series deviations into an anomaly stress statistic.
ya4fVEuIIS.problem: Anomaly detection often prioritizes architecture without modeling how observations depart from stable dynamical regimes.
ya4fVEuIIS.method: TipAD separates fast and slow dynamics in a dual-path predictor and feeds prediction residuals into a Kalman-based criticality estimator. A correspondence between critical-transition variance dynamics and Kalman covariance prediction motivates the design.
ya4fVEuIIS.key_idea: Model fast and slow dynamics separately, then transform prediction residuals into a stress statistic through Kalman estimation.
ya4fVEuIIS.evidence: TSB-AD-M experiments cover 17 datasets and 30 baseline methods using threshold-independent VUS-PR, alongside a theoretical covariance-equation comparison.
ya4fVEuIIS.claimed_gains: TipAD achieves the second-best average rank under VUS-PR on TSB-AD-M, which covers 17 datasets and 30 baseline methods.
ya4fVEuIIS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the dynamical-systems motivation, coherent fast-slow design, and broad standardized benchmark evaluation.
ya4fVEuIIS.main_concern: The experiments do not establish that the detector identifies critical transitions rather than ordinary distributional deviations.

LxC7C6AMxv.one_liner: Failure-driven harness revisions alternate with policy reinforcement learning to improve coding agents.
LxC7C6AMxv.problem: Fixed-harness policy training and fixed-policy harness search fail to accommodate how each component changes the other's capabilities.
LxC7C6AMxv.method: Self-HPO uses the current policy to analyze failures and propose harness revisions, then trains the policy under the selected harness. Hard tasks from training guide the next revision round with the updated policy acting as proposer.
LxC7C6AMxv.key_idea: Alternate self-proposed harness revisions with policy reinforcement learning, feeding hard training failures into the next harness-search round.
LxC7C6AMxv.evidence: Experiments with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B cover SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-Bench Multilingual, and SWE-Bench Pro, including component and cross-evaluation ablations.
LxC7C6AMxv.claimed_gains: Self-HPO improves Qwen3.5-35B-A3B from 61.0% to 69.5% on SWE-Bench Verified, with 54.2% → 59.7% on SWE-Bench Multilingual.
LxC7C6AMxv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that joint harness-policy optimization yields consistent gains over optimizing either component alone, including out-of-domain evaluations.
LxC7C6AMxv.main_concern: Missing budget-matched sequential-optimization baselines leave the specific benefit of repeated alternation unresolved.

eR0E6khF7c.one_liner: Solver feedback guides LLM synthesis of local control barrier functions with certified safety at hybrid-system mode switches.
eR0E6khF7c.problem: Constructing per-mode barriers requires both within-mode safety and safe transitions, making manual synthesis difficult.
eR0E6khF7c.method: An LLM proposes and revises symbolic local barriers using satisfiability-solver feedback. The solver checks each mode's CBF conditions and verifies that switching preserves membership in the next mode's safe set.
eR0E6khF7c.key_idea: Iteratively refine LLM-proposed local barriers using solver checks for both continuous-mode safety and safe switching.
eR0E6khF7c.evidence: Hybrid-system case studies include rover and cruise-control examples, with solver-certified barriers and comparisons against naive prompting without solver feedback.
eR0E6khF7c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate automating barrier synthesis while explicitly checking safety at mode switches.
eR0E6khF7c.main_concern: Comparisons only against naive LLM prompting do not establish added value over simpler non-LLM synthesis methods.

3jE89TlOx5.one_liner: Latent-variable inference combines response reliability and verifier rewards to estimate the prompt baseline used by GRPO.
3jE89TlOx5.problem: Group success counts ignore heterogeneous response reliability and can misestimate prompt solvability and relative advantages.
3jE89TlOx5.method: RLSI links verifier outcomes to latent response-success states through response-specific reliability. An efficient expectation-maximization procedure estimates prompt solvability for advantage construction.
3jE89TlOx5.key_idea: Infer latent response success from verifier outcomes and reliability, then use the estimated prompt solvability to construct advantages.
3jE89TlOx5.evidence: Theoretical analysis and experiments across six mathematical-reasoning benchmarks and two model scales compare GRPO, RW-GRPO, and homogeneous-reliability variants.
3jE89TlOx5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the latent-variable framing useful and the EM update simple, with consistent gains in the evaluated settings.
3jE89TlOx5.main_concern: The meaning and empirical validity of the response-reliability quantity need clearer justification.

4TvpUX36M2.one_liner: An independent verifier executes checks and revises them from feedback while keeping its observation and intervention interfaces fixed.
4TvpUX36M2.problem: Agents can repeat mistaken assumptions when reviewing work through the same history that produced those mistakes.
4TvpUX36M2.method: Sidecar maintains a separate verification context, tests assumptions through executable checks, and returns evidence at decision points. It revises checks using execution feedback while fixing the interfaces that constrain observation and intervention.
4TvpUX36M2.key_idea: Execute assumption checks in a separate context and revise only the checks, preserving fixed verification interfaces.
4TvpUX36M2.evidence: Experiments across multiple backbones and two benchmarks include Terminal-Bench 2.0, continuation controls, and self-reflection comparisons using the agent's own model.
4TvpUX36M2.claimed_gains: On Terminal-Bench 2.0, Sidecar raises task success from 17.3% to 25.0%, a gain of 7.7 percentage points.
4TvpUX36M2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical value of independent executable verification and the gains across agent models.
4TvpUX36M2.main_concern: Controls change context, evidence, or completion handling together, preventing isolation of the benefit of independent verification.

MpUPrJw5aI.one_liner: Paired prompt audits detect when SAM specialization reverses negative-point exclusion despite strong canonical segmentation scores.
MpUPrJw5aI.problem: Canonical positive-prompt validation can miss failures in the interactive prompt behavior retained by specialized SAM models.
MpUPrJw5aI.method: SAMLens gives reference and specialized models identical images and prompts, reporting both absolute responses and changes. It decomposes candidate masks and score-based selection to distinguish negative-point reversal from reduced response range.
MpUPrJw5aI.key_idea: Compare absolute and changed mask responses to identical prompts before and after specialization, then separate mask generation from candidate selection.
MpUPrJw5aI.evidence: Audits examine SAM-family adaptations on dense cell images and histopathology nuclei, with repeated training seeds and candidate-mask decomposition.
MpUPrJw5aI.claimed_gains: Full mask-decoder tuning raises overlap with a negatively marked neighboring object from 0.03 to 0.53, while other main-audit adaptations add at most 0.07.
MpUPrJw5aI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that canonical segmentation accuracy can hide meaningful negative-point failures and that paired auditing exposes them.
MpUPrJw5aI.main_concern: Limited interaction settings leave the relevance and generality of the reversal for realistic iterative annotation uncertain.

CPKW5mrvKb.one_liner: High-performing prompts teach equivalent weaker prompts through on-policy action distillation alternating with reinforcement learning.
CPKW5mrvKb.problem: VLA policies vary sharply across equivalent instructions, leaving weaker prompts with too few successful trajectories for direct RL.
CPKW5mrvKb.method: MOSAR uses a stronger prompt to generate teacher actions at states visited under multiple equivalent student prompts. It weights distillation by task-specific performance gaps and alternates RL with distillation using separate optimizer states.
CPKW5mrvKb.key_idea: Distill strong-prompt actions at student-visited states while alternating policy reinforcement learning with performance-gap-weighted cross-prompt distillation.
CPKW5mrvKb.evidence: Evaluations include RoboLab and REALM, with unseen-prompt tests and ablations of reinforcement learning, weighting, and optimizer design.
CPKW5mrvKb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that prompt sensitivity is practically important and that transferring behavior from stronger prompts is well motivated.
CPKW5mrvKb.main_concern: Inconsistent reported RoboLab unseen-prompt success rates undermine interpretation of the main results and variation analysis.

O0rYIR8t8y.one_liner: Common-support conditions characterize when reported beliefs can arise from Bayesian updating over hidden inference-time experiments.
O0rYIR8t8y.problem: Observable belief reports may reveal little about whether an agent performs Bayesian reasoning or accesses more informative evidence.
O0rYIR8t8y.method: The theory models prompts as hidden experiments followed by Bayesian updating and faithful posterior reporting. It characterizes rationalizable report distributions, compares experiment informativeness through couplings, and analyzes limitations of coarse-report aggregation.
O0rYIR8t8y.key_idea: Test Bayesian rationalizability through a state remaining possible under every report, and compare informativeness through couplings of excluded-answer sets.
O0rYIR8t8y.evidence: Theoretical characterizations cover Bayesian rationalizability, comparative experiment informativeness, and aggregation of coarse belief reports.
O0rYIR8t8y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory a useful warning that Bayesian rationalizability alone offers weak evidence about internal reasoning.
O0rYIR8t8y.main_concern: The permissive assumptions and exact-zero contradictions make the theory difficult to test or apply to actual language-model behavior.

USEjCJWDHx.one_liner: Historical experimental records condition language models to rank and select candidate research interventions.
USEjCJWDHx.problem: Research agents can propose experiments faster than they can execute them, creating a need to predict outcomes under limited budgets.
USEjCJWDHx.method: The study treats language models as Research World Models that predict intervention outcomes using knowledge from real experimental records. It evaluates transfer of this knowledge across environments and its use in multi-round experiment selection.
USEjCJWDHx.key_idea: Condition intervention-outcome predictions on prior experimental records and use those predictions to select promising experiments.
USEjCJWDHx.evidence: Evaluations use over 2,600 records from nine research environments representing more than 171,000 H100 GPU-hours, with ablations across 13 language models.
USEjCJWDHx.claimed_gains: Across five autoregressive pretraining environments, source-only records reduce macro-average best-of-3 regret by 52.2% when selecting three of sixteen candidates.
USEjCJWDHx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the extensive experimental records and evidence that research knowledge improves prediction beyond model choice or reasoning effort alone.
USEjCJWDHx.main_concern: Weak retrieval and regression baselines do not establish whether gains require LLM reasoning rather than access to historical records.

pfBpXB43Yk.one_liner: Unlearning and algorithm-name suppression test whether language models can recover algorithms when direct recall is inhibited.
pfBpXB43Yk.problem: Strong algorithm performance does not establish whether models can reconstruct foundational algorithms independently of memorized knowledge.
pfBpXB43Yk.method: The study suppresses target-algorithm recall through unlearning and separately blocks algorithm names during decoding. Recovery tests vary hints and use a generative verifier to sustain reasoning while checking non-target capabilities.
pfBpXB43Yk.key_idea: Suppress target-algorithm recall, then measure recovery under controlled hints and verifier conditions while monitoring non-target performance.
pfBpXB43Yk.evidence: Experiments cover 20 foundational algorithms and multiple 4B--12B models, with hint-level, name-suppression, and verifier ablations.
pfBpXB43Yk.claimed_gains: Suppressing algorithm-name mentions without unlearning reduces recovery rates by up to 45%.
pfBpXB43Yk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating memorized algorithm recall from reconstruction is an important question and find the systematic tests useful.
pfBpXB43Yk.main_concern: Unlearning may damage algorithm-specific reasoning or expression, so recovery failures do not isolate inability to rediscover algorithms.

Np7vuaOFCc.one_liner: Fusing human GUI trajectories into task-focused state graphs supports offline evaluation with multiple execution paths.
Np7vuaOFCc.problem: Third-party mobile apps often lack system APIs needed by emulator-based benchmarks to determine task success.
Np7vuaOFCc.method: MobiGraph filters task-irrelevant interface elements and merges semantically equivalent states from multiple human trajectories. The resulting graph supports dynamic interactions and alternative task-completion paths without system-level APIs.
Np7vuaOFCc.key_idea: Merge equivalent states and transitions across task trajectories to build an interactive offline graph of alternative GUI execution paths.
Np7vuaOFCc.evidence: The benchmark covers 240 tasks across 20 third-party apps and compares evaluation alignment with human assessments against AndroidWorld.
Np7vuaOFCc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value multi-trajectory fusion as a practical way to evaluate third-party-app tasks with multiple valid paths.
Np7vuaOFCc.main_concern: State merging and uncollected-action handling lack sufficient validation that graph execution preserves real-app behavior.

hTJdgdgTlY.one_liner: Instruction-grounded goal regions replace single-endpoint distance thresholds when evaluating navigation termination.
hTJdgdgTlY.problem: Endpoint proximity can reward instruction-inconsistent stops and reject alternative positions that satisfy the instruction.
hTJdgdgTlY.method: The framework extracts terminal spatial requirements, grounds referenced rooms and objects, and compiles them into navigable goal sets. GSR measures stopping inside a set, while GOSR measures reaching it anywhere along the trajectory.
hTJdgdgTlY.key_idea: Compile grounded terminal-language constraints into goal sets and score whether navigation stops within or passes through those sets.
hTJdgdgTlY.evidence: R2R and RxR annotations cover 65,253 training instructions and 12,845 manually verified validation cases, with re-evaluation of 17 open-source VLN methods.
hTJdgdgTlY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that semantic termination requirements expose a meaningful limitation of endpoint-distance evaluation.
hTJdgdgTlY.main_concern: Goal-set construction still depends on demonstration endpoints and routes, leaving target validity and consistency across valid demonstrations unclear.

gmCR6gwMUA.one_liner: A rational-power gated activation limits amplification to stabilize large-scale language-model pretraining.
gmCR6gwMUA.problem: SwiGLU's amplification can enlarge activation ranges and outliers, causing instability in low-precision language-model training.
gmCR6gwMUA.method: PowLU uses a rational power function to adapt nonlinearity and bound positive gating amplification. The paper analyzes its properties and evaluates scaling behavior and large-model pretraining.
gmCR6gwMUA.key_idea: Replace the gate with a rational-power function whose bounded positive amplification limits extreme activations.
gmCR6gwMUA.evidence: Theoretical analyses, scaling experiments, and Ling-3.0 comparisons at 7.9B and 124B total parameters evaluate PowLU against SwiGLU and SwiGLU-Clip.
gmCR6gwMUA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the amplification-control mechanism reasonable and recognize competitive results at substantial model scale.
gmCR6gwMUA.main_concern: Comparisons with alternative activation and stabilization methods are insufficient to establish PowLU's relative advantage.

OIkjt1pNfe.one_liner: Shared Gaussian denoising coordinates diffusion and Schrödinger-bridge regimes for target-conditioned peptide sequence and structure generation.
OIkjt1pNfe.problem: Peptide co-design must jointly satisfy sequence plausibility, structural validity, and sensitive target-binding geometry.
OIkjt1pNfe.method: PepHyD coordinates regime-specific noise schedules and reverse kernels from diffusion and Schrödinger bridges. A common conditional Gaussian formulation trains both regimes within one shared denoising framework.
OIkjt1pNfe.key_idea: Unify diffusion and bridge transition kernels through conditional Gaussian parameterization and coordinate their schedules during peptide co-generation.
OIkjt1pNfe.evidence: BioDB and LNR experiments compare hybrid dynamics with matched pure-diffusion and pure-bridge controls, stage allocations, and sampling budgets.
OIkjt1pNfe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shared hybrid generative formulation interesting and value comparisons with its individual stochastic regimes.
OIkjt1pNfe.main_concern: The paper does not establish that bridge-specific transport, rather than changed noise schedules, causes the improvements.

MmvzC24jS4.one_liner: Two-sample distribution comparison projecting score and log-density Taylor responses onto reference-defined local normal subspaces
MmvzC24jS4.problem: Standard discrepancy metrics such as MMD and KSD do not distinguish off-manifold normal distribution shifts from benign tangential variations.
MmvzC24jS4.method: Normal Log-Density Taylor Signature (NLTS) estimates the local normal subspace of a reference distribution from the dominant eigenspace of its negative-log-density Hessian and projects scores onto those directions to obtain local Taylor coefficients. It then compares these normal-projected log-density signatures between reference and test samples while suppressing tangential shifts.
MmvzC24jS4.key_idea: Extract local normal directions from the reference negative-log-density Hessian and compare projected first- and second-order log-density Taylor responses across two sample sets.
MmvzC24jS4.evidence: Supported by theoretical propositions under a small-noise manifold model and experiments on synthetic manifold shifts, CIFAR-10-C with learned score models, and single-cell perturbation datasets.
MmvzC24jS4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find distinguishing normal from tangential distributional shifts well motivated and appreciate the theoretical connection between score and Hessian geometry and local normal subspaces.
MmvzC24jS4.main_concern: The small-noise and symmetric-Hessian assumptions diverge from the asymmetric approximation used in practice, and the paper omits runtime overhead measurements and simpler score-norm baselines.

jVoRUnqQo3.one_liner: Wraps a frozen streaming 3D foundation model in causal tracking and asynchronous bidirectional re-observation over a revisable SLAM state
jVoRUnqQo3.problem: Streaming 3D foundation models emit fixed online pose and geometry predictions that cannot be revised upon loop closure to correct accumulated drift.
jVoRUnqQo3.method: Map2SLAM keeps LingBot-Map frozen, trains a lightweight loop-retrieval head on cached single-pass image encoder features, and treats model outputs as observations of an external persistent SLAM state. A causal streaming front-end tracks incoming frames and selects keyframes, while an asynchronous back-end re-runs joint bidirectional inference on past frames for verified loop-closure trajectory updates and post-sequence segment geometry refinement.
jVoRUnqQo3.key_idea: Reuse single-pass image features from a frozen streaming 3D model across causal front-end tracking, lightweight loop retrieval, and asynchronous bidirectional back-end re-observation on a revisable state.
jVoRUnqQo3.evidence: Evaluated on long-sequence visual SLAM benchmarks KITTI, VBR, and Oxford Spires using a frozen LingBot-Map backbone with ablations on loop verification and segment alignment.
jVoRUnqQo3.claimed_gains: Reduces mean ATE by over 40% compared with the best uncalibrated baselines across KITTI, VBR, and Oxford Spires.
jVoRUnqQo3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling frozen streaming 3D predictions into causal front-end tracking and bidirectional back-end state updates with single-pass feature reuse yields strong trajectory accuracy.
jVoRUnqQo3.main_concern: Dense 3D reconstruction quality is never quantitatively evaluated despite being emphasized, and runtime claims conflate dual-GPU front-end tracking with separate post-sequence refinement without fair baseline timing comparisons.

XCUW28sDnJ.one_liner: Three-stage vision-language training combining table-encoder adaptation, cell-grounded SFT, and decomposed-reward RL for reasoning over table images
XCUW28sDnJ.problem: Textual table serialization corrupts cell structure and discards visual cues, while raw table images bottleneck vision-language models on accurate cell perception and grounded multi-step reasoning.
XCUW28sDnJ.method: MERIT first adapts the visual encoder to table images using reconstruction, cell localization, and color-conditioned supervision, optionally pairing images with serialized tables. It then runs supervised fine-tuning on verified cell-evidence trajectories followed by GRPO reinforcement learning with separate rewards for evidence selection, calculation, final answer, and format.
XCUW28sDnJ.key_idea: Adapt the vision encoder via structure- and color-aware table tasks, then train explicit cell-coordinate evidence selection and reasoning with verified SFT trajectories and decomposed RL rewards.
XCUW28sDnJ.evidence: Evaluated on Qwen3-VL-8B across five table question answering and fact verification benchmarks with stage, modality, and reward ablations.
XCUW28sDnJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the three-stage pipeline coherent and practical for verifiable, cell-grounded reasoning over table images, showing consistent gains over its Qwen3-VL-8B backbone.
XCUW28sDnJ.main_concern: Ablations indicate that supervised fine-tuning drives most of the gain while encoder adaptation and decomposed RL rewards add modest improvements, and direct comparisons with closely related methods like Table-R1 are missing.

J1iUWRUJAK.one_liner: Assigns Shapley action credit for joint LLM retrieval sets by replaying action subsets against a fixed environment snapshot
J1iUWRUJAK.problem: Scalar rewards returned for jointly generated sets of retrieval actions cannot identify coalition-dependent credit for individual actions within the set.
J1iUWRUJAK.method: CASI executes joint generation and retrieval once, freezes replayable environment snapshot components, and evaluates counterfactual subsets of retrieval actions under shared conditions. It aggregates subset marginals via Shapley values and injects them into policy optimization through bounded zero-sum advantage shaping.
J1iUWRUJAK.key_idea: Evaluate counterfactual subsets of jointly generated retrieval actions against a frozen retrieval snapshot and aggregate marginal values into bounded zero-sum Shapley advantage shaping.
J1iUWRUJAK.evidence: Supported by an identifiability proposition for set sizes at least four, exhaustive five-action auction replay over 1,200 sponsored-search requests, evaluator sensitivity audits, and five independent policy training runs.
J1iUWRUJAK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the formal distinction between set-level reward broadcasting and coalition-dependent credit assignment via snapshot-grounded counterfactual subset replay.
J1iUWRUJAK.main_concern: Crucial experimental details (model identity, RL hyperparameters, and the cached-filter evaluator) are omitted, policy training lacks a Banzhaf baseline, and credit-alignment gains vanish under an alternative evaluator backend.
