CQ1RLoDU9X.main_concern: Reviewers unanimously emphasize the complete lack of human validation of the LLM-extracted decisions and outcome labels, as well as potential reward hacking when optimizing and evaluating with the same decision-similarity metric.

rMbRtcF0bY.one_liner: Combines cyclic oblique midpoint splits with regularized local polynomial leaf estimators to achieve log-free minimax multiclass rates.
rMbRtcF0bY.problem: Oblique decision trees capture non-axis-aligned boundaries but lacked sharp minimax multiclass excess-risk guarantees over arbitrary finite Hölder smoothness without extra logarithmic factors.
rMbRtcF0bY.method: Cyclic Oblique Forests apply purely randomized midpoint cuts cycling through a nondegenerate basis of oblique directions and fit regularized local polynomial estimators in each leaf, with depth and polynomial degree matched to smoothness.
rMbRtcF0bY.key_idea: Cycle midpoint splits through a basis of oblique directions and fit regularized local polynomials in irregular leaves to attain log-free minimax multiclass rates.
rMbRtcF0bY.evidence: Theoretical proofs establish minimax upper and lower bounds over Hölder classes (and sharper bounds under a margin condition), supplemented by experiments on UCI datasets.
rMbRtcF0bY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the sound theoretical extension of oblique-forest minimax rates to arbitrary finite smoothness, multiclass classification, and irregular boundary leaves without extra log factors.
rMbRtcF0bY.main_concern: Reviewers point out restrictive theoretical assumptions (uniform feature distribution, nondegenerate directions), unclear incremental novelty over balanced polynomial-leaf forests, limited experiments, and dense writing.

JDRRGFe567.one_liner: Uses a closed-loop LLM generate-calibrate-refine pipeline with error diagnostics to synthesize intervention-aware time-series models.
JDRRGFe567.problem: Real-world time series experience sparse, heterogeneous external interventions that fixed mechanistic models handle rigidly and deep learning models fail to generalize under limited data.
JDRRGFe567.method: TimeCoder prompts an LLM to propose executable intervention-aware model structures from domain knowledge and statistical descriptors, calibrates their parameters on data, and feeds structured residual diagnostics back to iteratively refine model structure.
JDRRGFe567.key_idea: Iteratively synthesize, parameter-calibrate, and structurally refine executable intervention-aware time-series models using LLM reasoning guided by temporal error diagnostics.
JDRRGFe567.evidence: Evaluations span four benchmarks across healthcare, hydrology, and epidemics comparing forecasting, classification, sparse-intervention generalization, and sample efficiency against deep learning and LLM baselines.
JDRRGFe567.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize intervention-aware time-series modeling as a relevant problem and note substantial baseline comparisons with strong reported forecasting results across four datasets.
JDRRGFe567.main_concern: Reviewers raise serious discrepancies in experimental tables (mismatched Qwen3-32B vs. Qwen3-Coder-Flash results and trial counts), limited novelty over prior LLM refinement loops, and missing ablations isolating structural refinement.

w7nMNmGmgs.one_liner: Constructs explicit M-by-N matrix games forcing the Double Oracle algorithm to take the maximum M+N-2 iterations.
w7nMNmGmgs.problem: Prior worst-case lower bounds for Double Oracle did not provide a general explicit construction attaining the exact trivial M+N-2 upper bound across all rectangular matrix sizes regardless of tie-breaking.
w7nMNmGmgs.method: The authors give an explicit M-by-N payoff matrix construction that forces Double Oracle from a singleton start to run for M+N-2 iterations under every equilibrium and best-response selection rule, extend it to sufficiently accurate inexact oracles and fixed stopping tolerances, and formalize the proofs in Lean.
w7nMNmGmgs.key_idea: Construct an explicit M-by-N payoff matrix whose subgame equilibria force strategies to enter one by one for M+N-2 iterations regardless of tie-breaking.
w7nMNmGmgs.evidence: Formal mathematical proofs verified in Lean establish the exact M+N-2 bound, oracle-error robustness, and fixed-tolerance behavior.
w7nMNmGmgs.claimed_gains: For all integers M, N >= 2, the explicit M-by-N matrix forces Double Oracle to run for exactly M + N - 2 iterations, matching the trivial worst-case upper bound.
w7nMNmGmgs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the explicit rectangular construction cleanly attains the exact M+N-2 bound independently of selection rules and quantifies oracle-error robustness.
w7nMNmGmgs.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical and asymptotic significance over Zhang & Sandholm (2024), noting the construction relies on exact termination at a pure equilibrium and requires exponentially accurate oracles in rectangular games.

7ktmLdjqgQ.one_liner: Penalizes candidate token logits at sampling time only when they extend the current suffix into an earlier verbatim span.
7ktmLdjqgQ.problem: Standard repetition penalties and n-gram blocking act on token recurrence rather than sequential loops, degrading formatting and fluency at strengths needed to stop verbatim looping.
7ktmLdjqgQ.method: Don't Repeat Yourself (DRY) adjusts sampling logits by penalizing a candidate token only if appending it extends the current suffix into an exact match of an earlier context span, using sequence-breaker tokens to protect formatting and chat templates.
7ktmLdjqgQ.key_idea: Apply a sampling-time logit penalty proportional to matched suffix-extension length only when a token continues an earlier verbatim span, reset by sequence-breaker tokens.
7ktmLdjqgQ.evidence: Experiments span models from 1.5B to 120B parameters across nine prompt families, a 600-pair human study, a placebo control, and AWQ-quantized 70B/120B evaluations on MT-Bench, MMLU, and GSM8K.
7ktmLdjqgQ.claimed_gains: DRY reduces the suffix-extension rate by 47% while improving lexical diversity, and cuts loop rates roughly in half on AWQ-quantized 70B and 120B models while preserving MT-Bench, MMLU, and GSM8K.
7ktmLdjqgQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge that DRY is a simple, easy-to-implement decoding penalty with low overhead and broad evaluation across multiple LLMs.
7ktmLdjqgQ.main_concern: Reviewers question its novelty over existing n-gram and suffix-based decoding penalties, point out missing core ablations (hard vs. soft, breaker sensitivity, scaling compute), and note overstated Pareto-frontier and human-study claims.

mRKeWKsRwp.one_liner: Measures the minimum shared linear rank needed to preserve LLM next-token distributions across prefixes and tests adaptive low-rank readouts.
mRKeWKsRwp.problem: Local low-dimensional sensitivity at single prefixes does not establish how much residual-stream width is needed to preserve next-token predictions across diverse contexts.
mRKeWKsRwp.method: The authors define context requirement dimension as the smallest rank of a shared linear map preserving next-token distributions within a fixed KL tolerance, and evaluate a two-stage adaptive readout that uses a low-rank prediction to select candidate tokens before refining probabilities from the full state.
mRKeWKsRwp.key_idea: Measure shared-map rank under a fixed next-token KL tolerance across prefixes and refine low-rank shortlisted tokens with the original state.
mRKeWKsRwp.evidence: Evaluated across 21 language models from nine model families over corpus prefixes and layers.
mRKeWKsRwp.claimed_gains: Across 21 models from nine families, fitted shared linear maps require 58–80% of final-state width to preserve next-token distributions across prefixes.
mRKeWKsRwp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the study is clearly written, tests a broad set of 21 models, and investigates a timely question about representation dimensionality.
mRKeWKsRwp.main_concern: Reviewers question the novelty and significance of the main finding—that different prefixes use different subspaces and thus require a wide shared basis—viewing it as expected from prior work.

fa1DKS5Anj.one_liner: Performs source-free machine unlearning by aggregating curvature-scaled forget-set gradient ascent steps estimated from two gradients per saved checkpoint.
fa1DKS5Anj.problem: Influence-function unlearning requires inverse Hessians over retained training data, which is often unavailable when deletion requests arrive.
fa1DKS5Anj.method: Caffeine estimates directional curvature along the forget-set gradient using two first-order forget-set gradient evaluations a small step apart at each saved training checkpoint, then aggregates the curvature-scaled gradient ascent steps into a single full-model update without retained data.
fa1DKS5Anj.key_idea: Estimate directional curvature from two nearby forget-set gradients at each saved training checkpoint and aggregate curvature-scaled ascent steps without retained data or Hessians.
fa1DKS5Anj.evidence: Evaluated on class and random-subset deletion across five image and text classification datasets.
fa1DKS5Anj.claimed_gains: Caffeine runs up to 25.3x faster than retraining on image tasks while being the only tested approximate method that both forgets and preserves accuracy without retained data.
fa1DKS5Anj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that Caffeine addresses a practical retain-data-free setting with a simple Hessian-free directional curvature estimator.
fa1DKS5Anj.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the reliance on saved training checkpoints, small-scale classification setups, missing objective details, and evaluation that does not distinguish true unlearning from output suppression.

okMBm9is6M.one_liner: Trains code agents with RL by verifying pre-action outcome beliefs against execution to compute step-level advantages and guide inference selection.
okMBm9is6M.problem: Code agents typically act reactively under sparse terminal rewards without anticipating action consequences or attributing failures to specific steps.
okMBm9is6M.method: ANTE requires the agent to state a pre-action belief verified by real execution, uses Belief-Anchored Policy Optimization (BAPO) to turn verified predictions into per-step advantages and trust-or-abstain credit, and applies ANTE-TTO to select among candidate actions at inference without an external scorer.
okMBm9is6M.key_idea: Verify pre-action execution beliefs online to construct per-step belief-anchored RL advantages and self-scored candidate action selection.
okMBm9is6M.evidence: Evaluated across three model scales (including Qwen3-32B), two harnesses, controlled Reactive/Retrospective baselines, and out-of-domain coding datasets.
okMBm9is6M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that verifying structured pre-action predictions via execution is a concrete, sensible mechanism evaluated across multiple datasets and controlled baselines.
okMBm9is6M.main_concern: Reviewers argue that claims of anticipating edit effects overstate the two-field discrete belief format, that BAPO and TTO gains are not cleanly isolated from budget or reward confounds, and that positioning versus related work is unclear.

td1JeNuV3X.one_liner: Reweights supervised fine-tuning loss to equalize budget across semantic token groups so short knowledge payloads are not drowned out by scaffolds.
td1JeNuV3X.problem: Uniform token-level SFT allocates loss budget by token count rather than knowledge importance, letting long scaffold or citation spans dominate short factual answers.
td1JeNuV3X.method: Group-Balanced SFT (GB-SFT) partitions target tokens into semantic role groups and equalizes loss weight across groups using one tunable dial and one structural switch unifying standard SFT, class-level, and span-level balancing.
td1JeNuV3X.key_idea: Reweight SFT token losses to balance total loss budget across semantic role groups rather than uniform token counts.
td1JeNuV3X.evidence: Evaluated across model families on benchmarks in law, medicine, code, and mathematics, plus two newly released contamination-controlled knowledge-injection benchmarks and partition ablations.
td1JeNuV3X.claimed_gains: On a legal QA benchmark, citations absorb 81% of uniform SFT loss versus 5% for answers; GB-SFT matches payload-only masking on knowledge injection while retaining 0.98 vs. 0.38 citation recall.
td1JeNuV3X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the loss-budget skew observation is clear and grounded, and that the partition ablation study honestly evaluates role-grouping sensitivity.
td1JeNuV3X.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains stem primarily from oracle semantic grouping rather than the objective itself (as SFT-GO with the same grouping matches or beats GB-SFT), that parameter beta is redundant, and that automatic grouping degrades on non-distinctive spans.

XetdVGr0yh.one_liner: Stabilizes group-relative RL for active reasoning agents via behavioral retention on mastered prompts and difficulty-aware batch sampling.
XetdVGr0yh.problem: Group-relative RL with binary outcome rewards collapses because mastered prompts produce zero within-group variance, silently exiting gradient updates and suffering forgetting.
XetdVGr0yh.method: AgentFrontier combines Frontier Retention, which applies lightweight behavioral regularization on mastered prompts to preserve solved trajectories, with Frontier Stabilization, which constructs difficulty-aware training batches across mastered, frontier, and unsolved prompts.
XetdVGr0yh.key_idea: Anchor mastered prompts with behavioral regularization and balance mastered, frontier, and unsolved prompts in each batch to prevent group-relative RL collapse.
XetdVGr0yh.evidence: Evaluated on active reasoning RL benchmarks against KL regularization, replay, and curriculum baselines, with diagnostic tracking and component ablations.
XetdVGr0yh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that diagnosing group-relative RL collapse via vanishing within-group reward variance on mastered prompts is clear and the proposed retention-plus-sampling fix is simple and effective.
XetdVGr0yh.main_concern: Reviewers find that the theoretical propositions fail to prove forgetting or directional likelihood drift, and question both the batch-sampling behavior late in training and the lack of multi-seed stability analysis.

7616Ld0g9b.one_liner: Generates compositional multi-part 3D geometry and PBR materials from one image using reusable set-indexed sparse latent slots.
7616Ld0g9b.problem: Existing compositional 3D generators either cap part counts or scale inference cost with part count, while monolithic material generators lack part awareness.
7616Ld0g9b.method: PartSynth introduces a Sparse Part Structure (SPS) with reusable set-indexed latent slots on a sparse 3D scaffold that jointly predict slot activity and features; connected components of decoded volumes define arbitrary part counts and condition adapted monolithic geometry and PBR stages.
7616Ld0g9b.key_idea: Represent arbitrary multi-part 3D structure with reusable set-indexed sparse latent slots whose decoded connected components guide part-aware geometry and PBR generation.
7616Ld0g9b.evidence: Evaluated on image-conditioned compositional 3D geometry and fixed-geometry PBR synthesis against TRELLIS.2 and part-generation baselines.
7616Ld0g9b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the sparse set-indexed slot representation is a clean, scalable way to handle flexible part counts with strong part-level geometry and PBR metrics.
7616Ld0g9b.main_concern: Reviewers point out coarse individual part resolution from omitting the high-resolution refinement stage, missing end-to-end runtime and part-structure correctness evaluations, and confounded ablations without matched-training controls.

TmSfRtYLK5.one_liner: Aggregates multi-agent LLM answers by style-normalizing one trace per answer and injecting minority bias to measure decision stability.
TmSfRtYLK5.problem: Multi-agent LLM aggregation is vulnerable to majority pressure and response-style biases that obscure reasoning quality when agents disagree.
TmSfRtYLK5.method: The framework applies bias control by presenting one style-normalized reasoning trace per distinct candidate answer for initial selection, then applies bias injection by placing each aggregator's chosen answer in the minority to elicit decision instability as a reliability signal without validation data.
TmSfRtYLK5.key_idea: Normalize reasoning style across distinct answers for initial selection, then inject adverse majority frequency to score decision reliability by flip persistence.
TmSfRtYLK5.evidence: Evaluated across three mathematical reasoning benchmarks, four heterogeneous LLM combinations, budget-matched controls, and multi-agent debate and Mixture-of-Agents.
TmSfRtYLK5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting adverse frequency bias as a test-time reliability stress test without validation data or model-strength priors is an intuitive idea.
TmSfRtYLK5.main_concern: Reviewers question whether gains stem from plain LLM selection over deduplicated answers rather than style normalization or bias injection, noting modest ablation margins, heuristic aggregation rules, and imperfect stability-correctness correlation.

2S3lTh23Lz.one_liner: Converts ANNs with arbitrary continuous nonnegative activations to SNNs by matching them to stationary spike fluxes of finite-state Markov neurons.
2S3lTh23Lz.problem: Most ANN-to-SNN conversion methods assume ReLU activations and rely on fixed activation-to-spiking-response mappings.
2S3lTh23Lz.method: The authors formulate spiking neurons as finite-state continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs) with affine input-dependent transition rates, prove uniform approximation of continuous nonnegative activations on compact intervals, and fit two- and three-state models to ReLU, sigmoid, softplus, and clipped ReLU.
2S3lTh23Lz.key_idea: Approximate arbitrary continuous nonnegative ANN activations using the stationary firing rate of finite-state continuous-time Markov chain neurons.
2S3lTh23Lz.evidence: Supported by a constructive uniform approximation theorem and conversion experiments on MNIST MLPs and VGG-11 on MNIST and CIFAR-10.
2S3lTh23Lz.claimed_gains: Within the CTMC family, clipping reduces SynOps by 27% on VGG-11/MNIST at the reported accuracy-gap criterion, though the trend reverses on VGG-11/CIFAR-10.
2S3lTh23Lz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using CTMC stationary spike flux for activation-flexible conversion is intuitive and backed by a clean uniform approximation theorem.
2S3lTh23Lz.main_concern: Reviewers note a disconnect between large-chain theory and low-state experimental models, missing optimization and transition-rate specifications, lack of recent ANN-to-SNN baselines, and higher SynOps than a standard baseline.

1HnmkMF5DR.one_liner: Aligns independently injected facts across hops by reusing a shared descriptor pool on bridge entities during knowledge-injection training.
1HnmkMF5DR.problem: Rewriting methods for parametric knowledge injection teach atomic facts well but leave latent two-hop composition accuracy low because bridge entities are never aligned across hops.
1HnmkMF5DR.method: Bridge Anchoring by Common Enrichment (BRACE) enriches both hops of injected facts using the same shared descriptor pool for the bridge entity so both atomic training examples present the bridge in a common form.
1HnmkMF5DR.key_idea: Attach a shared descriptor pool to the bridge entity across independently trained atomic hops to align its representation for single-pass multi-hop composition.
1HnmkMF5DR.evidence: Evaluated on a synthetic two-hop updated-facts benchmark across four pretrained LLMs (1.7B–14B, two families) and five domains with descriptor and budget controls.
1HnmkMF5DR.claimed_gains: BRACE improves composed accuracy over the strongest baseline in all 20 model-domain cells by 0.1% to 31% relative, and raises composition rate up to 83 (versus prior methods below 40 at 1.7B).
1HnmkMF5DR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating atomic acquisition from latent composition exposes a clear blind spot and that BRACE's text-level enrichment consistently improves composed accuracy across settings.
1HnmkMF5DR.main_concern: Reviewers point out that constructing per-chain descriptor pools requires knowing the two-hop chains in advance, contradicting the unenumerable-chains motivation, and note disjoint synthetic chains and lexical-bridge confounds.

jmMCBwohWI.one_liner: Modulates grouped low-rank feature residuals with an input-dependent multi-scale depth-wise spatial gate for backbone-agnostic dense vision PEFT.
jmMCBwohWI.problem: Standard channel-wise low-rank adapters are spatially uniform and suboptimal for dense vision prediction tasks under small parameter budgets.
jmMCBwohWI.method: MSLoRA operates on intermediate feature maps across convolutional, hierarchical, hybrid, and plain ViT backbones by gating a grouped low-rank projection with an input-dependent multi-scale depth-wise convolutional branch.
jmMCBwohWI.key_idea: Allocate part of a small feature-space PEFT budget to a multi-scale depth-wise spatial gate modulating a grouped low-rank residual.
jmMCBwohWI.evidence: Evaluated on COCO detection/segmentation (Cascade Mask R-CNN with ResNet-50 and Swin-B) and classification across multiple vision backbone families.
jmMCBwohWI.claimed_gains: On COCO with Cascade Mask R-CNN, MSLoRA reaches 42.9 box AP and 38.4 mask AP on ResNet-50 using 0.7M trainable parameters (2.7% of the backbone).
jmMCBwohWI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing dense-vision PEFT around spatial budget allocation with a unified feature-space adapter is well motivated and transparently reports costs and limitations.
jmMCBwohWI.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over prior depth-wise convolutional adapters, small single-run gains over additive or gate-only controls, dimensional inconsistencies in equations, and slower non-mergeable inference.

DFhuekT37f.one_liner: Replaces the lower-level minimizer in nonconvex bilevel optimization with a Gibbs distribution sampled via SGLD using covariance hypergradients.
DFhuekT37f.problem: Classical optimizer-centered bilevel optimization is unstable and requires arbitrary selection rules when the lower-level objective is nonconvex or multimodal.
DFhuekT37f.method: Value-Centric Hypergradient Descent (VCHD) models the follower as a Gibbs distribution solving an entropy-regularized lower-level problem, samples it with mini-batch SGLD, and estimates outer hypergradients via a Hessian-free sample covariance identity.
DFhuekT37f.key_idea: Formulate the lower-level follower as an entropy-regularized Gibbs distribution sampled with SGLD and differentiate via a Hessian-free covariance hypergradient.
DFhuekT37f.evidence: Supported by nonasymptotic convergence analysis without lower-level convexity and experiments on quadratic, double-well, and data-cleaning benchmarks.
DFhuekT37f.claimed_gains: Establishes nonasymptotic convergence to an epsilon-stationary point with O(epsilon^-3) sample complexity without assuming lower-level convexity.
DFhuekT37f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the Hessian-free covariance hypergradient and nonconvex O(epsilon^-3) convergence analysis provide a clean, practical alternative to implicit or unrolled differentiation.
DFhuekT37f.main_concern: Reviewers note that the Gibbs formulation was proposed in prior work, that theoretical assumptions (tail strong convexity, global smoothness, bounded outer loss) are violated in experiments, and that experiments do not isolate the estimator from SGLD noise regularization or exact forward-mode baselines.

TgZxorO7nB.one_liner: Jointly updates a contextual-bandit router and continually distills a local student model whenever an API teacher is queried online.
TgZxorO7nB.problem: Static LLM cascades cannot adapt to non-stationary query streams or improve local student autonomy while balancing serving quality and privacy.
TgZxorO7nB.method: The system frames routing between a local student and a large teacher as a contextual bandit updated from student-teacher agreement only when the teacher is called, while continually distilling teacher responses into the student without requiring teacher logits or ground-truth labels.
TgZxorO7nB.key_idea: Jointly adapt a contextual-bandit router from call-only agreement feedback and continually distill queried teacher responses into the local student.
TgZxorO7nB.evidence: Evaluated on a suite of non-stationary streaming task-shift testbeds against MLP and confidence-based routers at matched agreement levels.
TgZxorO7nB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the online evolving-cascade formulation and non-stationary streaming testbed capture a genuine, well-framed problem under limited feedback.
TgZxorO7nB.main_concern: Reviewers note that the router lacks a forgetting or re-exploration mechanism to detect student degradation after non-calls, and that reported gains rely on single swept runs without error bars and small margins over confidence routing.

28zRRzqKQA.one_liner: Allocates synthetic data-free quantization calibration prompts and images according to measured capability-module quantization sensitivity in LVLMs.
28zRRzqKQA.problem: Data-free quantization methods for vision-language models generate generic calibration samples that miss heterogeneous, capability- and module-specific quantization errors.
28zRRzqKQA.method: PromptQ uses Sensitivity-Driven Prompt Construction (SDPC) to estimate capability-module vulnerability from behavioral degradation and representation discrepancies under controlled quantization, then allocates diverse, module-aware prompts and synthesizes quantization-sensitive calibration images.
28zRRzqKQA.key_idea: Estimate capability-module quantization sensitivity via controlled perturbation and allocate synthetic calibration prompts and images toward the most vulnerable capabilities.
28zRRzqKQA.evidence: Evaluated across six model-setting combinations (including Qwen2.5-VL-3B at 4w8a and 5w5a), two architectures, small calibration budgets, and ablations.
28zRRzqKQA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that allocating data-free calibration samples by capability-module sensitivity is well motivated and yields consistent gains across evaluated synthetic baselines.
28zRRzqKQA.main_concern: Reviewers point out underspecified algorithmic details limiting reproducibility, small margins over generic prompting relative to high sample-generation time without statistical testing, and overclaimed theoretical bounds.

58ub6s86hL.one_liner: Estimates expected information gain for Bayesian experimental design as a diffusion-time squared likelihood-guidance steering cost using pretrained priors.
58ub6s86hL.problem: Estimating expected information gain for Bayesian optimal experimental design is computationally intractable under complex high-dimensional priors.
58ub6s86hL.method: The authors combine the MINDE score-KL identity with a diffusion posterior sampling (DPS) plug-in approximation to estimate expected information gain as an integral of squared likelihood guidance, reusing a single pretrained diffusion prior for both design scoring and posterior inference.
58ub6s86hL.key_idea: Approximate expected information gain via a diffusion-time integral of squared DPS likelihood guidance using a pretrained diffusion prior without training a design policy.
58ub6s86hL.evidence: Supported by approximation-error analysis and experiments on source localization, constant elasticity of substitution, and 64x64 Darcy flow parameter estimation.
58ub6s86hL.claimed_gains: On 64x64 Darcy source-position design, the method reduces mean relative L2 error of the posterior-mean log-permeability field by 25.2% and 2.8% after the first and second measurements versus ALINE.
58ub6s86hL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusing a pretrained diffusion prior via MINDE and likelihood guidance to score designs without retraining a policy is an interesting, practical idea.
58ub6s86hL.main_concern: Reviewers worry that DPS point-estimate approximations can systematically bias design rankings, and note weak low-dimensional baseline results, lack of runtime complexity analysis, and scalability limits of explicit likelihoods and sampled candidate pools.

aDaaN3GdM5.one_liner: Uses a causal-cut framework to derive joint expressivity bounds linking prompt budget, retained memory geometry, and frozen model limits.
aDaaN3GdM5.problem: Existing analyses rarely capture how prompt budget, retained state capacity, and frozen model parameters jointly constrain which outputs a language model can generate.
aDaaN3GdM5.method: The authors place a causal cut between prompt processing and generation to derive joint accessibility bounds governed by the tightest of prompt, memory, and model constraints, sharpening memory bounds via contraction and reachable-state geometry for Gated Linear Attention (GLA).
aDaaN3GdM5.key_idea: Impose a causal cut between prompt encoding and generation to bound accessible outputs jointly by prompt budget, reachable memory-state geometry, and fixed model constraints.
aDaaN3GdM5.evidence: Supported by theoretical expressivity bounds and controlled prompt-optimization experiments on two frozen GLA checkpoints, sliding-window controls, and Mamba.
aDaaN3GdM5.claimed_gains: On GLA-1.3B, increasing retained memory payload from 12 to 24 to 36 MiB raises the evaluated 50% output frontier from 8192 to 10240 to 12288 tokens.
aDaaN3GdM5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the causal-cut formulation provides a coherent unified theoretical framework for analyzing how prompt, memory, and model limits interact.
aDaaN3GdM5.main_concern: Reviewers note a disconnect between robust theoretical bounds and synthetic exact-memorization prompt-optimization experiments that neither verify theoretical assumptions nor test realistic downstream tasks.

zU8Dro0Won.one_liner: NonTextual Target Attack (NTA) decomposes jailbreak optimization into differentiable response-unsafety and adversarial-prompt sub-objectives without fixed target strings.
zU8Dro0Won.problem: Gradient-based jailbreaks targeting fixed affirmative strings restrict the adversarial search space and require many optimization iterations.
zU8Dro0Won.method: NTA replaces fixed textual targets with a non-textual objective maximizing output unsafety probability, decomposed into two differentiable unconstrained losses that alternate optimizing a dynamic response representation and an adversarial suffix near the original prompt with cross-vocabulary projection.
zU8Dro0Won.key_idea: Alternates differentiable optimization of an unconstrained unsafe response representation and an adversarial prompt suffix instead of matching fixed target strings.
zU8Dro0Won.evidence: Theoretical decomposition analysis and evaluations across multiple LLMs, two jailbreak benchmarks, alternative scorers, independent judges, black-box transfer, and defenses.
zU8Dro0Won.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that dynamically optimizing response representations rather than fixed target strings is well-motivated and clearly presented.
zU8Dro0Won.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing key non-textual and dynamic-target baselines (DTA, reward/entropy-based attacks, I-GCG), undermining the first-of-its-kind claim, and note judge-coupling issues where GPTFuzzer scores far exceed independent LLM judges.
